docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Internet Freedom Solution All you need for an unrestricted internet Hiddify – on your device

Hiddify is an easy-to-use VPN application available for iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. Connect seamlessly to your HiddifyManager or any other VPN panel. Download it on mobile or desktop and enjoy unrestricted internet access.

HiddifyManager - to manage proxies and users

HiddifyManager simplifies setting up your own VPN server, allowing you to manage it even from your mobile device. Easily share proxies with family, friends, groups, or even hundreds of users.

Connect to the unrestricted internet easier than ever.
  • Easy to Use
  • Ad-Free, Secure and Open-Source
  • Offers advanced features such as support for IPv6, multiple subscription link types and more
  • Supports a wide range of proxy protocols including Hysteria2, TUIC, SSH, Reality, VMess, VLESS, Trojan and WireGuard, AmneziaWG, Naive, Psiphon, WebSocket, Quic, gRPC, http-split, httpupgrade, ECH, and Sing-box, V2ray, Clash and Xray configs, and many more
Read more about the Hiddify and see the source codes Free Testing Proxy - WARP Config Set up your own personal and dedicated VPN server.
  • Effortless Installation
  • One of the best VPN Servers for Iran, China, Russia, Brazil and the whole world
  • Multi-Core, Multi-Domain and Unified User Management
  • Supports a wide range of proxy protocols including Hysteria2, TUIC, Reality, VMess, VLESS, Trojan and Shadowsocks, WireGuard, AnyTLS, Snell, Naive, Mieru, xHTTP, httpupgrade, gRPC, WebSocket, ECH, DNS tunnels, Telegram proxy, with Xray and sing-box (hiddify-core) cores, and many more
Read more about the HiddifyManager and see the source code Install on server

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
How can I make sure that Hiddify is safe?

To make sure Hiddify is secure, you can take the following steps:

  1. Review the Source Code 🛠️ Since Hiddify is open-source, you can examine the code directly on GitHub for any security issues or concerns🔍. Reviewing the code yourself or consulting with a developer you trust is a good practice✅.

  2. Check Community Feedback and Contributions 🌐 The Hiddify GitHub page and repositories often have contributions, issue reports, and discussions from other developers and users👥. By reading these discussions, you can gain insights into the software’s security and any potential vulnerabilities that may have been addressed or raised by the community🛡️.

  3. Use the Latest Version 🔄 Ensure you’re using the latest version of Hiddify, as it may include security patches and improvements🔒. You can check the release notes on GitHub to see updates related to security📈.

  4. Follow Standard Security Practices 🔐 Using Hiddify in a secure environment involves applying good security practices, such as:

  5. Restricting access 🚫
  6. Regularly monitoring activity 📊

  7. Keeping both your operating system and Hiddify software up-to-date 🆙

  8. Transparency of Configuration 🌟 Hiddify Manager enables users to configure their own servers, providing complete control over proxy settings and data🔄. This transparency ensures that users can maintain secure configurations and modify them as needed🔄. Similarly, the Hiddify app offers users and developers the flexibility to customize and adjust settings, including proxy configurations and connection management, to meet their specific needs📶. Being open-source, the app allows visibility of any modifications or improvements, ensuring that users retain full control over their app experience while safeguarding security and privacy at every stage🔐.

By following these steps, you can be more confident in Hiddify’s security as a privacy and anti-censorship tool🛡️✨.

Which devices does Hiddify support?

Hiddify is designed to work across a range of devices and operating systems, covering both server-side and client-side needs🌐:

  1. Server-Side Compatibility (Hiddify Manager) 🖥️ Hiddify includes a server-side application, called Hiddify Manager, which installs on an Ubuntu server (preferably Ubuntu 26.04 or 24.04). Hiddify Manager can be quickly set up with Cloud-init🚀, making it easy to deploy on popular cloud providers and datacenters🌩️. This server-side application manages configurations and connections for clients, offering a powerful backend for those seeking secure and stable internet access🔐.

  2. Client-Side Compatibility (Hiddify app) 📱 The Hiddify client-side application, simply called Hiddify, is versatile and supports all major operating systems, including:

  3. iOS 📲
  4. Android 🤖
  5. Windows 🪟
  6. Linux 🐧
  7. macOS 🍏

The development team is actively expanding compatibility to support additional device types, such as routers 📡 and 32-bit devices 🧩, to make Hiddify accessible to an even wider audience🔄.

With this structure, Hiddify provides a comprehensive solution for bypassing internet censorship and filtering, allowing users to set up servers independently and connect across multiple devices🔗, all while expanding accessibility on various platforms. 🌍

Is Hiddify free, ads-free, and open-source?

Yes, Hiddify is🌐:

  1. Free 💸 The Hiddify app is offered for free and has no subscription fees, especially for users worldwide who face internet filtering🌎. It allows users to quickly connect by importing proxies obtained from personal VPN servers (created by Hiddify Manager or any other VPN panel) or free services like Cloudflare WARP without any payment🔗. Additionally, Hiddify Manager is a free VPN server-building tool designed for non-commercial use⚙️.

  2. Ads-Free 🚫📢 Both the Hiddify app and Hiddify Manager are ads-free, providing a clean and distraction-free experience for users🧘‍♂️.

  3. Open-Source 🔓 Hiddify products are fully open-source, with the code available on GitHub. This transparency allows developers to review, contribute to, and customize the code, ensuring security and flexibility🔍.

These features make Hiddify a reliable and accessible tool for users seeking privacy and internet freedom without any cost or interruptions from ads🌈🔐.

How do I contact Hiddify’s support team?

To contact Hiddify’s support team, you can use the following channels📞🌐:

  1. GitHub Issues 🐞💻 For technical support or to report bugs, you can open an issue on the following GitHub repositories:
  2. Hiddify application Repository: github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app

  3. Hiddify Manager Repository: github.com/hiddify/hiddify-manager Opening an issue here allows the development team and the community to assist you directly🤝.

  4. Hiddify Website 🌐 Visit hiddify.com for additional contact information, resources, and documentation📚. The website also provides FAQs and updates to help with common questions🔄.

  5. Community Forums/Social Media 📲 You can also find support or ask questions in Hiddify’s community channels and social media:

  6. Hiddify Telegram Channel: https://t.me/hiddify
  7. Hiddify Support Group: https://t.me/hiddify_board
  8. Hiddify YouTube Channel: youtube.com/@hiddify
  9. Hiddify Instagram Page: instagram.com/hiddify_com
  10. Hiddify X Account (formerly Twitter): x.com/hiddify_com

These channels offer multiple ways to connect with the Hiddify support team and community members, keeping you informed about the latest updates and providing help when needed📢👥.

How can we support Hiddify?

  1. Financial Support 💸 You can support the Hiddify project financially to help with its development and continuation. For more information and to contribute, visit the Hiddify Financial Support page.

  2. Starring the Hiddify Project ⭐ By starring the Hiddify project, especially the repositories for Hiddify application and Hiddify Manager, you can help increase the project's visibility and credibility on GitHub.

  3. Contributing to Development 💻 If you have technical skills, you can contribute to the development of Hiddify. By helping to improve the code, adding new features, or fixing bugs, you can play an active role in the progress of this project. To contribute, simply visit the Hiddify GitHub.

  4. Giving a Five-Star Rating and Writing Reviews in Application Stores 🌟📱 By giving a five-star rating and writing reviews for the Hiddify app in various app stores, you can help increase its credibility and popularity, bringing it to the attention of more users. You can rate the app through the following links:

  5. App Store
  6. Google Play

  7. Microsoft Store

  8. Sharing and Raising Awareness 📢 By sharing Hiddify’s products, especially the Hiddify and Hiddify Manager, on social media and introducing them to people who need anti-censorship tools, you can help spread the project and increase its user base.

  9. Joining Social Channels and Groups 📲 By joining the Hiddify Telegram Channel and the Support Group, you can connect with other users and stay updated on the latest news and updates about the project. Also, follow the latest educational videos on the Hiddify YouTube Channel. Follow us on Instagram and X to stay informed about the latest project updates.

  10. Helping with Content Creation, Especially Video Content 🎥 You can help spread awareness and attract new users by creating educational and promotional content about Hiddify. Video content, such as tutorials on how to use and install Hiddify and highlighting its benefits, can be highly valuable for users. These videos can be shared on social media platforms and video-sharing sites like YouTube and Instagram to assist in better outreach and engagement.

  11. Providing Feedback and Reporting Issues 📝 By using the Hiddify app and submitting your feedback on the Hiddify repos, you can help improve the app's functionality and identify any issues.

Hiddify is built by a group of volunteers.

Development

Our developers bring our vision to life through Hiddify Manager and the Hiddify app.

Design

Our designers create beautiful visuals and improve the experience of Hiddify products through testing with users.

Content

We put together helpful content, from our full tutorials to YouTube videos.

User support

We are always there to answer your questions in our Telegram group.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
This page explains what information Hiddify collects, what it does not collect, and how it is used.

No personal dataNo names, addresses, phones or payments No activity logsNo browsing, destinations, content or DNS No sharingNo data goes to third parties No advertisingThere are no ads in the app

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Services provided by Hiddify are intended for use as is.

We do not gather any information from you. This app needs a private server from you, and we do not provide any server.

Crash data is sent via Sentry in the Hiddify app, without any sensitive data.

docs.title: VPN data
docs.text:
• We DO NOT collect or store any VPN data.
  • We DO NOT modify the contents of your VPN data.
  • We DO NOT share any sensitive or user-specific data with third parties.

This app is just a client app that users use to connect to their own servers. This means the app does not modify any VPN data, and users have complete control over, and liability for, their VPN data.

docs.title: 1.1 We do not Collect Sensitive Information
docs.text:
We do not gather, and do not even have access to, the following information:

  • Names (including subscriber names, usernames, and screen names)
  • Addresses (residential and business)
  • Telephone numbers
  • Payment details (credit card numbers, bank account info, billing records)

We don’t store sensitive data.

No logs are collected on online activities such as:

  • Browsing history
  • Traffic destination
  • Data content
  • DNS queries

docs.title: 1.2 Data Collection
docs.text:
This app needs a private server from your side, and we do not provide any server. So we are not able to gather any information from you. Crash data is sent via Sentry in the Hiddify client app, without any sensitive data.

What information can be sent to your private server that is setup by you or any others?

To add the server link in your client, you need a subscription link. With the subscription link your server can access:

  • Your IP address (as with any HTTP request, so be careful not to trust unknown servers)
  • Your Hiddify version

For your best experience, limited anonymous data can be collected on your server or any other server, after your explicit permission. It can include the following:

  • IP Address information of the Client
  • Operating System Version
  • App Version
  • Connection Status (TCP ping)

docs.title: 1.3 App Permissions
docs.text:
The app does not need any permissions to access your phone’s contacts, location, device ID, storage, microphone, camera, etc.

  • Contacts
  • Location
  • Device ID
  • Storage
  • Microphone

When you scan a QR code, the app may explicitly ask for camera permission.

docs.title: 2. Data Usage
docs.text:
Data is used for:

  • We do not collect any data, so we do not use it.
  • Crash data is sent via Sentry without any sensitive data.

docs.title: 3. Data Sharing and Transfer
docs.text: We do not share any data with any third parties. Crash data is sent via Sentry without any sensitive data.

docs.title: 4. Security Measures
docs.text: Strong security measures implemented to protect data. Staff access limited.

docs.title: 5. Data Retention
docs.text: We do not collect any data, so this does not apply to us.

docs.title: 6. Right to Be Forgotten
docs.text: We do not collect any data, so this does not apply to us.

docs.title: 7. Third Party Services
docs.text: Hiddify is designed to be used with your own deployed server. However, if you use third-party VPN services in our application, you should check their policies.

docs.title: 8. Advertising
docs.text: We do not have any advertising.

docs.title: 9. Children’s Privacy
docs.text: Parents are encouraged to teach children about online privacy.

docs.title: 10. Changes to This Privacy Policy
docs.text: We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. Thus, you are advised to review this page periodically for any changes. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page. These changes are effective immediately after they are posted on this page.

docs.title: Chain, Extra security and Proxy unblocker in the Hiddify app
Chain: Extra security and Proxy unblocker (WARP and Psiphon)
docs.text:
The Hiddify app can put a second free tunnel, WARP or Psiphon, in front of or behind your own profile. This is called the chain. It has two optional layers:

  • Extra security: your traffic leaves through WARP or Psiphon after your proxy. Use it when you don't trust the proxy, for example a public or free config: the proxy's owner can't see your traffic, and sites see the IP of WARP or Psiphon, not of the proxy.
  • Proxy unblocker: your proxy is reached through WARP or Psiphon. Use it when your own (personal) proxy is filtered: the unblocker gets the connection past the filter.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). The screenshots come from Android; the options are the same on every platform. For the free WARP profile itself, see How to use WARP in the Hiddify app.

docs.title: The quick way: Quick settings
docs.text:
On the Home page, tap Quick settings at the bottom.

  1. Extra security ("When you don't trust the proxy"). Once it is on, the line under it says who sets your IP, for example Your IP is set by WARP.
  2. Proxy unblocker ("Gets the proxy past filtering").

Tap the value on the right of either one to choose Turn off, Psiphon or WARP. Configuration opens the Chain page with all the options.

The first time you choose WARP or Psiphon, the app shows its terms (Cloudflare WARP consent or Psiphon license agreement); accept them to continue.

docs.title: The Chain page
docs.text:
Open Settings → Chain (Extra security & unblocker). It shows the path of your traffic from top to bottom:

  • App: your apps' traffic enters the chain here.
  • Extra security (1): off, Psiphon or WARP.
  • Main profile (2): your active profile.
  • Unblocker (3): off, Psiphon or WARP.
  • Filtering: the traffic leaves for the internet.

The green Final IP label shows which layer's IP the sites will see.

Which one should I use?

  • A public or free config you don't trust → Extra security. It may reduce speed.
  • Your own config that is filtered → Proxy unblocker. It is only useful for a personal proxy, not for public ones, and makes the proxy a bit slower.
  • You can use both at once.

docs.title: WARP options
docs.text:
When a layer is set to WARP, its options appear under it:

  1. WARP is selected; Final IP moves to this layer.
  2. Tunnel: how WARP connects: Auto, WireGuard, AmneziaWG or MASQUE. Leave Auto unless WARP does not connect on your network.
  3. License key: a WARP+ key, if you have one. Free WARP needs none.
  4. MTU: leave it on Auto.

With a set tunnel type, more options appear:

  • WireGuard: Endpoint (Assigned by Cloudflare, Scan to find a working address, or Custom), Clean IP, Port, and WireGuard noise (noise count, mode, size and delay; modes such as Standard, Random, QUIC, DNS, SIP or STUN) to make the connection harder to detect. The Scanner has its own options (max RTT, timeout, how many addresses, ports and ranges).
  • AmneziaWG: the junk packet options (Junk packets, Min junk size, Max junk size).
  • MASQUE: HTTP version, server name, IPv6, UDP and keepalive timings, TLS fragment and Encrypted Client Hello (ECH).

For Psiphon you can Select server region (Auto, or a country).

If WARP or Psiphon does not connect, try another Tunnel, or switch the layer to the other provider.

docs.title: DNS and TLS tricks in the Hiddify app
DNS and TLS tricks settings in the Hiddify app
docs.text:
This page explains Settings → DNS and Settings → TLS tricks. The defaults work for most people: change these only when a site does not open or your connection is blocked.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). The screenshots come from Android; the options are the same on every platform.

docs.title: DNS
docs.text:
DNS turns a site's name (google.com) into an IP address. A filter can block or fake these answers, so the app asks a DNS server through the proxy.

  1. Remote DNS: the DNS server used through the proxy for the sites you open. Default: tcp://8.8.8.8. You can pick another from the list (for example udp://1.1.1.1 or https://1.1.1.1/dns-query) or type your own. Remote DNS domain strategy chooses IPv4 or IPv6 answers (Auto, Prefer IPv6, Prefer IPv4, IPv4 only, IPv6 only).
  2. Turn on fake DNS: the app answers DNS with placeholder addresses at once and resolves the real address at the proxy's side. It can make connecting faster; turn it off if an app misbehaves.
  3. Outbound server resolver (direct): the DNS server used without the proxy, to find the address of your proxy servers themselves. Default: 1.1.1.1 (in China 223.5.5.5). Outbound domain strategy works like the strategy above.

Tip

If your profile's servers are given by name and the app can't reach them, change Outbound server resolver to another server, for example 8.8.8.8.

docs.title: TLS tricks
docs.text:
TLS tricks change the first packet of an encrypted (TLS) connection so the filter can't read the site's name in it. They help with configs that the filter blocks by their SNI, the site name sent at the start of TLS.

  1. Turn on fragment: the master switch. The other options can only be changed when it is on.
  2. The fragment options:
    • Fragmentation packets: which packets are cut: TLS Hello (the first one, usually enough) or 1-1 … 1-5.
    • Fragment size: the size of each piece in bytes, as a range (default 10-30).
    • Fragment sleep: the pause between pieces in milliseconds (default 2-8).
  3. Turn on mixed SNI case mixes upper and lower case in the site name (gOoGlE.cOm). Turn on padding adds random bytes to the first packet; Padding size sets how many (default 1-1500).

Tricks can make a connection slower. Turn them on one by one, and turn them off again if they don't help.

How these tricks work, and how to find good values: How the TLS trick works and A good way to find TLS trick values.

Info

You can also send only some sites direct with the fragment trick: in a routing rule, choose Direct with fragment. See Routing in the Hiddify app.

docs.title: DNS tunnels in the Hiddify app: Soar, DNSTT and MasterDNS
docs.text:
When almost everything is blocked but DNS still works, the Hiddify app can carry your traffic inside DNS queries. This page explains what a DNS tunnel is, when it helps, and answers a frequent question: where do I add resolvers?

Written for Hiddify app 5.5

The screenshots come from Hiddify app 5.5 on Android. The profile edit page is the same on computers (Windows, macOS, Linux).

docs.title: What is a DNS tunnel?
docs.text:
• A DNS resolver is the server that turns site names into addresses, like Google's 8.8.8.8 or Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1. On most networks, asking a resolver still works even when everything else is blocked.
  • The app puts your data inside these queries. The resolver carries them to your tunnel server (because the server owns the tunnel domain), and the server connects you to the open internet.
  • The data is encrypted; the resolver and the filter only see ordinary DNS queries.

It is slow

Each DNS query carries only a little data, so a DNS tunnel is much slower than a normal proxy, and it carries TCP only (voice calls and games that need UDP do not work). Use it only when nothing else connects.

docs.title: Three DNS tunnels in the Hiddify app
docs.text: Which one should you use? The one your server runs. You get its link from the server owner and add it like any other link (+ → Clipboard). If your own server is Hiddify Manager 13 or later, it can make DNSTT and MasterDNS tunnels.

docs.title: Where do I add resolvers?
docs.text:
The app has no separate "add resolver" screen: resolvers are part of the profile itself. There are three ways:

Whichever way the resolvers come in, the app tests them all and uses only those that really answered; if one stops working, it is set aside and the next one takes its place. So listing a few extra resolvers does no harm.

docs.title: Way 1: in the profile link
docs.text:
Whoever makes the link writes the resolvers in it. If you make the link yourself, or want to change it before adding it, find this part:

  • Soar and MasterDNS: resolvers=8.8.8.8,1.1.1.1
  • DNSTT: resolver=8.8.8.8,1.1.1.1 (no s)

docs.title: Way 2: automatic
docs.text: If the link has no resolvers, or says resolvers=auto instead of a list, the app finds resolvers itself: the device's own, a ready list for your country (Iran, China and Russia), and public resolvers. It takes the country from Region in the routing settings, or from country=ir in the link. resolvers=8.8.8.8,auto means "this resolver, plus automatic finding".

docs.title: Way 3: edit by hand in the app
docs.text:
For a profile you have already added:

  1. On the home screen, tap the profile name to open the profile list, tap ⋮ next to the profile and choose Edit.

  2. In the Config Editor, open outbounds → 0 → resolvers. Tap ⋯ next to resolvers, then Append and String: an empty line is added.

  3. The easiest way to type the address: in the tree menu above the editor, choose text. The whole config is now text: type the address inside the empty "", for example "9.9.9.9". Every address is in quotes and separated from the next by a comma. You can also delete a resolver or add "auto".

  4. Tap Save at the top. Profile saved appears.

Subscription profiles

If this profile came from a subscription link, the next update of the subscription may wipe your edit. In that case, ask the server owner to put the resolvers in the link itself.

docs.title: A few tips
docs.text:
• Which resolvers? Start with auto; the app finds the best ones itself. If on your network only domestic resolvers answer (for example your operator's), add them next to auto.
  • Doesn't connect? First make sure a normal proxy really does not work; then add a few more resolvers or set auto. If no resolver forwards the tunnel domain's queries to the server, a DNS tunnel cannot help.
For experts
  • A resolver can be 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1:5353. With the smart resolver pool (on by default), tcp://, DoT (dot://host:853) and DoH (https://host/dns-query) work too.
  • Every setting of each tunnel, including the smart pool and automatic finding: Soar, DNSTT, MasterDNS and the smart resolver pool.

docs.title: Free profiles in the Hiddify app
Free profiles in the Hiddify app
docs.text:
No server and no link yet? The Hiddify app has a few free profiles you can add with one tap. They are meant for emergencies: they are shared by many people and there is no guarantee that they work.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). The list of free profiles is loaded from the internet, so it can change without an app update. The profiles shown depend on the Region you chose (Settings → Routing).

docs.title: Add a free profile
docs.text:
1. On the Home page, tap + (Add profile) at the top.

  2. Turn on Free at the bottom of the panel.

  3. The free profiles appear, each with a tag (WARP, Mix or Serverless). Tap one.

  4. Read the note about the profile, then tap Continue to add it (or Cancel).

The profile is added like any other profile, and updates itself.

docs.title: The free profiles
docs.text:
Profile Tag For What it is WARP & Psiphon WARP Iran, China and other regions Cloudflare WARP (a free WireGuard VPN) and Psiphon. Adding it means you agree to Cloudflare WARP's terms of service and privacy policy. Patterniha Mix Iran Public configs, published with their owners' consent, collected, tested and checked. Anonymous Mix Iran Public configs from another collection, tested the same way. Mahsa Mix Iran Public configs from another collection, tested the same way. Anonymous Serverless Serverless Iran Configs with no server in between: they use features of the Hiddify core to reach sites directly. They only work for services that are not blocked by IP. The profile may have several variants: if one does not work on your network, try another.

The configs in the Mix profiles are run by people you don't know. For more safety, you can turn on Extra security. It adds a WARP or Psiphon layer after the config: your traffic leaves through WARP or Psiphon, so the people who run the config cannot see it. It is not turned on automatically; turn it on yourself for any public or free config.

Warning

There is no guarantee that free configs work. Use them only in emergencies, and don't send passwords or other sensitive information through a config you don't trust.

docs.title: The Hiddify app on Windows, macOS and Linux
The Hiddify app on a computer: VPN or system proxy, administrator permission, tray
docs.text:
On Windows, macOS and Linux, the Hiddify app works like on a phone, with a few things of its own: how it sends your traffic (VPN or system proxy), the administrator permission that VPN mode needs once, the tray icon, and starting with your computer.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.6). To install the app, see How to install the Hiddify app. On a computer the menu is a sidebar on the left (Home, Profiles, Settings, Logs, About) instead of the tabs at the bottom.

docs.title: VPN or system proxy?
docs.text:
Since 5.9 the app starts in VPN mode on computers too. The first time you connect in VPN mode, it asks Send all apps through the VPN? with two choices:

  • Use VPN mode (All apps, recommended): Hiddify adds a virtual network to your computer, and every app goes through it on its own: browsers, Telegram, games, updates. Name lookups (DNS) go through Hiddify too, so sites blocked that way open as well. It needs administrator permission once, to install Hiddify's background service; after that it connects without asking. (The Linux AppImage asks at each start.) Turn off other VPN apps while you use it.
  • Use system proxy (Browsers and most apps): Hiddify changes your computer's proxy setting. Apps that follow it, such as browsers, go through Hiddify; the rest (Telegram, many games, some update tools) connect directly. No administrator permission is needed, and Hiddify puts the setting back when you disconnect.

What is this? in that window explains both. If you pick the system proxy, the app says Switched to system proxy mode. You can change it in Settings.

When you choose VPN mode, the system asks for permission: on Windows click Yes; on macOS enter your Mac password; on Linux enter your password. If you cancel that prompt or type a wrong password, the app shows Administrator permission was not given, so VPN mode could not connect. Tap connect again to get the same choice, or pick Use system proxy.

docs.title: Change the mode later
docs.text:
• Settings → Inbound → Service mode: VPN, Set system proxy, Proxy service only (only apps you point at the local proxy, port 12334), and on Linux Router (whole network), see Router mode on Linux.
  • The Quick settings on the Home page, or the tray icon menu.

Click Quick settings at the bottom of the Home page: the four buttons at the top switch the mode (Router appears on Linux only).

docs.title: Administrator permission for a profile
docs.text:
Some settings of a profile work better with administrator permission. Then the app asks Administrator permission recommended: Run as administrator, or Continue without administrator permission (those settings are turned off for this connection). Show configurations lists which settings need it, and Don't ask again for this profile remembers your answer.

You can change that answer on the profile's page (profile ⋮ → Edit): Administrator permission: Ask each time, Always use administrator permission or Always continue without administrator permission.

docs.title: Tray icon
docs.text:
The app puts an icon in the system tray (on Linux, in the top bar). Its menu has:

  • Dashboard (Linux): opens the window.
  • Connect / Disconnect.
  • Service mode: switch between the modes.
  • Quit: closes the app and disconnects.

docs.title: Start with your computer, and closing the window
docs.text:
In Settings → General:

  • Start at login: the app opens when you sign in to your computer.
  • Start minimized: it starts in the tray, without a window.
  • When closing the window: Ask each time, hide the app to the tray (it stays connected), or exit it. When asked (Hide or exit the app?), Remember this choice saves your answer.

docs.title: Other settings only on computers
docs.text:
• Settings → General → Use the system's TLS when available: connections without a TLS fingerprint use the TLS of Windows or macOS.
  • Settings → Inbound has extra ports: Direct port, and on Linux and macOS also Transparent proxy port and Redirect port.
  • Routing rules can match Process names and Process paths (for example chrome.exe): see Routing in the Hiddify app.

docs.title: The Hiddify app on Android TV
The Hiddify app on Android TV: add a profile from your phone
docs.text:
Typing a long subscription link with a TV remote is slow. Since version 5.9, the Hiddify app on Android TV can take the link from your phone instead: scan a code on the TV, paste the link on your phone, and import it on the TV.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.6) on Android TV and Google TV. The TV uses the Android app: see How to install the Hiddify app. On the TV the menu is a sidebar on the left: Home, Settings, Logs, About (and Profiles once you have added a profile).

docs.title: Add a profile from your phone
docs.text:
You need: the TV and your phone on the same Wi-Fi network, and your subscription link on the phone.

  1. On the TV, open Hiddify and choose + (Add profile) at the top.

  2. The panel shows Add from your phone with a QR code.

  3. Scan the code with your phone's camera. A page opens on the phone: Send to Hiddify on your TV, with four short steps. (No camera app? Type the address shown under the code, for example 192.168.1.20:40413/098732, into the phone's browser.)

  4. On the phone, copy your subscription link (or any proxy link or config), tap the box on that page, paste the link, and tap Send to TV.

    Then a green Sent to your TV box appears at the top and all three steps get a tick. The page stays open, so you can send another link if you want.

  5. The link shows up on the TV (Received from your phone). Press Import with the remote, or Discard if it is the wrong link. Nothing is added until you press Import.

    The profile is on the TV's home page, ready to connect:

The panel closes after each import. To send another link, open + (Add profile) on the TV again.

Info

  • The page on the phone works only while Add profile is open on the TV, and only on your local network. Nothing goes over the internet.
  • If the TV says it is not on a local network, connect it to Wi-Fi.
  • After too many wrong codes the TV locks the code: close Add profile and open it again for a new one.

docs.title: From the Hiddify app on your phone
docs.text:
If the profile is already in the Hiddify app on your phone, you don't need to copy the link:

  1. On the TV, open + (Add profile) so that the code shows.

  2. On the phone, open the profile's ⋮ menu and choose Share. The share window has a Send to TV button: tap it and scan the code on the TV.

    Send to TV is there only for profiles that have a subscription link. For a profile you made from a single config, copy its link and use the page above instead.

  3. Press Import on the TV.

If the phone says it couldn't reach the TV, check that both are on the same Wi-Fi. If it says the code expired, open Add profile on the TV again and scan the new code.

docs.title: Other ways
docs.text: The Add profile panel on the TV also has Clipboard, File and Manually, and the Free switch for the free profiles.

docs.title: Everything else works like on Android
docs.text: The TV runs the same Android app. After the profile is added, connecting, choosing a server, the settings, routing, WARP, DNS and TLS tricks and sharing the connection work as on a phone; only the layout is wider and you move with the remote (arrows and OK). See How to use the Hiddify app for the basics.

HiddifyCli is now called Hiddify Core (hiddify-core). Its guide has moved and is kept up to date on the Hiddify Core pages. This page is kept so that old links still work.

Go to the Hiddify Core guide Command-line reference

docs.text:

The commands are the same as before, only the program name changed: HiddifyCli run -c <link> is now hiddify-core run -c <link>. On Windows the file is still called HiddifyCli.exe.

docs.title: Free internet for every device behind an OpenWrt router
docs.text:
With Hiddify Core on your OpenWrt router, every phone, laptop, TV and game console at home can use your proxy, without installing anything on them. This page explains how.

Written for Hiddify Core 5.9

This page is for Hiddify Core 5.9 (5.9.3). Older versions of this guide set this up by hand with redsocks and iptables rules. That is not needed any more: the Hiddify Core package has a router mode that does it, and the old iptables commands do not work on OpenWrt 22.03 and newer, which use nftables.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Install Hiddify Core on the router and give it your connection link: follow Hiddify Core on OpenWrt, steps 1 and 2.

docs.title: Router mode (the default)
docs.text:
The Hiddify Core package starts in router mode. In this mode:

  • every device behind the router goes through the proxy, for TCP, UDP and ping;
  • nothing needs to be set up on the devices: they keep using the router as usual;
  • connections from outside still reach the router and its port forwards.

To check it, connect a phone or computer to the router's Wi-Fi or cable and open a site that shows your IP address. It should show the IP of your proxy server.

If router mode was turned off, turn it on again:

uci set hiddify-core.main.mode='router'
uci commit hiddify-core
/etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
• Look at the log: logread -e hiddify-core. Errors about the config or the subscription mean the link in step 2 is wrong or can't be downloaded.
  • Check that the service runs: /etc/init.d/hiddify-core status.
  • Restart it: /etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart.
  • If only the router itself should use the proxy, use proxy mode instead (option mode 'proxy'): the proxy then runs at 127.0.0.1:12334 on the router only. See Router mode and proxy mode.

docs.title: How to contribute to the Hiddify app
docs.text:
The Hiddify app is open source: github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app. You can help by reporting problems, translating, or changing the code. This page shows each way.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

The commands below match the repository as of version 5.9 (Flutter 3.38.5 or newer).

docs.title: Report a problem or suggest a feature
docs.text:
1. Search the issues, open and closed. If someone already reported it, add what you know there.
  2. Otherwise open a new issue and pick Bug report or Feature request. Write the app version (Settings › About), your device and system, and the steps that cause the problem.
  3. Add the logs. How to get them, and how to send a crash report from the app: Logs and reporting a problem. Remove your links, IPs and passwords before you post.

For a big change, open an issue first and agree on it with the maintainers, before you write code.

docs.title: Translate
docs.text:
The app's texts are in assets/translations: one file per language, such as fa.i18n.json. en.i18n.json is the base; every other file has the same keys.

  • To fix a translation, edit the file of your language on GitHub (the pencil icon) and send the change as a pull request. GitHub makes the fork and the branch for you.
  • Keep the keys, the ${…} placeholders and the line breaks (\n) as they are; translate only the text.
  • If you work locally, run make translate after editing to check the files and regenerate the code.

docs.title: 1. Get the code
docs.text:
1. On GitHub, open hiddify/hiddify-app and click Fork. This makes your own copy of the repository under your account.
  2. Clone (download) your fork, and add the original repository as upstream:
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/hiddify-app.git
cd hiddify-app
git remote add upstream https://github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app.git

docs.title: 2. Install the tools
docs.text:
• Flutter 3.38.5 or newer (flutter --version shows it), with its tools for your target: Android Studio and the Android SDK for Android; Xcode for iOS and macOS; Visual Studio with "Desktop development with C++" for Windows.
  • make, curl and tar. On Debian or Ubuntu, make linux-install-deps installs what a Linux build needs.

docs.title: 3. Prepare a platform
docs.text:
Run the command for the platform you build for:

make android-prepare     # or: windows-prepare, linux-prepare, macos-prepare, ios-prepare

It runs flutter pub get, generates the code (dart run build_runner build) and the translations (dart run slang), and downloads the Hiddify Core library for that platform from the hiddify-core releases. Run it again after you switch branches.

While you work:

  • after changing a model, provider or anything with generated code: make gen;
  • after changing a translation file: make translate.

docs.title: 4. Run it
docs.text:
flutter devices           # lists phones, emulators and your computer
flutter run -d <device-id>

A release build for testing: make android-release (or windows-release, linux-release, macos-release).

docs.title: 5. Build the core yourself (optional)
docs.text:
Only needed if you change Hiddify Core too. The core is the hiddify-core submodule; it needs Go:

git config submodule.hiddify-core.url https://github.com/hiddify/hiddify-core.git   # if you have no SSH key on GitHub
git submodule update --init --recursive hiddify-core
make build-android-libs   # or: build-windows-libs, build-linux-libs, build-macos-libs, build-ios-libs

Changes to the core itself go to hiddify-core (and hiddify-sing-box), as their own pull requests. Don't work around a core bug in the app: fix it in the core, or report it there.

docs.title: 6. Send your change
docs.text:
1. Start a branch from the latest code:

    git fetch upstream
git switch -c fix/short-name upstream/main

  2. Make one change per branch. Write commit messages in the Conventional Commits style, for example fix(home): keep the connect button disabled while stopping.

  3. Don't commit generated files (*.g.dart, *.freezed.dart, the generated translations in lib/gen), the downloaded core libraries, the hiddify-core submodule pointer, or any real link, IP or key.
  4. Test on Android and on one desktop system.

  5. Bring your branch up to date and push it to your fork:

    git fetch upstream
git rebase upstream/main
git push -u origin fix/short-name

  6. On GitHub, open a pull request from your branch to hiddify/hiddify-app, base main. Say what was wrong, what you changed and how you tested it. For a change you can see, add before and after screenshots or short videos.

docs.title: Talk to the team
docs.text:
• Hiddify group on Telegram and channel
  • Email: contribute@hiddify.com

docs.title: How to install the Hiddify app
How to install the Hiddify app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to download and install Hiddify app on your phone or computer. Hiddify app is a free, ad-free and open-source client that connects you to a proxy or VPN server so you can reach the free internet. You need it if someone (or your own Hiddify server) gave you a config or subscription link.

Hiddify app is built on sing-box (the engine that makes the connections). It supports many protocols, including VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Reality, TUIC, Hysteria, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, Naive and SSH, and it accepts sing-box, V2ray, Clash and Clash Meta subscription links. See the full feature list on GitHub.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2), a pre-release for now. The download links below always give you the latest version. The store versions (Google Play, App Store, Microsoft Store) may still be on the stable version 5.5.5 for a while.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Check that your device is supported:

Device What you need Android Android 7.0 or later iPhone / iPad iOS 15 or later Windows Windows 10 (version 1809) or Windows 11, 64-bit macOS macOS 10.15 (Catalina) or later, Intel or Apple Silicon Linux 64-bit Linux, x64 or ARM64 (arm64); Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora-based systems are best supported

Windows 7 and Windows 8

Hiddify app does not support Windows 7 or 8.

docs.title: Which file should I download?
docs.text:
Pick the row for your device. Store versions update themselves; the files from GitHub do not.

Device Recommended Other options Android Google Play APK file: universal (works on every phone), arm64, arm7, x86_64 iPhone / iPad App Store — Windows Setup file (.exe) Microsoft Store, MSIX package, portable ZIP, winget macOS DMG file PKG installer, App Store (Apple Silicon Macs) Linux Install command (below), which picks the right package for your system .deb x64, .deb ARM64 (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint), .rpm x64, .rpm ARM64 (Fedora, openSUSE), AppImage x64, AppImage ARM64

All files are also listed on the GitHub releases page.

docs.title: Install the app
docs.text:
Open the section for your device.

Install on Android (click)

From Google Play (recommended)

  1. Open Hiddify on Google Play.
  2. Tap Install.
  3. When the install finishes, tap Open.

From an APK file (if you cannot use Google Play)

  1. Download the universal APK. It works on every Android phone.

  2. Open the downloaded file from your notifications or from the Downloads folder.

  3. Android shows Preparing app... for a moment, then a warning that apps from unknown sources can be risky. Tap Continue. (On some phones it asks instead to turn on Allow from this source in Settings; turn it on and go back.)

  4. Android asks Install this app?. Tap Install.

  5. When you see App installed, tap Open (or Done to open it later).

If Google Play Protect asks

Google Play Protect may warn about an app from outside Google Play. Tap More details, then Install without scanning.

Install on iPhone or iPad (click)

  1. Open Hiddify Proxy & VPN on the App Store.

  2. Tap Get and confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your password. When it is installed, the button changes to Open.

  3. Open the app. The first time you connect, iOS asks if Hiddify may add VPN configurations: tap Allow.

  4. Enter your iPhone passcode to confirm. You only do this once; after that, the app connects directly.

Note

The app is not available in the App Store of every country. If you cannot find it, your Apple ID may be set to a country where it is not offered.

Install on Windows (click)

You can also install from the Microsoft Store, or open Command Prompt and run:

winget install Hiddify.Next

(Hiddify.Next is the app's old name; it still installs the current Hiddify app.)

To install with the setup file:

  1. Download the setup file (Hiddify-Windows-Setup-x64.exe) and double-click it.

  2. If a blue Windows protected your PC window appears, click More info. Windows shows this for apps that are not yet well known to it; it does not mean the file is harmful.

  3. Click Run anyway.

  4. Windows asks "Do you want to allow this app from an unknown publisher to make changes to your device?". Click Yes.

  5. Choose the language of the installer and click OK. (The installer has no Persian; the app itself does, you choose it on the first start.)

  6. The installer shows where the app will be installed. Keep the default folder and click Next.

  7. Choose extra options: a desktop shortcut, and Automatically start Hiddify when Windows starts. Click Next.

  8. Click Install, and wait while the files are copied.

    A green bar shows the progress. It usually takes less than a minute; do not close the window or click Cancel.

  9. When you see Completing the Hiddify Setup Wizard, keep Launch Hiddify ticked and click Finish. The app starts. Later you can start it from the desktop shortcut or the Start menu.

If the app does not start

If Windows shows an error about a missing file such as MSVCP140.dll, install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64) and try again.

Install on macOS (click)

On a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) you can also install from the App Store.

To install with the DMG file:

  1. Download the DMG file (Hiddify-MacOS.dmg). It works on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.

  2. Open your Downloads folder and double-click the file. A window opens; the install steps are written in it, in English and Persian.

  3. Drag the Hiddify icon onto the Applications folder. This copies the app to your Mac.

  4. Before you open the app for the first time, open Terminal (in Applications > Utilities, or search for it with Spotlight) and run this command. It removes the quarantine flag that macOS adds to downloaded apps:

    sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Hiddify.app

    Type your Mac password when asked (nothing appears while you type) and press Return.

  5. Open Applications and double-click Hiddify.

\"Hiddify\" Not Opened (or \"Hiddify.app\" is damaged)

If you skip step 4, macOS refuses to open the app. On macOS 15 the message is "Hiddify" Not Opened: Apple could not verify "Hiddify" is free of malware…, with the buttons Done and Move to Trash; older macOS versions say "Hiddify.app" is damaged and can't be opened. The app is not harmful: click Done (or Cancel), not Move to Trash, run the command from step 4, and open the app again.

Another way: the PKG installer from Terminal

Download Hiddify-MacOS-Installer.pkg and install it from Terminal. The app is then installed without the quarantine flag, so step 4 is not needed:

sudo installer -pkg ~/Downloads/Hiddify-MacOS-Installer.pkg -target /

Double-clicking the .pkg file in Finder shows the same "Not Opened" message, because the installer is not signed by Apple.

From now on, you can open Hiddify from Applications like any other app.

Install on Linux (click)

Option 1: Install command (easiest)

Open a terminal and run:

bash <(curl -fsSL https://github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app/releases/latest/download/install.sh)

The script finds your system (x64 or ARM64; Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/openSUSE or other), downloads the right file of the release, checks it and installs it: the .deb package on Debian and Ubuntu, the .rpm package on Fedora and openSUSE, and the AppImage on other systems. When your system can use more than one, it asks which one you want. Type your password when asked. The same command also installs the app on macOS.

On Debian and Ubuntu it asks Choose 1-2 [1]: press Enter for 1, the .deb package with its VPN service (recommended), or type 2 for the AppImage in ~/.local/bin (for your user only). When it prints Done. Start Hiddify from the app menu., open Hiddify from your applications menu.

Option 2: AppImage (works on most 64-bit distributions)

  1. Download the AppImage file (Hiddify-Linux-x64.AppImage; on an ARM64 computer, Hiddify-Linux-arm64.AppImage). You do not need to extract it.

  2. Open a terminal and make the file executable. This example assumes the file is in your Downloads folder:

    chmod +x ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Linux-x64.AppImage

  3. Start the app:

    ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Linux-x64.AppImage

    You can also double-click the file in your file manager.

If nothing happens or you see an error about FUSE (a system library that AppImage files need), install it in a terminal and try again.

On Ubuntu 22.04:

sudo apt install libfuse2

On Ubuntu 24.04 and newer:

sudo apt install libfuse2t64

Option 3: .deb or .rpm package

  1. Download the .deb package (Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint) or the .rpm package (Fedora, openSUSE). On an ARM64 computer, take the ARM64 .deb or the ARM64 .rpm.

  2. In a terminal, run the command for your package:

    sudo apt install ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Debian-x64.deb

    sudo dnf install ~/Downloads/Hiddify-rpm-x64.rpm

  3. Open Hiddify from your applications menu.

docs.title: First start
docs.text:
The first time you open the app, a welcome screen with three options opens. The app picks the language from your phone's settings. Check the three options, then tap Start.

PhoneComputer

  1. Language: if the app's language is wrong, tap Language and choose yours.
  2. Region: tap Region and choose the country you are in (for example Iran (ir)). Choosing Persian as the language does not change the region by itself; the default is Other. The app uses this to open local websites directly, without the proxy. If your country is not in the list, choose Other.
  3. Turn on analytics: this switch is off by default. If you turn it on, the app sends anonymous crash and usage data that helps the developers improve it.
  4. Tap Start.

You should now see the app's home page. Next time you open the app, it goes straight to this page. The + button at the top adds a config or subscription link, and the big button in the middle (Tap to connect) connects you. The small label next to the name shows your app version.

Note

The phone screenshots on this page come from version 5.9.6 on Android 17, and the computer ones from Windows 11. On other phones the system screens may look a little different.

docs.title: How to use the Hiddify app
How to use the Hiddify app
docs.text: This page shows you how to add your connection link to Hiddify app, connect, pick a server and change the most useful settings. It is for anyone who has installed the app and received a link from their provider or from their own Hiddify server.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  1. Hiddify app installed on your device. If you have not installed it yet, follow How to install the Hiddify app.
  2. A connection link from your provider. This is usually your user page link (a personal web page that a Hiddify panel makes for each user) or a subscription link. No link yet? The app has free profiles too: see Add a free profile.

A few words you will see on this page:

  • Profile: one connection link saved in the app. A profile can contain many servers.
  • Subscription link: a link that gives the app a list of servers and updates it automatically. It must start with https://; the app does not accept plain http:// subscription links.
  • Config: the settings for one single server, for example a link that starts with vless:// or vmess://.
  • Proxy: one server in your profile that your traffic can go through.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). Version 5.9 is a pre-release for now; the stable version 5.5.5 does not have every feature on this page yet. The screenshots come from Android. On iPhone and on computers the steps are the same, but some screens look a little different.

docs.title: Add a profile to the app
docs.text:
1. Open your user page link (you got it from your provider or panel admin). It shows your remaining traffic and days, and a big connect button.

  2. Tap the big button in the middle. The "Configure Your VPN" window opens.

  3. Tap HiddifyApp. The app opens and adds your profile, and you are done. If the app does not open, tap Copy Link at the bottom of the same window to copy your profile link, and go on with step 4.

  4. Open Hiddify app. On the Home page, tap the + button at the top of the screen. The "Add profile" panel opens at the bottom.

  5. Add the copied link in one of these ways:

    • Tap Clipboard. The app reads the link you copied and adds it.

    • Or tap Manually, type any name in Name, paste the link in URL, and tap Add. You can also turn off auto update, or choose how often the app updates the profile.

    • Or, if the link is shown as a QR code, tap QR code and point your camera at it.

    • Or, if you got the profile as a file, tap File and choose it.

When it worked, your profile appears at the top of the Home page. If you see "Invalid URL" or "Failed to add profile", check that you copied the whole link and that it starts with https://.

docs.title: Add a free profile
docs.text:
If you have no link, you can still try the app with a free profile:

  1. Tap + on the Home page.

  2. Turn on the Free switch at the bottom of the panel. A list of free profiles appears, for example WARP & Psiphon, Patterniha, Anonymous, Mahsa and Anonymous Serverless. The list comes from the internet and can change.

  3. Tap a profile. Some profiles show their terms first (for WARP & Psiphon, the terms of Cloudflare WARP). Tap Continue to accept them and add the profile.

Free profiles are shared by many people and are not always fast. Use them when you have nothing else. See also How to use WARP in the Hiddify app.

docs.title: Add a single config
docs.text:
Use this if you want to add only one server instead of a whole subscription.

  1. On your user page, tap the menu button (☰) at the top and choose All Configs.

  2. The page lists your subscription links first, then each single config under Individual Configs. Tap Get Link next to the config you want.

  3. In the window that opens, tap Copy Link. (Another phone can also scan the QR code in this window.)

  4. Open Hiddify app and tap the + button.

  5. Tap Clipboard. The config is added to the app.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. After you add the profile from your panel, the Home page looks like this. The card at the top shows the active profile with the name you gave it, how much traffic you have used of your plan (here 0GiB / 10GiB) and how many days are left.

  2. Tap the big connect button in the middle of the screen (Tap to connect).

  3. The first time, your phone asks for permission:

    • On Android, the app may first ask to send notifications: tap Allow. Then Android shows "Connection request": tap OK.
    • On iPhone, tap Allow and enter your passcode (see How to install the Hiddify app).
    • On a computer, see VPN mode on a computer.

When the connection works, the button turns green and shows Connected, with the delay (how fast the server answers) under it. Below that, a card shows the proxy you are using right now. With a Hiddify panel profile it usually shows Select · Auto: the Auto group tests all the configs of your panel and uses the fastest one. To disconnect, tap the big button again.

If it stays on Connecting... or shows an error, try another server on the Proxies page (see below), or tap the update button on your profile card to download a fresh server list. If nothing works, contact your provider.

docs.title: Manage profiles
docs.text:
• Update a profile: tap the update button (the two arrows) on the left of the profile card. This downloads the newest server list from your provider.

  • Switch to another profile: tap the profile card. A list of all your profiles opens; tap the one you want. In this list, Sort changes the order and Update subscriptions updates all of them at once.

  • Pin, update, share, edit or delete a profile: in the list, tap the three dots on the left of a profile.

  • Share a profile: Share shows a QR code that another phone can scan with Hiddify, the subscription link to copy, and Send to TV to send the profile to Hiddify on an Android TV.

docs.title: Check and choose a server (Proxies)
docs.text:
1. Connect first. Then, on the Home page, tap the card of the active proxy (under the connect button). The Proxies page opens.

  2. You see every config that your panel gives you, for example XHTTP VLess TLS H1 D1 IP4 or gRPC VLess D1 IP4, with its delay on the right. The first entry, Auto, is not a server: it always uses the fastest config. Delay is how long the server takes to answer, in milliseconds (ms): lower is faster.

  3. By default Auto is selected. To use one specific config instead, tap it; tap Auto to go back.
  4. To measure the delay again, tap the lightning button at the bottom right (Test delay). The button above it (Speed test) measures download and upload speed.

  5. To sort the list, tap the sort button at the top and choose Default, Alphabetically, By delay, By usage, By upload speed or By download speed.

  6. To see the details of a server, touch and hold it. You can also Share that one server or Edit it (the app copies it to a new profile of its own), or turn on Pin proxy so that it always stays loaded and tested beside the fastest ones.

docs.title: Quick settings
docs.text:
On the Home page, tap Quick settings at the bottom of the screen. From here you can:

  • Choose the service mode:
    • VPN: all traffic of the device goes through the app. This is the default on phones and computers.
    • Proxy: the app only runs a local proxy. Other apps must be set up to use it.
    • System proxy (computers only): browsers and most apps use the proxy automatically. See VPN mode on a computer.
  • Turn on Connection sharing: other devices on your network can use your connection.
  • Extra security (for when you don't trust the proxy): adds an extra layer, so the provider of your proxy can't see your traffic. Good for public and anonymous proxies. It may make the connection slower.
  • Proxy unblocker: helps a filtered proxy connect. It is useful for a personal proxy, not for public ones, and makes the proxy a bit slower.

Leave Extra security and Proxy unblocker on Off unless you need them. You find the same options under Settings > Chain.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Tap Settings at the bottom of the screen. The settings are grouped into General, Chain, Routing, DNS, Inbound, TLS tricks, Logs and About. Leave everything except General at the defaults unless your provider tells you to change it.

Open General. The most useful options are:

  • Language: the language of the app.
  • Theme mode: System default, Light mode, Dark mode or Black mode (fully black, which saves battery on some phone screens).
  • Turn on analytics: send anonymous crash reports to help the developers. It is off by default.
  • Reduce animations: keeps the connect button still and stops looping effects, to save battery.
  • Turn off battery optimization (Android): stops Android from closing the VPN in the background.
  • Start at login (computers): start the app when you log in.
  • Start minimized (computers): start the app hidden in the system tray (the small icons next to the clock) instead of opening its window.

The service mode is also under Settings > Inbound > Service mode.

docs.title: VPN mode on a computer
docs.text:
On Windows, macOS and Linux, the app now starts in VPN mode, like on phones: all apps, including Telegram and games, go through Hiddify.

VPN mode needs administrator permission once (called root on Linux and macOS). The first time you connect, the app asks "Send all apps through the VPN?" and offers two choices:

  • Use VPN mode (recommended): all apps go through Hiddify. Your computer then asks for administrator permission: click Yes on Windows, or enter your password on macOS and Linux. After that, the app connects without asking again. With the AppImage on Linux, it asks once each time you start the app.
  • Use system proxy: no administrator permission is needed, but only browsers and most apps go through Hiddify; Telegram and a few other apps are left out. You can switch back to VPN later in Quick settings or in Settings > Inbound > Service mode.

On Linux the password prompt looks like this (its look depends on your desktop):

When it is connected, the home page shows Connected:

More about the modes, the tray icon and starting with the computer: The Hiddify app on a computer.

Turn off other VPN apps while you use VPN mode: two VPNs at once get in each other's way. On Linux there is also a Router (whole network) mode, which sends the traffic of every device that this computer routes through Hiddify: see Router mode on Linux.

If you cancelled the permission prompt, just connect again and choose again. If the app still shows "Missing privilege" or "Administrator permission was not given", close it completely (right-click its icon in the system tray and click Exit), then open it as administrator:

Open the app as administrator on Windows

  1. Right-click the Hiddify icon on the desktop or in the Start menu and click Run as administrator.

  1. Click Yes when Windows asks for permission.

Open the app as administrator on macOS

  1. If the app is open, close it completely: click the Hiddify icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen (next to the clock) and click Exit.
  2. Open the Terminal app (in Applications > Utilities, or search for it with Spotlight).

  3. Type this command in Terminal and press Return:

    sudo /Applications/Hiddify.app/Contents/MacOS/Hiddify

  4. Type your Mac password and press Return. Nothing appears while you type the password; that is normal. The app opens with administrator rights.

Keep the Terminal window open while you use the app: if you close Terminal, the app closes too.

If macOS says \"Hiddify.app\" is damaged

This means macOS put the downloaded app in quarantine; the app is not broken. Run this command once in Terminal and open the app again (full steps in How to install the Hiddify app):

sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Hiddify.app

Open the app as root on Linux

With the .deb package (what the install command installs): install Hiddify's VPN service once from a terminal, then connect again in the app. You do not need to run the app itself with sudo:

sudo /opt/hiddify/HiddifyCli admin_bgservice install $USER

This is the same command the password prompt runs. It is useful when no password window appears, for example when you started Hiddify from a terminal or over SSH.

With the AppImage: open a terminal and run the app with sudo. This example is for the AppImage in your Downloads folder; change the path if your file is somewhere else:

sudo ~/Downloads/Hiddify-Linux-x64-AppImage.AppImage

  • Routing: send some sites or apps direct, or through the proxy
  • DNS and TLS tricks: when configs don't connect
  • Chain, Extra security and Proxy unblocker

docs.title: Hiddify Core on OpenWrt
docs.text:
This page shows how to install Hiddify Core on an OpenWrt router, give it your connection link, and send the traffic of your whole home network through it. Hiddify Core (hiddify-core, also called HiddifyCli) is the engine of the Hiddify app, without the app: see Hiddify Core.

Written for Hiddify Core 5.9

This page is for Hiddify Core 5.9 (5.9.3) and OpenWrt 23.05 or newer (OpenWrt 24.10 and 25.12 use the apk package manager, older versions opkg). Older guides told you to download hiddify-cli-linux-…tar.gz and write a service by hand: that is not needed any more, and those files no longer exist.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Free space on the router: Hiddify Core needs about 105 MB of free storage. Check it on the router:

    df -h /overlay

    Many small routers have only 16 to 128 MB of flash. If yours has less free space, add a USB drive as extra storage (extroot) first, or use a router or mini PC with more storage.

  • SSH access to the router (ssh root@192.168.1.1, or the address of your router).

  • A connection link: a subscription link or config links, for example from your Hiddify panel.

docs.title: Step 1: install
docs.text:
The installer finds your router's processor, downloads the ready package of the latest Hiddify Core release, installs it and starts the service. It needs bash and curl, which OpenWrt does not have by default.

  1. Install bash and curl.

    On OpenWrt 24.10 and newer (apk):

    apk update && apk add bash curl

    On OpenWrt 23.05 (opkg):

    opkg update && opkg install bash curl

  2. Run the installer:

    bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hiddify/hiddify-core/main/installer.sh)

When it finishes, it prints Installation successful! and the places of the config and the service.

Install the package by hand instead

Each Hiddify Core release has a package for every OpenWrt processor type: .apk files for OpenWrt 24.10 and newer, .ipk files for OpenWrt 23.05.

  1. Find your router's package architecture: apk --print-arch (or, on OpenWrt 23.05, opkg print-architecture, the last line). For example mipsel_24kc, aarch64_cortex-a53 or x86_64.
  2. Download the file with that name from the release, for example hiddify-core-5.9.3-r0_mipsel_24kc.apk or hiddify-core_5.9.3_mipsel_24kc.ipk, and copy it to /tmp on the router.
  3. Install it: apk add --allow-untrusted /tmp/hiddify-core-*.apk (or opkg install /tmp/hiddify-core_*.ipk).
  4. Start it: /etc/init.d/hiddify-core enable && /etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart.

docs.title: Step 2: give it your connection link
docs.text:
Hiddify Core's run command reads your links and builds the rest of the configuration by itself. It reads subscription links, single config links (vless://, vmess:// …), and sing-box, Clash and Xray configs: see what run can read.

  1. Put your subscription link (or your config links, one per line) in a file:

    echo 'https://example.com/your-subscription-link' > /etc/hiddify-core/links.txt

  2. Tell the service to use this file, and restart it:

    uci set hiddify-core.main.conffile='/etc/hiddify-core/links.txt'
uci commit hiddify-core
/etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart

docs.title: Step 3: check that it works
docs.text:
• The service log:

    logread -e hiddify-core

  • On a phone or computer connected to the router, open a site that shows your IP address. It should show the IP of your proxy server, not your own.

docs.title: Router mode and proxy mode
docs.text:
The service has two modes, set in /etc/config/hiddify-core (option mode):

  • router (the default): every device behind the router goes through Hiddify Core, for TCP, UDP and ping, with nothing to set up on the devices. Connections from outside still reach the router and its port forwards. See Free internet for every device behind the router.
  • proxy: only a local HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy runs on the router itself, at 127.0.0.1:12334.

To change the mode:

uci set hiddify-core.main.mode='proxy'
uci commit hiddify-core
/etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart

docs.title: Manage the service
docs.text:
You want to Command Stop or start it /etc/init.d/hiddify-core stop / start Restart it after a change /etc/init.d/hiddify-core restart Turn it off at boot /etc/init.d/hiddify-core disable See the log logread -e hiddify-core Update to the newest version run the installer of step 1 again Remove it apk del hiddify-core (or opkg remove hiddify-core)

The package keeps its settings when you upgrade OpenWrt itself (sysupgrade). Every option of Hiddify Core is explained in Hiddify Core and the command-line reference.

docs.title: How to use UDP Turn Relay
docs.text:
Not supported in Hiddify app 4 and later

The relay= parameter described here works only in the old Hiddify app 2.x (Hiddify Next). Since version 4.0 (February 2026), when the app's core moved to sing-box 1.13, the parameter is ignored, and it is still ignored in Hiddify app 5.9: a link with relay= connects directly to the server, without the relay. This page is kept for reference.

docs.title: What it was
docs.text:
UDP Turn Relay uses the TURN server of a messenger as a relay. TURN servers carry the voice and video calls of messengers. When a messenger works inside a filtered network (a domestic messenger, or a foreign one that is not blocked), its TURN server can pass your traffic on to your own server. The connection looked like this:

It worked only with configs that run over UDP, such as Hysteria2 and TUIC v5. It did not work with Reality or other TCP configs.

docs.title: The link format
docs.text:
The relay was added to the end of a Hysteria2 or TUIC link as a URL-encoded relay parameter:

relay=urlencoded(turn://user:pass@host:port?realm=realm)
  • user and pass: the username and password of the messenger's TURN server.
  • host and port: the address of the TURN server.
  • realm: the TURN realm (the authentication area) of the server.

For example, turn://user:pass@turn.example.com:443?realm=example.com URL-encoded is:

relay=turn%3A%2F%2Fuser%3Apass%40turn.example.com%3A443%3Frealm%3Dexample.com

It goes before the # of the link, after an &:

hysteria2://password@server.example.com:443?obfs=salamander&obfs-password=secret&sni=www.speedtest.net&insecure=1&relay=turn%3A%2F%2Fuser%3Apass%40turn.example.com%3A443%3Frealm%3Dexample.com#test

Messengers close their TURN servers to this kind of use quickly: the one used in the first examples (Bale) did so within a short time.

docs.title: What to use instead
docs.text: To reach your server through another path with the current app, see Chain, Extra security and Proxy unblocker (WARP or Psiphon before or after your server) and, on the server side, relay servers.

docs.title: Related articles
docs.text: How to use the Hiddify appHow to install the Hiddify app

docs.title: How to use WARP in the Hiddify app
docs.text:
This page explains how to use Cloudflare WARP in Hiddify app: the easy ways (a free profile, or one choice in the settings) and the advanced way (writing your own warp:// config). Use it if you want a free connection, or if you want to hide your proxy traffic behind WARP.

WARP is a free VPN service from Cloudflare. It is based on WireGuard, a fast and simple VPN protocol. Hiddify app creates a WARP account for you and can add "noise" (extra fake packets) so that WARP traffic is harder for filters to detect and block.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.6). Older versions had a separate WARP page in the settings, with a Detour mode; in the current versions WARP is part of Chain, described below.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Hiddify app: see How to install the Hiddify app.
  • For the advanced way, you should already know how to add a profile: see How to use the Hiddify app.

docs.title: The easy way: the free WARP profile
docs.text:
1. On the Home page, tap +.
  2. Turn on the Free switch at the bottom of the panel and tap WARP & Psiphon.
  3. A window called WARP & Psiphon explains the profile. Tap Continue. The profile is added.
  4. Tap the big connect button. The first time, Android asks to allow notifications and the VPN connection; allow both.

This profile has several WARP connections (WireGuard, MASQUE and AmneziaWG, and WARP in WARP) and Psiphon, and picks one that works for you (balance · Round robin). See Add a free profile.

docs.title: Use WARP together with your own proxy (Chain)
docs.text:
You can put WARP in front of or behind your own profile:

  1. On the Home page, tap Quick settings at the bottom of the screen. (The same options are in Settings > Chain.)
  2. Choose one of these and set it to WARP:
    • Extra security ("When you don't trust the proxy"): you connect to your proxy first and then to WARP. Websites see a Cloudflare IP instead of your proxy's IP, and your proxy provider can't see your traffic.
    • Proxy unblocker ("Gets the proxy past filtering"): your proxy server is reached through WARP. Use this if your proxy server's IP is blocked. It is useful for a personal proxy, not for public ones.
  3. The first time, read the Cloudflare WARP consent message and tap Agree.
  4. Connect as usual. When it works, the connect button turns green.

Leave the one you don't need on Off (in the list it is called Turn off): each layer makes the connection a little slower.

The last picture shows Proxy unblocker set to WARP; its subtitle then reads "A filtered proxy may connect".

docs.title: WARP options
docs.text:
Open Settings > Chain (in the list it reads Chain / Extra security & unblocker). The page shows the layers in order: App → Extra security → your main profile → Unblocker. (On this page Proxy unblocker is called Unblocker.) Under the layer that uses WARP you find its options:

  • Tunnel: how the app talks to WARP: Auto (default), WireGuard, AmneziaWG or MASQUE.
  • License key: a WARP+ key, if you have one.
  • MTU: leave it on Auto unless you know you need another value.

The Proxy unblocker layer has more options, because it has to get past the filter:

  • Endpoint: which Cloudflare address to connect to: Assigned by Cloudflare, Scan (default: the app looks for an address that works on your network; its settings are under Scanner) or Custom (your own clean IP and port).
  • WireGuard noise: Noise count, Noise mode, Noise size and Noise delay. They work like the ifp, ifpm, ifps and ifpd parameters explained below.
  • MASQUE and AmneziaWG: options for those two tunnels.

Quick test

To try a ready-made WARP profile, open hiddify.com/warp on a device that has Hiddify app and tap the link there.

docs.title: The advanced way: write your own WARP config
docs.text:
Note

The warp:// link still works in 5.9.6. Add it with Clipboard; the Manually form only takes http(s) subscription links and says "Invalid URL" for a warp:// link.

You can build a warp:// link yourself and add it to the app like any other config (copy it, then tap + and Clipboard). The parts of the link are explained below.

docs.title: Noise modes (ifpm)
docs.text:
Noise is a few fake packets that the app sends just before WARP's handshake, so that the start of the connection does not look like WireGuard. ifpm sets what these packets look like. These are the same choices as Noise mode in the app's Chain settings:

ifpm In the app What the fake packets look like (not set) Auto With Endpoint set to Scan, the scanner finds the noise that gets through on your network. m4 Standard Random bytes after a short header. This is the core's own packet. random Random Only random bytes, with no header (like Xray's noise). quic QUIC (HTTPS) Real QUIC Initial packets, like the start of a visit to an HTTPS/3 site. quic-mimic QUIC handshake A copy of a real QUIC handshake. dns DNS (google.com) DNS questions about google.com. dns-cloudflare DNS (cloudflare.com) DNS questions about cloudflare.com. sip SIP (VoIP call) The start of an internet phone call. stun STUN (video call) The packets a video call sends first.

Tip

Start with m4 (Standard). If WARP does not connect on your network, try quic, dns or sip. Older articles mention the modes m1 to m6 and h…/g…: the current versions treat these like Standard.

docs.title: Number, size and delay of noise packets
docs.text:
Each of these is a range (min-max). Each time, the app picks a random value inside the range.

  • ifp: how many noise packets to send. For example, ifp=40-80 sends between 40 and 80 noise packets.
  • ifps: the size of each noise packet, in bytes. For example, ifps=40-100 makes each packet between 40 and 100 bytes.
  • ifpd: the delay between noise packets, in milliseconds. For example, ifpd=4-8 waits between 4 and 8 ms. Smaller delays usually work better.

docs.title: Which Cloudflare IP to use
docs.text:
• auto4: Cloudflare gives the config an IPv4 address automatically.
  • auto6: Cloudflare gives the config an IPv6 address automatically.
  • auto: Cloudflare can give either an IPv4 or an IPv6 address.
  • A clean IPv4 address: type it directly. For example: 188.114.97.170
  • A clean IPv6 address: put it inside []. For example: [2a01:4ef:f0:10a5::1]

A clean IP is a Cloudflare IP address that is not blocked on your network.

Tip

You can find clean IPs with a scanner, for example: CFScanner, Quick WARP on WARP, Ptechgithub WARP. These are community tools, not made by Hiddify.

docs.title: Name of the config
docs.text:
To give the config a name, add # and the name at the end. The name must be one word (no spaces). For example:

warp://auto#NAME

docs.title: WARP in WARP (WoW)
docs.text:
You can chain two WARP connections: you connect to the first WARP, and from there to the second one. Websites then see the IP of the second WARP. Add &&detour= after the first WARP config, followed by the second one. For example:

warp://auto&&detour=warp://auto

docs.title: Putting it all together
docs.text:
The general form of a WARP config is:

warp://License@IP:port?ifp=n1-n2&ifps=s1-s2&ifpd=d1-d2&ifpm=mode#name

Example:

warp://auto?ifp=40-80&ifps=40-100&ifpd=4-8&ifpm=m4#m4

This adds a WARP config named m4 to the app.

You can also chain two WARPs. For example:

warp://auto?ifp=40-80&ifps=40-100&ifpd=4-8&ifpm=m4#m4&&detour=warp://188.114.97.170:894?ifp=40-80&ifps=40-100&ifpd=4-8&ifpm=quic#quic

This adds a config named m4 that goes through a second WARP (WARP in WARP) named quic.

For more examples, see the official sample files warp and warp2.

Final tips

  • Use one of the scanners above to find a clean IP that works on your network, then build your config with the formula above.
  • If it does not connect, change the ranges (ifp, ifps, ifpd) or try another mode, and test again.
