docs.title: Import, export and reset settings, and edit a profile in the Hiddify app
Import, export and reset settings, and edit a profile
docs.text:
This page shows how to save all your Hiddify app settings to a file (to move them to another device, or to keep a copy), how to bring them back or reset them, and how to edit a profile.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). The screenshots come from Android; the menus are the same on every platform.

docs.title: Export your settings
docs.text:
Open Settings and tap ⋮ at the top, then Export.

  1. Copy anonymous options to clipboard
  2. Export anonymous options to file
  3. Copy all options to clipboard
  4. Export all options to file
  5. Reset options: puts every setting back to its default (profiles are not touched).

Anonymous options are all your settings without your private ones: the WARP+ license keys of the chain (Extra security and Unblocker) and the local network sharing password. Use them when you share your settings with someone, or attach them to a question in a support group. All options include those too: use them only for your own devices.

The file is JSON. It holds the app's settings, not your profiles: add your profiles on the new device separately (or share them, see below).

Tip

HiddifyCli can run with these settings: export all options to file and pass the file with -d.

docs.title: Import settings
docs.text: Settings → ⋮ → Import → Import options from clipboard or Import options from file. The app asks first: importing overwrites all your settings with the imported values.

docs.title: Edit a profile
docs.text:
On the Home page, tap the profile card (or View all profiles), then ⋮ next to a profile:

  • Pin: keeps it at the top of the list.
  • Update: downloads the latest servers of the subscription now.
  • Share (1): as a QR code or subscription link, the full configuration (JSON, your settings included), or Send to TV (see Hiddify on Android TV).
  • Edit (2): opens the profile page below.
  • Delete: removes it (you can't undo this).

  1. Name: the name shown in the app.
  2. URL: the subscription link the profile updates from.
  3. Turn off auto update: stops automatic updates of this profile.
  4. Auto update interval: how often it updates (for example every 12 hours).
  5. Config Editor: the profile's configuration, as a tree or as text, with search. Change it only if you know the config format; a wrong edit can stop the profile from connecting.

Tap Save at the top to keep your changes.

On computers, the profile page also has Administrator permission (Ask each time, Always use administrator permission or Always continue without administrator permission): see Hiddify on desktop.

The profiles list (Home → profile card) also has Sort (alphabetically or by last update) and Update subscriptions (all at once). Subscriptions that have expired, ran out of traffic or keep failing to update can be removed together with Remove inactive subscriptions.

docs.title: Logs and reporting a problem in the Hiddify app
Logs and reporting a problem in the Hiddify app
docs.text:
When something does not work, the logs say why. This page shows where they are, how to save them, and how to send a report to the Hiddify developers without your servers or passwords in it.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). The screenshots come from Android. On computers the Logs page is in the sidebar.

docs.title: The Logs page
docs.text:
Open Settings → Logs.

  1. Buffer: how many lines are kept on the page.
  2. Pause, clear and share the logs.
  3. Full report: makes a report for the developers (see below).
  4. Category and Level filter the lines; the Filter box above searches them.
  5. Core level: how much the core writes. It takes effect after you reconnect; set it to debug only while you look for a problem.

The share button saves or sends the logs:

  1. Recent logs: what you see on the page.
  2. App and core log: errors from both, across runs.
  3. Core log: everything the core recorded.
  4. Diagnostics report: crash reports, logs, the connection state and your settings, without servers or passwords, in one file.

If the core crashed, a Core crash item also appears: what the core was doing when it last crashed.

Warning

The Recent logs, App and core log and Core log files can contain your server addresses. Look at them before you post them anywhere public. The Diagnostics report and Full report remove servers, keys and passwords.

docs.title: Report a problem
docs.text:
Open Settings → About → Report a problem, or Full report on the Logs page.

The report holds the logs, the app and connection state and your settings, with servers, keys and passwords removed, as one zip file you can look at before sending.

  1. What happened? (optional): what you did, what you expected, what you saw instead.
  2. Send to Hiddify: the app encrypts the report and uploads it itself. Only the Hiddify team can open it.
  3. Send on Telegram: to the support bot. Private: only the Hiddify support team sees it.
  4. Send by email: to the Hiddify team. Private.
  5. Open a GitHub issue: public, anyone can read the issue and download the file.

For Telegram, email and GitHub, the app first saves the report, then shows the steps: open the bot, mail or GitHub page, attach the file and send it.

docs.title: After a crash
docs.text: If the app crashed the last time, it asks at the next start: Hiddify crashed last time, with the same ways to send a report. Sending it helps the developers fix the crash.

docs.title: Router mode of the Hiddify app on Linux
Router mode on Linux: Hiddify for your whole network
docs.text:
Router mode turns a Linux computer that routes a network (a gateway, a mini PC between your modem and your Wi-Fi, a Raspberry Pi-like box) into a transparent proxy for every device behind it. Phones, TVs, consoles and IoT devices all go through Hiddify with no app and no settings on them.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

Router mode is new in Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2) and exists only on Linux. On a router with OpenWrt, use Hiddify Core on OpenWrt instead; on a Linux server with no screen, see the core's router mode.

docs.title: What it covers
docs.text:
• TCP, UDP and ICMP of the devices behind the gateway: web, DNS, QUIC, games, calls and ping.
  • DNS on port 53 is answered by Hiddify, so names are not resolved by your ISP.
  • Connections from outside keep working: SSH or the web page of the gateway itself, a VPN server on it, and port forwards to a device behind it.
  • The gateway's own networks and private addresses stay direct, so the devices still reach the gateway and each other.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Linux computer that already routes your network (the other devices use it as their gateway).
  • nftables support in the kernel (standard on current Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora; the nft command itself is not needed) and the nfqueue kernel module, nfnetlink_queue (Hiddify loads it when modprobe is there).
  • /dev/net/tun, and administrator (root) permission.

If the nfqueue module is missing, router mode does not start and says so: router mode needs nftables and the nfqueue kernel module .... The message is in Logs.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
1. Install the Hiddify app on the Linux gateway and add your profile.

  2. Open Settings → Inbound → Service mode and choose Router (whole network). You can also switch it from Quick settings or the tray menu (Router).

    In Quick settings at the bottom of the home page, it is the last of the four buttons: Proxy, System proxy, VPN, Router.

  3. Connect. Like VPN mode, it asks once for administrator permission. When it is connected, the home page shows Connected as usual, and every device behind the gateway now goes through Hiddify.

When it starts, router mode turns on IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding if they are off, and puts forwarding back as it was when you disconnect.

Warning

Every device behind the gateway now goes through your proxy. Keep Bypass LAN on, and send local services direct with routing rules if needed.

docs.title: Routing in the Hiddify app: per-app routing, regions and your own rules
docs.text:
Routing decides which traffic goes through the proxy, which goes straight to the internet (direct), and which is blocked. This page explains every option of Settings → Routing.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.2). The screenshots come from Android. App-based routing is on Android only; the rest is the same on every platform.

docs.title: Open the routing settings
docs.text:
Open Settings and tap Routing.

  1. Region: the country you are in. It decides which sites go direct (the built-in rule Sites in …) and which apps the auto selection picks. Choices: Iran, China, Russia, Afghanistan, Indonesia, Türkiye, Brazil and Other.
  2. App-based routing (Android): choose apps that skip the VPN, or the only apps that use it.
  3. Balancer strategy: how traffic is spread when your profile has several servers.
  4. Default proxy: which server is used until you pick one yourself.
  5. IPv6: whether IPv6 is used at all.
  6. Add rule (the + button): make your own rule.

docs.title: App-based routing (Android)
docs.text:
Turn on App-based routing, then pick a mode:

  • Bypass: the apps you choose do not use the VPN. Everything else does. Good for banking apps and local apps that refuse foreign IPs.
  • Proxy only: only the apps you choose use the VPN. Everything else goes direct.

Tap Choose apps to pick the apps. Hide system apps keeps the list short, and the search button finds an app by its name.

Auto selection based on (your region) adds a ready list of apps for your region to the list of the current mode by itself (for Bypass: apps that usually need to stay direct, such as local banking apps), and keeps it up to date. Apps you removed by hand stay removed. Tap the refresh button next to it (Update now) to update the list at once. Apps added this way have an Auto tag. The ⋮ menu of the app list can import, export or clear your selection.

Tip

An app that is not in the VPN does not follow any routing rule (the app list shows Outside the VPN · rule won't apply).

docs.title: Per-app routing on computers (Windows, macOS, Linux)
docs.text:
On a computer there is no app list to tick. You choose apps with a routing rule, by the name of their program file. This works only in VPN mode (the editor shows Available only in TUN mode).

  1. Open Settings → Routing and click + (Add rule).
  2. Set Outbound if match: Direct to keep the app outside the VPN (for example a game or a local banking program), Proxy to send it through the VPN, or Block.
  3. Click Process names, then +, type the program's file name and click OK. On Windows it ends in .exe, for example chrome.exe or Telegram.exe; on Linux and macOS it is the program's name, for example firefox. Add as many names as you need.
  4. Click the ✓ at the top to save the rule.

How do I find the file name?

On Windows, open Task Manager, right-click the app and choose Go to details: the highlighted name (for example chrome.exe) is the one to type. Process paths does the same with the full path, for example C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe, when two programs have the same name. Package names is for Android only.

Microsoft Store apps, and why not .msi
  • Type the name of the program that runs, not of the file you installed it with. An .msi file, or an .exe you downloaded to install, is only the installer. For example, Bing Wallpaper installs with BingWallpaper.exe, but the program that runs is BingWallpaperApp.exe. The rule only accepts names ending in .exe (or .bat, .cmd, .com).
  • Apps from the Microsoft Store work the same way: open the app, then find its name in Task Manager → Go to details. Or open PowerShell, run tasklist /apps, and look for the app in the list; the .exe name is in the first column.
  • Some apps run more than one program; add every name you see.
  • For Store apps, use Process names, not Process paths: they live in C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\… in a folder whose name has the version number in it, so the path changes with every update.
  • Some Store apps download in the background through Windows itself (for example svchost.exe); that part does not carry the app's name and is not caught by the rule.

docs.title: Balancer strategy
docs.text:
When the app balances traffic over several servers, it chooses a server for each connection:

  • Round robin: each connection uses the next server, so sites may see your IP change.
  • Consistent hash: each site always uses the same server.
  • Sticky session: each site keeps a random server until you reconnect.

If sites log you out or ask for a captcha again and again, try Consistent hash or Sticky session.

docs.title: Default proxy
docs.text:
Until you choose a server on the proxies page, the app uses:

  • Lowest ping: the fastest one.
  • Balance: connections are spread over all of them (with the balancer strategy above).
  • First proxy: the profile's first server.

docs.title: Resolve destination and IPv6
docs.text:
• Resolve destination: the app finds the IP address of each site before it sends the traffic. Leave it off unless you know you need it.
  • IPv6: Off (IPv4 only) is the default, because most proxies have no IPv6 at their exit, and a connection the proxy cannot carry breaks sites like Google and YouTube. On, IPv4 first and On, IPv6 first use IPv6 only through a proxy that was tested to carry it. IPv6 always stays inside the VPN. Tap the ⓘ next to IPv6 for the full explanation.

docs.title: Built-in rules
docs.text:
Below the options is the list of rules. The app checks them from top to bottom, and the first rule that matches decides. Built-in rules have a lock icon; you can turn each one on or off:

  • Bypass LAN: your home network (router, printer, TV) stays direct.
  • Android services (on other platforms: Apple services, Microsoft services or Linux updates): system services go direct.
  • Ads and malware: blocked.
  • Sites in (your region): local sites go direct.

A built-in rule can't be changed. To change one, Duplicate it and edit the copy. Drag the handle (≡) to change the order.

docs.title: Add your own rule
docs.text:
Tap + (Add rule). A rule says which traffic (the conditions) and where it goes (Outbound if match).

  1. Name: a name for the rule.
  2. Outbound if match: Proxy, Direct, Direct with fragment (direct, with the TLS fragment trick) or Block.
  3. URLset: links to ready-made rule-set files (.srs or .json), each a long list of sites, for example a list of ad sites. This field is not for a site's address; see the warning below.
  4. Package names (Android, VPN mode only): apps by their package name. Process names and Process paths are the same on computers, for example chrome.exe or /usr/lib/chromium/chromium.

Further down you can also match Networks (TCP or UDP), Destination ports and Source ports (for example 443 or 1:65000), Protocol (TLS, HTTP, QUIC, STUN, DNS, BitTorrent), Destination IP CIDR and Source IP CIDR (for example 10.0.0.0/24), and sites by Domain, Domain suffix (for example .ir), Domain keyword or Domain regex. Fill in only what you need; a rule matches when all the filled fields match. Tap the ✓ at the top to save.

Example: send every .ir site direct

Add a rule, set Outbound if match to Direct, and under Domain suffix add .ir.

Don't put a site's address in URLset

URLset downloads a rule-set file from the link you give it. A site's address such as https://github.com is a web page, not a rule-set file, so the whole rule stops working: the site is not blocked, even if the domain fields are filled in correctly. To pick a site, use Domain suffix (next section), and keep URLset empty.

Where do I get a URLset link?

URLset takes the raw link of a rule-set file. It starts with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ and ends in .srs (or .json). The app downloads the file through the VPN and refreshes it every few days.

Hiddify's own lists are in the hiddify-geo repository, branch rule-set. The app's built-in rules use them too:

  • block/: ads, malware, phishing and crypto miners.
  • country/: the sites (geosite-…) and IP addresses (geoip-…) of Iran, China, Russia, Turkey, Afghanistan, Brazil and Indonesia.

For example, every Iranian site:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hiddify/hiddify-geo/rule-set/country/geosite-ir.srs

To get the link of another file, open it on GitHub, tap View raw (or Raw) and copy the address of the page that opens.

You don't need this list to open Iranian sites directly: the built-in Sites in (your region) rule already does that.

Other rule-set files in sing-box format work too. If you find a list you trust somewhere else, test it before you rely on it: with a wrong link, the whole rule stops working.

docs.title: Step by step: block a site, or send it direct or through the proxy
docs.text:
Here we block GitHub as an example. The steps are the same for any site; only step 3 changes:

  • Block: the site does not open at all.
  • Direct: the site opens without the VPN, for example a banking site that does not open from abroad.
  • Proxy: the site always goes through the VPN, even if a rule lower in the list (for example "Sites in your region") would send it direct.

The steps:

  1. In Settings → Routing, scroll down to the rules and tap +.

  2. Tap Name and write a name you will recognize, for example Block GitHub.

  3. Tap Outbound if match and choose Block (or Direct or Proxy).

    1. Scroll down and tap Domain suffix, then +. Write only the site's name, github.com: no https://, no www, no / at the end. Tap OK, then the back arrow.

    2. Tap the ✓ at the top to save. The new rule appears at the top of the list, switched on.

    3. Test it: close the browser completely and open the site again. You don't need to disconnect; the app applies the rule right away. A blocked site shows an error like this:

    Which domain field should you use?

    • Domain suffix github.com: the site and all its subdomains (github.com, docs.github.com, api.github.com). This is the right choice almost always.
    • Domain github.com: only this exact address; docs.github.com still opens.
    • Domain keyword github: every address that contains the word, for example githubusercontent.com too.

    You can put several sites in one rule: add each one as a separate line.

    If it does not work

    • URLset of the rule must be empty (see the warning above).
    • The ✓ is grey when there is nothing new to save. If you changed something and the ✓ is still grey, go back and open the rule again to check that your values are there.
    • Rules are checked from top to bottom; if another rule above yours matches the site first, move yours higher with the handle (≡).
    • In versions before 5.9.9, Domain suffix accepts only endings like .com. Update the app, or use Domain github.com together with Domain keyword github.

    The ⋮ menu of the Routing page can Import rules from the clipboard or a file, Copy rules or Save rules to file (to move them to another device), and Reset to default rules.

    Warning

    Only import rules from a source you trust: rules decide where your traffic goes.

docs.title: Share your Hiddify connection (local proxy and network sharing)
Share your connection: local proxy and local network sharing
docs.text:
Besides the VPN, the Hiddify app opens a local proxy that other apps on the same device can use, and it can share the connection with other devices on your home Wi-Fi: a laptop, a TV, a game console. These options are in Settings → Inbound.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

This page is for Hiddify app 5.9 (5.9.6). Each picture has a Phone and a Computer tab; the options are the same, computers have a few extra ports.

docs.title: Turn sharing on quickly
docs.text:
On the Home page, open Quick settings and turn on Connection sharing. It is the same switch as Share on local network below.

On a computer (the phone looks the same):

docs.title: The Inbound page
docs.text:
Open Settings → Inbound.

PhoneComputer

At the top:

  • Service mode: VPN (every app goes through Hiddify) or Proxy (only apps set to use the proxy; on computers also Set system proxy, and on Linux Router). See Hiddify on desktop.
  • Strict route and TUN implementation: technical VPN options. Leave them as they are.

Under Local proxy:

  1. Proxy port (SOCKS5/4, HTTP): the local proxy, on port 12334 by default. One port serves SOCKS5, SOCKS4 and HTTP. In VPN mode it is closed (closed in VPN mode), because apps already use the VPN.
  2. Keep open in VPN mode: keeps the local proxy open in VPN mode too, for apps set to use a proxy.
  3. Require password: apps must send a user name and password. Some apps, such as browsers, can't send a SOCKS password.

When you switch to Proxy mode (in Quick settings), the app shows how to point an app at the local proxy: This device lists the steps, the Server (127.0.0.1) and Port, and whether a password is set (Set password). The same window opens from the Proxy mode · how to use hint on the Home page.

PhoneComputer

Under Local network sharing:

  1. Share on local network: other devices on your network can use the proxy.
  2. Sharing port: the port for other devices, 12338 by default.
PhoneComputer

Proxy secret (3) is the password of the proxy. Tap the eye to see it, or Generate new for a new one. Without a secret, any app on this device, and any device on the network while you share, can use the proxy.

Warning

Keep a proxy secret while you share on a network you don't control (a café, an office). Anyone on that network could otherwise use your connection.

docs.title: Use the shared connection on another device
docs.text:
1. Keep Hiddify connected on the sharing device, and put both devices on the same Wi-Fi.

  2. On the sharing device, open the values to enter: switch Quick settings to Proxy (the window opens by itself the first time), or tap the Proxy mode · how to use hint on the Home page. This device shows the values for apps on the same device; Other devices shows the IP, port, user name (hiddify by default) and password for the network, with a QR code (SOCKS5 · same network only) and a Turn on sharing button if sharing is off. Tap a value to copy it, or use Copy link or the Telegram link.

    PhoneComputer

  3. On the other device, open the app's or system's proxy settings, choose SOCKS5 (or HTTP), and enter the IP of the sharing device, the sharing port and, if set, the user name and password.

Tip

Telegram has its own proxy setting: the Telegram link fills it in for you.

docs.title: URL scheme and subscription format of the Hiddify app
docs.text:
This page is for people who make subscription links, panels or bots for the Hiddify app: the links that open the app, what a subscription may contain, and the headers and link parameters the app reads.

Written for Hiddify app 5.9

Everything on this page was checked against the code of Hiddify app 5.9.2 and the Hiddify Core it ships with.

docs.title: Links that open the app
docs.text:
When the Hiddify app is installed, a link of this form opens the app and asks the user to add the profile:

hiddify://import/<link>#<name>
  • <link> is a subscription link (in any format the app reads, see below) or a single proxy link such as vless://….
  • #<name> (optional) is the profile name. The app asks the user before it adds a profile from an external link.

Examples:

hiddify://import/https://example.com/sub/abc123#My VPN
hiddify://import/trojan://password@example.com:443?security=tls&type=ws&path=%2Fws#Server 1

docs.title: Other forms the app understands
docs.text:
These forms are read when the user adds them in the app (from the clipboard or with Add profile › Manually). As a link that opens the app, use hiddify://import/… above.

hiddify://install-sub?url=<URL-encoded link>#<name>
hiddify://install-config?url=<URL-encoded link>#<name>
hiddify://install-proxy?url=<URL-encoded link>#<name>
v2ray://install-config?url=<URL-encoded link>&name=<name>
clash://install-config?url=<URL-encoded link>&name=<name>
sing-box://import-remote-profile?url=<URL-encoded link>#<name>

The schemes hiddify, v2ray, v2rayn, v2rayng, clash, clashmeta and sing-box all work with a url= parameter. A name= parameter, when given, is used instead of the #name part. A plain https://… link may also carry ?name=….

docs.title: Sharing routing rules
docs.text:
In Settings › Routing, the ⋮ menu has Copy rules to clipboard. It copies a link of this form:

hiddify:///settings/routing-options?routeRule=<base64 of the rules as JSON>

Opening it on another device opens Routing and, after a warning ("Import route rule?"), adds the rules.

docs.title: What a subscription may contain
docs.text:
The content of a subscription link (or of a file the user imports) can be:

  • Share links, one per line, plain or as one base64 block. The core reads: vless, vmess, trojan, ss, ssconf, tuic, hysteria, hysteria2 (hy2), ssh, naive (naive+https, naive+quic), anytls, snell, mieru (mierus), socks, http/https (also phttp/phttps), wg/wireguard/awg, warp, psiphon, tor, ovpn, dnstt, dnst, masterdns, soar, slipnet, masque, aether and direct. The x prefix (xvless://, xvmess://, xtrojan://) runs a link with the Xray core, and the s prefix (svless://, …) with sing-box.
  • A sing-box JSON config, a Clash / mihomo YAML config, an Xray JSON config, a WireGuard .conf file or an OpenVPN .ovpn file.
  • Other subscription links: a line with an http(s):// address that has a path is downloaded, and its content takes the place of the line. A line that fails to download is dropped.

Example of share links:

#profile-title: My VPN
vless://11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555@example.com:443?security=tls&sni=example.com&type=ws&path=%2Fws#WebSocket TLS
hysteria2://password@example.com:443?sni=example.com&obfs=salamander&obfs-password=secret#Hysteria2
tuic://11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555:password@example.com:443?alpn=h3&congestion_control=bbr&sni=example.com#TUIC

docs.title: Profile name
docs.text:
The app uses the first of these that is not empty:

  1. A name the user typed when editing the profile.
  2. The profile-title header.
  3. The file name in the content-disposition header.
  4. The #name part of the subscription link.
  5. The last part of the link, without .json, .yaml, .yml or .txt.
  6. "Remote Profile".

docs.title: Subscription headers
docs.text:
The server can send these HTTP response headers with the subscription. If you can't set headers (for example a file on GitHub), put them as comments in the first 10 lines of the content, starting with # or //:

#profile-title: base64:SSDinaTvuI8gSGlkZGlmeQ==
#profile-update-interval: 12
#subscription-userinfo: upload=455727941; download=6174315083; total=1073741824000; expire=1767225600
#support-url: https://t.me/hiddify
#profile-web-page-url: https://hiddify.com

A real HTTP header wins over the same header in the content. The app reads only these headers:

Header Value What the app does profile-title text, or base64: + UTF-8 text in base64 The profile name. Use base64 for emoji or non-Latin names: base64:SSDinaTvuI8gSGlkZGlmeQ== shows "I ❤️ Hiddify". content-disposition attachment; filename="name.txt" or filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded> The profile name, when there is no profile-title. profile-update-interval hours, a whole number above 0 How often the app updates the profile, unless the user changed it. subscription-userinfo upload=…; download=…; total=…; expire=… Shows the used and total traffic (bytes) and the days left (expire is a Unix time in seconds). total=0 or no total means unlimited; expire=0 or no expire means no expiry. profile-web-page-url a URL Shows a button that opens your web page (for example the user page). support-url a URL Shows a support button. ipinfo-url a URL The address the app uses to show the exit IP and its country. extra-security psiphon or warp Turns on Extra security through Psiphon or WARP for this profile. The user's own choice in the app wins. fragment size,sleep,method or tlshello,size,sleep Turns on TLS fragment for this profile, read like the link parameter below. The user's own setting wins. keep-top a number, or -1 How many of the fastest proxies the app keeps running (default 5). -1 keeps all. The user's own choice wins.

Not read any more

moved-permanently-to and DNS were read by older versions. Hiddify app 5.9 ignores them.

docs.title: Link parameters
docs.text: Besides the usual parameters of each protocol, Hiddify reads these in a share link. Parameter names don't care about case, _ or -: mux_type, mux-type and muxtype are the same.

docs.title: TLS fragment
docs.text:
&fragment=<size>,<sleep>,<method>
&fragment=tlshello,<size>,<sleep>

size is the size of each piece in bytes and sleep the pause between pieces in milliseconds, each a number or a range such as 10-100. All three parts are needed. Example: &fragment=10-100,100-200,tlshello. You can also give fgsize= and fgsleep= on their own. See How the TLS trick works.

docs.title: Other TLS tricks
docs.text:
• mc=1: mixed-case SNI (for example ExAmPle.com).
  • padsize=<range>: adds a padding extension of this many bytes before the SNI, for example padsize=100-200. It needs a browser fingerprint (fp=chrome or another).

docs.title: MUX
docs.text:
Parameter Meaning muxtype smux, yamux or h2mux. MUX is on only when this is set. muxmaxc the maximum number of connections muxsmax the maximum number of streams in one connection mux the minimum number of streams in one connection muxpad true to add padding (the server must use it too) muxup, muxdown upload and download speed in Mbps for TCP Brutal; both are needed

Example: &muxtype=h2mux&muxmaxc=4&muxpad=false&muxup=10&muxdown=50

Old parameter names

Older versions of this page wrote mux=smux, mux_max, mux_min, mux_up and mux_down. The app does not read those names: use the table above.

docs.title: One-Year Anniversary of Hiddify
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify was born in September 2022, after the internet in Iran was shut down. In its first year it went from a list of VPS providers and one-click server installs to a multi-user panel, the HiddifyNG and HiddifyN apps, and the first version of a new cross-platform app. All of it was volunteer work.

docs.title: The Story of Hiddify…
docs.text:
Hello to all Hiddify supporters,

Around this time last year, we were all in shock, and everyone was trying to help in any way they could.

Many of our loved ones gave their lives, and their absence will always be felt in our hearts.

Many lost their eyesight, others were fired, some were imprisoned, and more…

All of this happened as part of protests for their natural rights.

These events will never be erased from our minds and will always bring pain to our hearts.

It was during these difficult days last year that we decided to do what we could by providing simple access to the internet, making it easier for the dear people of our country. That was the beginning of this project, and Hiddify was born during these very days.

In the first days, we tried to review various censorship methods and create a list of VPS providers.

After that, we created extremely easy and free installations for Microsoft Azure.

We expanded the project to other datacenters, including quick installations for Hetzner, Oracle Cloud, and OVH. The goal was for everyone to be able to set up their own server without any technical knowledge.

Then, we developed the initial version of the Hiddify server and tried to teach the activation process for the client in a simple way. We also worked to ensure that the server app was resistant to VPN detection bots, obtained valid certificates, set safety configurations, and applied appropriate settings.

As time passed and the internet situation remained dire, we worked harder to simplify complex concepts to make them accessible to everyone. Additionally, we made many articles and tutorial videos available so that everyone could perform complex configurations.

On the client side, existing apps were not as user-friendly as they should have been. Our parents, for example, couldn’t connect with them at all.

To address this, we first created custom versions of Hiddify Clash for Android and desktop to make the user connection process easier.

Gradually, your support for the project grew, and this provided extra motivation to add more features to the panel. We developed the multi-user version of the panel, redesigned many components, improved structures, and set up a support group on Telegram.

On the client side, after developing several versions of the Hiddify Clash app, many bugs in the Clash Meta core led us to seek an alternative solution.

After thoroughly reviewing and redesigning the entire client process based on performance tests, we decided to use the best market solutions. This led to the birth of the custom HiddifyNG and HiddifyN versions, which were warmly welcomed by you all.

For example, HiddifyNG was downloaded more than 100,000 times on Google Play and received a 4.8 out of 5 rating from you, which is incredible for an app less than five months old.

At the same time, on the server side, we added new protocols and introduced more features, including automatic CDN IP selection, simultaneous use of multiple domains, adding intermediate nodes, and many other features that cannot all be mentioned here.

docs.title: One-Year Anniversary of Hiddify
docs.text:
On our first anniversary:

On the client side, we introduced the cross-platform HiddifyNext app for Android, Windows, Linux, and Mac, and we will soon release it for iOS as well.

Our goal was to make it easy for developers to implement new protocols across all operating systems and to maintain integration across platforms.

The new app design is simple, performs efficiently, and uses minimal system resources. We will continue to add more exciting new features to it.

If you are a panel developer, read the app's URL scheme to see how to connect your panel to the app.

On the server side, in addition to previous protocols like Vless, Vmess, and Trojan, we introduced newer protocols such as Reality gRPC, WebSocket, H2, and SSH. In the panel’s beta version, protocols like Hysteria2 and TUICv5 with unified user management are now available and can easily be accessed in the beta version. They will be officially released soon.

If you would like to test the beta version and use the newer protocols, you can find out how to upgrade to the beta here. The next stable panel release will be the most bug-free and fastest version yet, so it will remain in beta for a longer period.

Everything that has been done so far has been spontaneous, voluntary, and without any financial gain. All the donations from you have gone toward the project and will continue to do so.

Through this difficult journey, we sincerely thank everyone who has helped us in any way to ensure that the dear people of our country remain connected to the free internet and can emerge from this absolute darkness.

We are also grateful to everyone who has fought for the internet for all.

To all of you who have continuously supported and stood by us on this journey, we are deeply thankful.

We hope for a day when no one is oppressed or controlled by authoritarian regimes.

#Women_Life_Freedom

Hiddify, for a free internet.

docs.title: Hiddify's Second Anniversary
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify was born on 23 September 2022, after the internet in Iran was shut down. In two years we went from a few server install guides to Hiddify Manager and the Hiddify app: more than half a million active installs on Google Play, more than 5.7 million app downloads from GitHub and more than 24,000 stars. This post walks through that road step by step.

docs.title: The Story of Hiddify: From Birth to Today
docs.text:
A detailed report to our dear supporters on what we did in these two years

It was around this time two years ago when we all found ourselves in a great shock, and everyone tried to help in any way they could. This was the beginning of our work.

These days remind us of a deep sorrow, a great grief that united us in pursuit of a right we all deserve.

About the version numbers

"HiddifyManager version 1 to 8" in this post are the versions of the Hiddify panel; the server package had its own numbers then (7 to 10). Some dates and features are a little different in the release history: for the exact details of each version, see its own post, from Hiddify Manager 1 to Hiddify Manager 8.

❤️ Freedom

Internet freedom, freedom of thought, political freedom, economic freedom, and freedom in all aspects of life.

We worked for internet freedom because we believed, and still do, that this freedom brings the other freedoms with it.

In late September 2022, after people's access to the free internet became even more restricted, we decided to do what we could: give simple access to the internet and make things easier for the people of our country. This was the start of the project, and Hiddify was born in those days.

docs.title: Starting after a great shock
docs.text: In the first days we wrote a review of censorship methods and a list of sites that sell VPS servers, and put them in the Awesome-Freedom repository, so that anyone with a little technical knowledge could buy a server and make their own VPN.

docs.title: The first tools
docs.text:
Then, in October of the same year, we made a very easy and free install on Microsoft Azure.

In November we extended the project to other data centers, with quick installs on Hetzner, Oracle Cloud, Vultr and OVH. The goal was that everyone could set up their own server without any technical knowledge.

docs.title: The first version of HiddifyManager
docs.text: In December 2022 we made the first version of HiddifyManager and tried to explain very simply how to turn it on in a client app. We also made HiddifyManager resist VPN detection bots, get a valid certificate, set safe settings, run suitable configs and give them to the user.

docs.title: More HiddifyManager, and the first guides
docs.text: As the disastrous internet situation went on, we kept making complex ideas simpler so everyone could use them. We also published many articles and video tutorials, so that even complex settings were possible for everyone.

docs.title: HiddifyClash, a simpler client
docs.text:
On the other side, the client apps of the time were not simple enough: our parents could not use them at all.

So, as a first step, in January 2023 we made custom versions of HiddifyClash for Android and desktop, to make connecting simpler.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 1
docs.text: Little by little more of you joined the project, and that gave us the energy to start the Telegram support group in February. We also added more to the panel, and in March 2023, after several early versions, HiddifyManager version 1 came out with many users and many domains; much was redesigned and the structure got better.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 2
docs.text:
Before Nowruz 2023 (March) we released HiddifyManager version 2, with new features such as:

  • a web app (PWA)
  • a tutorial video in the panel when you click ❓
  • choosing the ports of the protocols, renaming proxies, and fingerprints

During Nowruz we found out that the Xray developers had added us to their list of web panels. It felt very good, because they had found us themselves.

In the same days, with the help of our friends at IRCF, we added subscription links made automatically for the user's mobile operator to HiddifyManager 2, and the AutoCDN domain was born.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 3
docs.text:
In April we redesigned the panel, and HiddifyManager version 3 came out with a focus on stability, simplicity and beauty. In this version:

  • The dashboard was redesigned: processes and system resources in separate tiles, plus online users and usage.
  • Every page was redesigned, and a dark mode was added.
  • Search in the settings, and other visual improvements.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 4
docs.text:
We released HiddifyManager version 4 in May. Its most important feature was support for the new Reality protocol. It also added:

  • many admins with separate permissions
  • a Telegram bot connected to the panel
  • a dedicated domain for the subscription link
  • automatic domain setup in Cloudflare

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 5
docs.text:
Because you asked again and again for more protocols, we kept going, and HiddifyManager version 5 came out in the same month with:

  • the ShadowTLS v3 protocol
  • a new panel theme
  • a limit on how many users an admin or agent can make

docs.title: The HiddifyN and HiddifyNG apps
docs.text:
On the client side, after several versions of HiddifyClash, the many bugs of the Clash Meta core made us look for another way.

After we studied and redesigned the whole client side based on performance tests, we decided to build on the good apps already available. In April 2023 our custom HiddifyNG and HiddifyN were born, and you liked them a lot.

For example, HiddifyNG passed 100,000 downloads on Google Play alone in less than 5 months, with a rating of 4.8 out of 5, which is remarkable for such a young app.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 6
docs.text: On the server side, in May 2023, version 6 added fragment and WARP+ to HiddifyManager. With WARP the server's IP no longer leaked at the destination, and fragment, by cutting packets into pieces, made it easier to get past the filter. The sing-box core was added too, and HiddifyManager became the only panel that supported two cores, with accounting on both.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 7
docs.text:
In June, HiddifyManager version 7 came with more protocols and important features, such as:

  • many Reality and Worker domains
  • a redesigned "add domain" page
  • WARP version 2

docs.title: Version 7 of HiddifyN and HiddifyNG
docs.text: We kept developing the HiddifyNG and HiddifyN clients, added routing and load balancing, and released version 7 of these apps.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 8
docs.text:
Then, on the server side, next to the earlier protocols such as VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Reality, gRPC, WebSocket and H2, a friend helped us add the secure SSH protocol in HiddifyManager version 8, together with:

  • temporary short links, in the style of Inspector Gadget
  • a smart subscription link
  • a simpler way to turn the VPN on from the user page

docs.title: The start of the cross-platform Hiddify app
docs.text:
On our first birthday, on the client side, we started the cross-platform Hiddify app for Android, Windows, Linux and Mac, in October 2023.

Our goal was that developers could add new protocols to every operating system easily, and that all systems worked the same way.

The new app was very simple, fast, and light on the system.

docs.title: The Hiddify Reality Scanner
docs.text: Because of new limits on the Reality protocol, in November 2023 we made a scanner that finds, on any network, SNIs that work for a Reality domain, to get around those limits.

docs.title: The Hiddify app on Google Play
docs.text: With HiddifyManager in a good place, we decided to focus more on the Hiddify app: more protocols and features, and every platform, including iOS. Version 0.6 came with every protocol that worked, including Hysteria and TUIC, and it was published on Google Play.

docs.title: Hiddify app 0.12
docs.text:
Version 0.12 came out in December 2023 with new features, such as:

  • basic routing rules by region
  • a redesigned logs page
  • more selectors on the proxies page
  • the TLS Trick feature
  • BeePass support
  • D-Pad support on Android TV
  • support for China and Russia

docs.title: Hiddify app 0.13
docs.text:
With your GitHub issues and many requests, we went on, and version 0.13 came out in January 2024 with:

  • bypass LAN
  • sharing the VPN on the network
  • support for the new core
  • support for Afghanistan

docs.title: The Hiddify app on the Microsoft Store
docs.text: In February the app was officially published on the Microsoft Store, from version 0.16.7.

docs.title: HiddifyCli for systems without a desktop
docs.text: In March we released a version of the app without a graphical interface, with every feature, so that you can use it on servers and systems without a desktop.

docs.title: HiddifyManager version 10
docs.text:
With the new Hysteria 2 and TUIC 5 protocols and updates to the old ones, HiddifyManager version 10 came out in March 2024. It brought many basic changes, such as:

  • a move to an SQL database, and a much faster panel
  • more security, such as stronger authentication for proxies and the panel
  • a new, innovative user page

docs.title: The Hiddify app beta for iOS
docs.text: At the same time, after a lot of effort, we published the Hiddify app beta for iOS on Apple's TestFlight. This gave some of you access to the app on iOS, and we kept working to get it into the App Store.

docs.title: Hiddify app 1, for Nowruz 2024
docs.text:
Version 1 of the app came out with a Nowruz theme for the Persian New Year, with many new features:

  • WARP support
  • a VPN service on Windows and Mac
  • smart fragment
  • quick settings
  • failover for configs
  • WireGuard noise
  • a delay indicator under the connect button

docs.title: The Hiddify relay builder
docs.text:
In May 2024 we released one tool to build relay (tunnel) servers more easily, with the methods that work:

  • IP-Tables
  • GOST
  • Dokodemo-Door
  • HA-Proxy
  • Socat
  • WST

docs.title: Hiddify app 1.4
docs.text:
In June 2024 version 1.4 came out with new features, such as:

  • reserving WARP
  • syncing the WARP key with the app's own key
  • better fragment

docs.title: Hiddify app 1.5
docs.text:
We kept going, and version 1.5 came out with:

  • built-in routing with rule sets that update themselves
  • an option to remove ads from websites

docs.title: Hiddify app 2
docs.text:
In August we released version 2 of the app. Its most important features:

  • sing-box and Xray cores at the same time
  • the new generation of filter bypass, Split HTTP
  • both IPv4 and IPv6 for WireGuard
  • a config editor
  • more WARP modes

docs.title: An amazing record for the Hiddify app
docs.text: Less than a year after the first version of the Hiddify app, its active installs on Google Play passed half a million. The app was also downloaded more than 5.5 million times from GitHub. This was far beyond what we had imagined, and we owe it all to your support.

docs.title: At the end of the second year
docs.text:
At the end of our second year we had reached:

  • more than half a million active installs of the Hiddify app on Google Play
  • more than 5.7 million downloads of the Hiddify app from GitHub
  • more than 2 million downloads of HiddifyManager from GitHub
  • more than 24,000 stars for the Hiddify project on GitHub

And this is the road we took, in short:

docs.title: The start of the third year
docs.text:
Here is a short look at our plans.

In our third year we will keep walking this hard road, and push the Hiddify app and HiddifyManager forward with more strength.

docs.title: In the Hiddify app
docs.text:
• The iOS version will be in the App Store.
  • New features, such as extensions for the app.
  • Better fragment.
  • Versions for 32-bit systems and other systems such as routers.
  • New, trending protocols.
  • Adaptive routing.
  • A clean IP scanner.
  • And hundreds of other features you will see soon.

docs.title: In HiddifyManager
docs.text:
• A central panel, so you can manage many servers from one panel.
  • Extensions.
  • New, effective protocols.
  • And more features you will see.

docs.title: Last words
docs.text:
On this hard road, we thank from the bottom of our hearts everyone who helped in any way, so that the people of our country could stay connected to the free internet and get out of this total darkness.

We also thank everyone who worked to give access to the free internet.

And to all of you who were always with us and never left us alone on this road: thank you, more than words can say.

Here's to the day when no one is limited and controlled by totalitarian governments.

#Women_Life_Freedom

🕊️Hiddify, Internet Freedom Solution🕊️

In 30 seconds

Hiddify turned three on 23 September 2025. In its third year the Hiddify app reached the App Store, the Hiddify core got extensions, and Hiddify Manager became lighter and faster with Docker installs and version 11. This post looks back at year three, from the second anniversary to today.

docs.title: Year three in a few numbers
docs.text:

  • Hiddify app: version 2.5, and close to 500 commits for the next generation of the app. (GitHub)
  • Hiddify core: from version 3.0 to 3.2. (GitHub)

(23 September 2024 to 23 September 2025, from the GitHub releases and commits.)

docs.title: Hiddify app
docs.text:
• On the App Store (October 2024): the Hiddify app was approved and now installs on iPhone and iPad from Apple's official store too, next to Android, Windows, Linux and Mac.
  • Version 2.5 (September 2024): the last version of the 2.x line. After it, work began on the next generation of the app, which came out later as Hiddify app 4.

docs.title: Hiddify core
docs.text: • Extensions (September 2024): with core 3, developers can add new features and pages to the Hiddify app. The first extension was an IP scanner.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
• Version 10.80 (December 2024): Docker became a real way to install, WireGuard and Shadowsocks were added to the v2rayNG links, and installing got faster.
  • Version 11 (July 2025): XHTTP with separate upload and download domains, QUIC, a rebuilt proxy system, and up to half the memory use.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text:
Hiddify is made by a small team and many volunteers: people who translate the app, try the test versions, report problems and answer questions in the groups. Thank you all. Our goal is the same as on the first day: the open internet is a right for everyone.

How you can help:

  • Star the projects on GitHub and rate the app in the stores.
  • Tell a friend and share our guides.
  • Report problems from inside the app or on GitHub.
  • If you can, support us.

docs.title: Hiddify turns four
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify started on 23 September 2022, when the internet in Iran was shut down. Four years later, the Hiddify app is at version 5 and Hiddify Manager at version 14, both still free, open source and without ads. This post looks back at the last two years, since our second anniversary.

docs.title: Two years in numbers
docs.text:
• Hiddify app: from version 2.5 to 5. More than 34,000 stars on GitHub.
  • Hiddify Manager: from version 10 to 14, four big releases. More than 9,600 stars on GitHub.
  • One shared engine, hiddify-core, under both.

(Star counts checked on 16 November 2026.)

docs.title: What the Hiddify app learned
docs.text:
• No server? No problem. Free profiles with WARP and Psiphon connect without a subscription link (version 4).
  • Chain (version 5): Extra security and Proxy unblocker put WARP or Psiphon in front of or behind your own proxy with one choice.
  • One connection for the whole home: share your connection with a computer or a TV, and send a profile to Android TV from your phone.
  • Routing that thinks for you: the app picks which apps go through the proxy (Routing).

docs.title: What Hiddify Manager learned
docs.text:
• Version 11 (July 2025): XHTTP and separate upload and download domains.
  • Version 12 (February 2026): Mieru, Naive, HTTP/2, ECH and a Telegram proxy that counts traffic.
  • Version 13 (September 2026): many servers from one panel, DNS tunnels for heavy filtering, a new dashboard.
  • Version 14 (October 2026): a new, simpler admin panel with quick setup, Hysteria, TUIC and OpenVPN.

docs.title: A new home for the guides
docs.text: This website was rewritten too: the app and manager guides have new screenshots, Persian and English pages now say the same thing, and every guide ends with related articles.

docs.title: Thank you
docs.text:
Hiddify is made by a small team and many volunteers: people who translate the app, test beta versions, report bugs and answer questions in the groups. Thank you. Our goal has not changed: free internet is everyone's right.

How you can help:

  • Give the projects a star on GitHub and rate the app in the stores.

docs.title: DNS tunnels in Hiddify: when almost everything is blocked
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

From 5 March 2026 the Hiddify app and Hiddify Manager learned DNS tunnels. They hide traffic inside DNS questions, which are rarely fully blocked. They are slow, but in the worst shutdowns they can still connect: DNSTT, VayDNS, MasterDNS and Soar.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• DNSTT in the core (March 2026), then many resolvers at once.
  • VayDNS with automatic choice of resolvers.
  • MasterDNS and Soar (November 2026); MasterDNS with few resolvers is about 8 times faster with our multi-resolver pool.
  • Links such as dnst://, masterdns:// and soar:// open in the app.
  • In the panel since Hiddify Manager 13.

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
Today these tools live inside the Hiddify app and Hiddify Manager. Start with the app, or run your own server.

Download the Hiddify app For experts

docs.title: How Hiddify Manager began: Hiddify Config and its first panel
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

The project that became Hiddify Manager started on 26 September 2022 as Hiddify Config: scripts that turn a cloud server into a working proxy. By 14 January 2023 it had a one-command install, more than ten protocols, user pages with QR codes, and its first panel (version 5).

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• September 2022, the first days: a Telegram proxy (MTProxy) and one-click templates for Microsoft Azure: paste a template at the cloud provider and get a working proxy.
  • October 2022: Shadowsocks (with v2ray for CDN, and with faketls), VMess, TCP BBR for speed, and the first one-command install on Ubuntu.
  • Smart routing in Clash: three modes: only filtered sites through the proxy, everything except Iranian sites (recommended), or everything.
  • November–December 2022: user guide pages with QR codes, usage monitoring, arm64 servers, and Trojan.
  • No domain needed: the install worked with sslip.io, turned the firewall on, and showed a temporary proxy link on the server for an hour, so anyone could get started.
  • One-click deploy on Oracle Cloud (free servers), Vultr, Hetzner and OVH.
  • January 2023: the Xray core with VLESS, VMess and Trojan links, with and without a CDN, and a speed test on the user page.
  • Version 5 (14 January 2023): the first Hiddify panel: many domains, configs you can turn on and off, fake CDN and gRPC. Version 6 (February) added TUIC and moved certificates to acme.sh.

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
Hiddify Manager is at version 14 now. Install the latest version, or update yours from the panel (take a backup first).

Install Hiddify Manager For experts
  • The repository was called hiddify-config until October 2023; today it is Hiddify-Manager.
  • Versions 1 to 6 have no git tags; version 5 is the "V5" merge of 14 January 2023, version 6 the v6 branch merged on 6 February 2023.
  • The README of February 2023 lists more than 20 protocols plus the Telegram proxy, tested on Ubuntu 20.04 and 22.04 (amd64, arm64).
  • Sources: first commit, one-command install, Xray, V5

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 10.70: SplitHTTP and fragment
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 10.70 came out on 29 July 2024. It added SplitHTTP, a new way to pass the filter over a CDN, Xray fragment, WireGuard output in the panel, and an editor for the text users see. Two weeks earlier, 10.50 had added quick setup steps for a new server.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• SplitHTTP (Xray), also over HTTP/3 (QUIC), which works well behind a CDN.
  • Xray fragment, and a custom URL test.
  • WireGuard output in the panel.
  • HTML editor for the custom text on the user page.
  • Quick setup (10.50): a few steps for a new server, with some services off by default.
  • Better IPv4 and IPv6 handling (10.50), and Reality and VLESS can be turned on separately (10.30).
  • Lighter server (10.20): Xray or sing-box configs that are not needed are turned off to save memory.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 11 is out
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 11.0.0 came out on 10 July 2025. It adds XHTTP, which can send upload and download through different domains, QUIC, a rebuilt proxy system where every setting can be changed, and it uses up to half the RAM it used before.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• XHTTP protocol, also with Reality (Reality XHTTP).
  • Separate domains for upload and download. Upload and download can use different domains or ALPNs, which makes the traffic harder to detect.
  • QUIC, next to H1, H2, WS and HTTPUpgrade, and it works with a CDN.
  • A rebuilt proxy system: change every parameter of each proxy as you like.
  • Bulk actions on users: delete, turn on, turn off, or reset the days and traffic of many users at once.
  • A password for the admin panel, an extra lock on admin access.
  • Up to 50% less RAM and lower CPU use.
  • Faster, simpler installation.
  • IP instead of a domain in proxies, and a custom User-Agent.
  • Better IP choice for AutoCDN domains, with random recent User-Agents.
  • Send chosen sites through WARP now also for Hysteria, Shadowsocks and TUIC.
  • A Docker version (first test version).
  • Many panel improvements in look and use.

docs.title: Should I update?
docs.text:
Newer versions are out now (12, 13 and 14), and an update takes you straight to the latest one. Take a backup first, then follow How to update HiddifyManager.

Install or update Hiddify Manager For experts: more changes in 11
  • Xray core 25.6; Python 3.13.
  • New HAProxy version (on Ubuntu 24.04 only), for more exact and faster routing.
  • sing-box subscription updated.
  • Changes since 10.86.4: Hiddify-Manager and the 11.0.0 release.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 12 is out
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 12.0.0 came out on 21 February 2026. It adds new ways to connect that are harder to block (Mieru, Naive and HTTP/2), a Telegram proxy that counts each user's traffic, and ECH, which hides the site name in the TLS handshake.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• New protocols: Mieru and Naive. Two more ways for your users to connect. Naive looks like normal Chrome traffic, also over QUIC. Mieru has its own TCP and UDP settings.
  • HTTP/2 (h2) transport, and Reality over TCP is now on by default.
  • Telegram proxy (MTProxy) with traffic counting. Each user gets their own Telegram proxy link, and the panel counts its traffic like any other config.
  • ECH (Encrypted Client Hello). A new TLS setting; when it is on, the links your users get include ECH, so the name of the site is hidden from the filter.
  • Fragment settings (size and timing of the packets) can now be changed in the panel.
  • sing-box is back next to Xray, so more client apps work with the same links.
  • Certificates for an IP address, better automatic certificates (ACME), and a resolve IP option for each domain.
  • SSH proxy now also carries UDP (UDP over TCP).
  • New actions on users in the users list.

The protocols are turned on and off in the panel settings. This is how the list looks in today's panel:

docs.title: Should I update?
docs.text:
Yes, if you run version 11. Take a backup first, then update from the panel (Actions › Update). See How to update HiddifyManager. Newer versions (13 and 14) are out now, so the update takes you straight to the latest one.

Install or update Hiddify Manager For experts: more changes in 12
  • Mieru: separate TCP and UDP settings; better Naive over QUIC.
  • No-header TCP stream option and fixed TCP settings for Xray.
  • Unified proxy generation for sing-box and Xray; hiddify-core updated.
  • Changes since 11.0.0: Hiddify-Manager, hiddifypanel.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 13 is out
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 13.0.0 came out on 26 September 2026. Now one panel can run many servers (nodes), there are DNS tunnels for times when almost everything is blocked, and the panel has a new dashboard that shows your users and servers at a glance.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• Many servers, one panel (nodes). Add other servers as nodes of your main panel. You add users and admins once, on the main panel, and they work on every node. Their traffic on all nodes is added up, and one subscription link has configs for all your servers.
  • DNS tunnels: DNSTT, VayDNS, MasterDNS and Slipstream. These carry traffic inside DNS questions. They are slow, but they can still work when almost every other way is blocked.
  • New dashboard with online users, usage charts and the health of each node.
  • More Xray options: VLESS encryption and flow, and more Reality and TCP settings.
  • Any kind of domain can be added, with extra fields you can use in your own proxy templates.
  • Choose more than one proxy at a time, and a reworked custom proxy maker.
  • Users: a "7 days" quick action, and admins can reset a password or get the admin link again.
  • Safer clicks: dangerous actions (like deleting) ask you to confirm first.
  • Persian font Vazirmatn and a layout that works better on phones.

This is the nodes list of the main panel (in today's panel):

docs.title: Should I update?
docs.text:
Yes. Take a backup first, then update from the panel (Actions › Update). See How to update HiddifyManager. Version 14 is out now, so the update takes you straight to it.

Install or update Hiddify Manager For experts: more changes in 13
  • Parent/child sync of users, TLS certificates and proxies; the parent reads configs from its children.
  • SNI routing with rust-rpxy-l4 next to HAProxy; DNS resolver and decoy upstream settings for HAProxy.
  • A hiddify-mysql service; lazy loading of the Xray API for lower memory use.
  • Experimental Docker install (Install Hiddify using Docker).
  • Changes since 12.0.0: Hiddify-Manager, hiddifypanel.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 14 is out
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 14.0.0 came out on 18 October 2026, and 14.2.0 on 6 November 2026. The panel has a new, simpler look with a quick setup, and it adds Hysteria, TUIC and OpenVPN, a new Telegram proxy, and an outbound manager (WARP, Tor and more) in one place.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• A new admin panel. Cleaner pages, a quick setup for a new server, and it can be installed like an app on your phone or computer (PWA).
  • A Protocols page to turn each protocol on or off in one place.
  • New protocols: Hysteria and TUIC, Trojan with Reality, and, since 14.2, OpenVPN (UDP and TCP).
  • Telegram proxy, new engine (telemt), also as a web proxy for Telegram Web.
  • Outbound manager: send traffic out through WARP, Tor or another server, with a default per admin. The panel tells you if Tor is not available.
  • ECH per domain: turn Cloudflare ECH on only where you need it.
  • WireGuard configs can be downloaded as .conf files (a .zip when there are several).
  • Users: copy a QR code as an image, add limits to many users at once, and (14.2) choose whether new users go to the top or the end of the list.
  • Admins (14.2): each admin's users' traffic is counted with a reset period, like users; filter admins by permission.
  • Support box editor (14.2): write the text users see on their page with a built-in editor and ready-made designs.
  • Block BitTorrent (14.2): one switch that works on every core.

The new dashboard:

And the quick setup for a new server:

docs.title: Should I update?
docs.text:
Yes. Version 14 is the one we support now. Take a backup first, then update from the panel (Actions › Update); see How to update HiddifyManager.

For a new server, use Ubuntu 26.04 or 24.04. Ubuntu 22.04 still works, but use it only when your provider has nothing newer (prerequisites).

Install or update Hiddify Manager For experts: more changes in 14
  • Clash Meta configs in the subscription (proxy_v3), with Hysteria and TUIC templates.
  • Telegram bot webhook secret check; Telegram web proxy domains served by telemt wildcard hosts (14.2).
  • Firewall rework with domain port redirection; better IPv6 handling.
  • 14.2: external MySQL/MariaDB and Redis server; journald and logrotate limits; decoy requests go to HTTPS first; Xray 26.10.31, hiddify-core 5.3.0, telemt 3.5.16.
  • Changes: 13.0.0 → 14.0.0, 14.0.0 → 14.2.0 (panel); Hiddify-Manager.

docs.text:
In 30 seconds

The first stable Hiddify Manager 1.0 came out on 28 February 2023, together with the first numbered server package (Hiddify Config 7.0). One server could now serve many users on many domains, with TUIC and ShadowTLS, a Telegram bot for admins, and each user's usage and days left in their subscription link.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• Many users and many domains on one server, with a default parent domain and a quick-setup window for domains.
  • TUIC ("the fastest protocol with the lowest latency") and ShadowTLS (1.1).
  • Choose proxies per domain, and give each domain a name (alias) and a description (1.1).
  • Clash profile per domain: users pick one domain's proxies, or a sequential, load-balance or automatic group (1.1).
  • Telegram bot for admins, then a command to create many accounts (1.1–1.6).
  • Usage and days left in the subscription link (1.2) and on the user page (1.4); a user's days start at the first connection.
  • Turn users off, reset a user's package (1.3), and delete many users at once (1.5).
  • Random proxy paths, which you can change, for more security (1.5); v2rayNG links for Android (1.2).

  • Many ports for every config; ports 80 and 443 can now be removed.
  • Rename proxies and choose the TLS fingerprint (iOS, Edge, random…).
  • Restart from the panel, a timer while settings apply, and a notice when the panel is out of date.
  • Hidden from search engines and bots.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 7: two cores, Xray and sing-box
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 7 came out on 29 May 2023, with server package 10.0. It added a second core, sing-box, next to Xray, with usage counted on both: the only panel that could do this. Reality now works on many domains and over gRPC, and Cloudflare Worker domains arrived.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• sing-box next to Xray, with a core selector and usage on both cores.
  • Reality on many domains, and Reality over gRPC.
  • Cloudflare Worker domains, and domain fronting (7.0.7).
  • Downgrade: go back to an earlier version from the update menu.
  • REST API for the panel.
  • Help videos from YouTube, with a local copy when YouTube is blocked.
  • Portuguese, and government sites removed from the decoy sites.
  • Open source (7.1.6, July 2023): the panel's code was published under an open-source license.

docs.title: Hiddify Manager 8: SSH proxy and one smart link
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify Manager 8 came out on 29 August 2023, with server package 10.2. A friend helped us add the secure SSH proxy. One smart subscription link now gives every app the configs it understands, short links are easy to type on another device, and the panel became much faster.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• SSH proxy ("liberty bridge"), with UDP over SSH.
  • One smart subscription link (the "auto" page and button): the panel gives each app the right configs.
  • Short links that work for a short time, in the style of Inspector Gadget.
  • Full sing-box configs in the subscription; sing-box 1.7 and 1.8 supported later (8.8).
  • Faster panel with Redis, and a MySQL database on the server.
  • Change the Reality keys, and open the panel by IP over HTTPS.
  • One-click QR codes (8.1), and links for Streisand and Hiddify Next.
  • Beta channel (8.6), and a safer first setup (8.8.96).

The Hiddify app 1.0 came out on 18 March 2024, with a Nowruz theme. Hiddify Next is now simply Hiddify. It has WARP built in, smart fragment, quick settings, and a VPN service on Windows and Linux, so you don't need to run it as administrator every time.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:

  • Smart fragment (TLS Tricks, more mature).
  • Quick settings on the home page.
  • VPN service on Windows and Linux: VPN mode without asking for administrator rights each time.
  • Failover: if a config fails, the app moves to another one.
  • Connection info on the home page: the active server, speed, IP and ping under the connect button.
  • WireGuard noise, and importing Clash and sing-box configs.
  • New icons and navigation, and haptic feedback.

docs.title: Hiddify app 4 is out
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify app 4.0.4 came out on 19 February 2026, and 4.1 followed in March. It has free profiles you can add with one tap, an Extra security mode, ready-made app lists for the per-app proxy on Android, and new ways to connect such as Naive, AmneziaWG and DNSTT.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• Free profiles. Add free WARP and Psiphon profiles from the app, without a subscription link.
  • Extra security. Put WARP behind your own proxy, so websites see a Cloudflare IP and your proxy provider can't see where you go.
  • Per-app proxy that picks the apps for you (Android). The app downloads a list of apps for your region and keeps it up to date; you can still change it by hand.
  • New protocols: Naive, AmneziaWG, raw WireGuard configs with "noise", and (4.1) DNSTT for heavy filtering.
  • Quick settings on the home page, and settings sorted into clearer groups.
  • More about your connection: your IP's country with its flag, and upload/download speed and the active profile in the Android notification.
  • Balancer strategies (4.1): choose how the app spreads traffic over the proxies of a profile.
  • Fragment (4.1): split the TLS handshake into packets to get past some filters.
  • Desktop: start on login on macOS, the window opens where you left it, and a raw AppImage on Linux.
  • You can now delete the active profile.

docs.title: Should I update?
docs.text:
Version 5 is out now, and it is better in every way. Update to the latest version from your store or from How to install the Hiddify app.

Download the Hiddify app For experts: more changes in 4
  • More inbounds on desktop: TPROXY, REDIRECT and DIRECT.
  • Route rules with regex checks; endpoint in the JSON editor.
  • enable-warp in profile headers; WARP license errors shown on connection failure.
  • Region detection from time zone and locale (4.1).
  • Changes: 2.5.7 → 4.0.4, 4.0.4 → 4.1.2.

docs.title: Hiddify app 5 is out
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

Hiddify app 5.5.5 came out on 4 November 2026 (the first 5.x test versions came a few days before). The big new thing is Chain: put WARP or Psiphon in front of or behind your proxy with one choice. You can also share your connection with other devices, send a profile to your TV, and let the app pick which apps go through the proxy.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• Chain: Extra security and Proxy unblocker. Two simple choices in quick settings. Extra security adds WARP after your proxy, so sites see a Cloudflare IP. Proxy unblocker reaches a blocked proxy through WARP or Psiphon.
  • WARP you can tune: choose the tunnel (WireGuard, AmneziaWG or MASQUE), pick a noise mode by name, and let the scanner find an address that works on your network.
  • Share your connection. Let your computer, TV or another phone use the connection of this device, with a QR code to set it up.
  • Send a profile to Android TV from your phone on the same Wi-Fi, instead of typing a long link with a remote.
  • Routing by app, chosen for you. The app picks the apps that should go through the proxy, and you can change the list. Built-in rules (for example Apple services) are ready to turn on.
  • A new home page: the connect button shows the traffic around it, and the proxy card shows each step of the connection.
  • Import and share more easily: import from a file or a zip; share a profile as a link, a QR code or a file.
  • Updates outside the stores: the app can download and install its own update.
  • Always-on VPN on Android; on Windows and Linux the VPN mode works out of the box, and on macOS the VPN runs as a system extension.

Chain in quick settings, sharing with other devices, and sending a profile to a TV:

docs.text:
Yes. Update from Google Play or the App Store, or download version 5 from How to install the Hiddify app. Your profiles stay as they are.

Coming next, in the 5.9 test versions: report a problem from the app with the logs attached, a router mode that shares the VPN with your whole network on Linux, OpenVPN profiles, and 19 more languages.

Download the Hiddify app For experts: more changes in 5
  • enable-warp and enable-psiphon profile headers merged into extra-security; a fragment header lets a subscription tune fragmentation.
  • LAN sharing: a local proxy without a password on its own port.
  • Desktop TUN core interface on Windows and Linux; macOS packet tunnel system extension.
  • mTLS for the core's gRPC; custom ipinfo-url; masterdns outbound template in the JSON editor.
  • Changes: 4.1.2 → 5.5.5.

docs.title: Hiddify core: one engine for every platform
docs.text:
In 30 seconds

With the first Hiddify Next app, on 11 September 2023, we released hiddify-core 0.1: one engine that runs the same way on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux. It is built on hiddify-sing-box, our version of sing-box with features the original does not have, such as TLS tricks, WARP and Psiphon.

docs.title: What was new
docs.text:
• One engine, five systems: the app looks and works the same everywhere.
  • hiddify-sing-box (since May 2023): TLS fragment and tricks, WARP (WireGuard, AmneziaWG, MASQUE), Psiphon, XHTTP and DNS tunnels.
  • ray2sing: reads VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Hysteria2, SSH, WireGuard and WARP links and turns them into sing-box configs.
  • Xray inside (core 1.9, July 2024) for configs sing-box cannot run.
  • More than 100 releases; about 880,000 core and 1,060,000 sing-box downloads from GitHub.
  • Core 5 (October 2026): hot reload, chains for Extra security and Proxy unblocker.
