docs.title: How to monitor server resources on HiddifyManager
How to monitor server resources on HiddifyManager
docs.text: This page shows you how to check your server's CPU (processor), RAM (working memory) and disk space, and what to do when one of them is full. Use it when the panel or the connections become slow, freeze, or stop responding.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• The panel loads very slowly or does not open.
  • Connections become slow or drop, even though the server's IP is clean.
  • Installing or updating Hiddify Manager fails with an out-of-memory or "no space left on device" error.

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• A process is using most of the CPU or RAM.
  • The disk is full, often because of large log files or old backups.

docs.title: Check 1: the dashboard in the panel
docs.text:
The quickest check needs no commands.

  1. Log in to your HiddifyManager panel. The Dashboard opens first.
  2. Scroll down to the Node Health card. Each server is a "node"; This server is the one the panel runs on. The card shows CPU, RAM and Network charts, and a table with each node's Uptime, Panel version, Disk use, Uptime Upload, Uptime Download, Connections and Unique IPs. If you have several nodes, you can pick one in the node filter at the top of the dashboard (All nodes).

docs.title: Check 2: CPU and RAM with htop
docs.text:
htop is a program that shows, live, how much CPU and RAM each running program (each process) uses.

Before you start, connect to your server over SSH (a secure way to type commands on a remote server). See How to connect to the server via SSH. If the HiddifyManager menu opens, press Cancel (or Esc) to close it. If the menu is still on the screen, type clear and press Enter.

  1. If htop is not installed, install it. Run this on your server, over SSH:

    apt install htop

    On Ubuntu it is usually installed already.

  2. Open htop:

    htop

  3. To sort the processes by CPU use, click the CPU% column header. The process at the top uses the most CPU.

  4. To sort by RAM use, click the MEM% column header.
  5. To exit htop, press q (or Ctrl+C).

docs.title: A HiddifyManager service uses too much CPU or RAM
docs.text:
HiddifyManager's services have names that start with hiddify-, for example hiddify-panel, hiddify-xray, hiddify-core and hiddify-haproxy. Older guides mention hiddify-nginx and hiddify-singbox: nginx was removed in v14, and hiddify-singbox is now hiddify-core.

If one of these services uses most of the CPU or RAM, restart the services. Run this on your server, over SSH:

hiddify restart

You can also run hiddify with no options to open the HiddifyManager menu and choose restart with the arrow keys. See How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH.

When the restart is done, check that every service is running:

hiddify status

Then open htop again and check whether the usage has gone down. If it goes up again soon, ask for help in the Hiddify Telegram group.

docs.title: RAM looks full
docs.text:
RAM is short-term memory that running programs and the operating system use. Some facts that help you read the numbers:

  • How much RAM is used does not depend directly on how many users you have. HiddifyManager's services and the operating system need memory whether you have 10 users or 1,000.
  • Linux uses spare RAM as a cache (a temporary copy of files, to make things faster). So RAM use of up to about 80% is normal. You do not need to do anything.
  • Do not reboot the server just because RAM looks full.

If you still want to empty the cache, run these commands as the root user, on your server, over SSH:

sync && sysctl -w vm.drop_caches=3

If that command gives an error, use this one instead. It also prints the free memory before and after:

free && sync && echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches && free

If your server has very little RAM, adding swap (disk space used as extra memory) can help. See How to enable Swap on Linux.

docs.title: The disk is full
docs.text:
1. Check disk space. Run this on your server, over SSH:

    df -h --total

    You should see a table like this:

  2. Look at the line for your main disk (the one mounted on /, often called sda1 or vda1). If Use% is close to 100%, free some space.

  3. HiddifyManager keeps its logs in /opt/hiddify-manager/data/log (older versions used /opt/hiddify-manager/log/system, which no longer exists). To empty all the log files without breaking the services that write to them:

    find /opt/hiddify-manager/data/log -type f -name "*.log" -exec truncate -s 0 {} +

    Since v14, HiddifyManager limits its own logs (each log file is emptied when it grows past 100 MB, and the system journal is capped at 500 MB), so logs rarely fill the disk on their own.

  4. HiddifyManager also keeps automatic backups in /opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup. If that folder is large, download the backups you want to keep, then delete the old ones. Do not delete the rest of /opt/hiddify-manager/data: it holds your database and settings.

  5. Run df -h --total again to check that space has been freed.

docs.title: How to set DNS server on HiddifyManager
How to set DNS server
docs.text:
This page shows you how to choose the DNS server that your HiddifyManager server uses, and how to check that DNS works. You need it if sites don't open through your proxy, or if a DNS leak test shows the wrong DNS servers.

DNS (Domain Name System) turns names into IP addresses. For example, when you open google.com, your device first asks a DNS server "what is the IP of google.com?". The DNS server answers with the IP address, and only then does your device connect to the site.

Your server needs a working, trusted DNS server, just like your phone or computer.

docs.title: Well-known public DNS servers
docs.text:
Big companies run free DNS servers that work worldwide. These are good choices for your server:

Address Provider 1.1.1.1 Cloudflare 8.8.8.8 Google

docs.title: Symptoms of a DNS problem on the server
docs.text:
• Sites don't open through the proxy, or open very slowly, while the connection itself works.
  • The installer or an update shows the warning DNS is not working.
  • A DNS leak test shows DNS servers you didn't choose.

The fix is one or both of the methods below.

docs.title: Method 1: set the DNS server in the panel
docs.text:
The panel's DNS Server setting is the DNS server that the server and its proxies use to look up sites for your users. When you change it, the server's own system DNS changes with it. The default is 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare).

  1. Log in to your HiddifyManager admin panel.
  2. In the sidebar, under Settings, click Settings.
  3. DNS Server is an advanced setting, so turn on the Show Advanced Settings switch at the top of the page. Then type DNS Server in the search box (Search all settings…). The setting is the first row of the General Settings card, with the Advanced label.
  4. Open the DNS Server list and pick a public DNS, for example Cloudflare 1.1.1.1. To use a DNS server that is not in the list, choose Custom and enter its address.
  5. Click Save.
  6. When the panel asks, click Apply Configs so the change takes effect.

docs.title: Method 2: set the server's own DNS over SSH
docs.text:
The server's operating system also uses a DNS server, for example to download updates. On Ubuntu, HiddifyManager uses the systemd-resolved service for this. Method 1 already changes it, but if the server's DNS doesn't work (for example, you can't open the panel), set it with the script that comes with HiddifyManager (the installer uses the same script).

  1. Connect to your server over SSH. If the HiddifyManager menu opens, press Ctrl+C to leave it.

  2. Run this command on your server. It sets the DNS servers to 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1:

    sudo /opt/hiddify-manager/scripts/common/change_dns.py 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1

  3. When it finishes, the last line should say DNS servers set to 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1.

Don't delete or lock /etc/resolv.conf

Older guides told you to delete /etc/resolv.conf, write it by hand, and lock it with chattr +i. Don't do this on a current HiddifyManager server. On Ubuntu this file is managed by systemd-resolved, and locking it can stop HiddifyManager's installer from repairing DNS. If you locked it before, unlock it with sudo chattr -i /etc/resolv.conf.

docs.title: Check DNS on the server
docs.text:
Run these commands on your server, over SSH.

  1. Check which DNS servers the system uses:

    resolvectl status

    Look for the line DNS Servers. It should list only the servers you chose, for example 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1.

  2. Check that a name can be resolved:

    nslookup google.com

    If it works, you see one or more Address: lines with Google's IP addresses. The Server: line may show 127.0.0.53. That is normal: it is the local systemd-resolved service, which forwards the request to the servers from step 1. If you see an error such as connection timed out or server can't find, DNS doesn't work: repeat Method 2.

    (If nslookup is missing, install it with sudo apt install dnsutils.)

Learn more about DNS leaks

docs.title: How to setup Firewall on HiddifyManager
How to setup Firewall on HiddifyManager panel
docs.text: This page explains what a firewall is, how to turn on HiddifyManager's built-in firewall, and how to open a port by hand when a program that HiddifyManager does not know about needs one.

docs.title: What is a firewall?
docs.text:
A firewall is software or hardware that controls which network traffic may reach a computer or server, and blocks the rest. Here we only deal with the software firewall on Linux servers.

On Linux, a common firewall tool is iptables. You give it a list of rules. Each rule says which traffic (for example, which port, a numbered "door" that a service listens on) is allowed through and which is blocked. HiddifyManager uses iptables.

docs.title: The firewall in the HiddifyManager panel
docs.text:
HiddifyManager can manage the server's firewall for you. When it is on:

  • Only the ports HiddifyManager needs stay open: SSH (port 22 and the port your SSH server really uses), 80, 443, 53, and every port your enabled proxies use (the same list that Public ports shows on the panel's Actions page).
  • All other incoming connections are blocked.
  • Ping (ICMP) is still allowed, so you can still test whether your IP is clean.
  • When you change a port or turn a proxy on or off in the panel, HiddifyManager updates the rules for you when you apply the changes.

The firewall is off by default. We recommend turning it on, because it makes your server harder to attack.

To turn it on:

  1. Log in to your HiddifyManager panel.
  2. In the sidebar, under Settings, click Settings, and find the General Settings card. You can also type Firewall in the settings search box.
  3. Turn on Firewall.
  4. Click Save, and apply the changes when the panel asks you to.

Before you turn it on

If you run other programs on the same server that need their own ports (for example another panel or a web server), open those ports by hand first, as shown below. Otherwise they stop working once the firewall is on.

docs.title: Open a port by hand
docs.text:
Do this only for programs that HiddifyManager does not manage. HiddifyManager opens the ports of its own proxies by itself.

Before you start, connect to your server over SSH (a secure way to type commands on a remote server). If you don't know how, see How to connect to the server via SSH. If the HiddifyManager menu opens, press Cancel (or Esc) to close it. If the menu is still on the screen, type clear and press Enter.

  1. Run this command on your server, over SSH. This example opens TCP port 1234. Replace 1234 with the port number you need:

    iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 1234 -j ACCEPT

    If the program uses UDP, run the same command with -p udp instead of -p tcp. If your server uses IPv6, run the same command again with ip6tables instead of iptables.

  2. Check that the rule was added:

    iptables -L INPUT -n --line-numbers

    You should see a line with ACCEPT and dpt:1234 (your port).

  3. Save the rules so they survive a reboot:

    netfilter-persistent save

    If the command is not found, install it with apt install iptables-persistent and run it again.

docs.title: Block ping (optional)
docs.text:
HiddifyManager's firewall rules always allow ping. Most people should leave it that way, because ping helps you check whether your server is reachable. If you still want to block ping, run this on your server, over SSH:

iptables -I INPUT -p icmp -j DROP

To allow ping again, remove that rule:

iptables -D INPUT -p icmp -j DROP

Remember that online ping tests will fail while ping is blocked. Use a TCP test on port 443 instead.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• You can't connect over SSH after turning on the firewall: HiddifyManager opens port 22 and the port your SSH server is using when the firewall rules are applied. If you changed the SSH port afterwards, apply the panel's configuration again, or log in through your hosting provider's web console and run hiddify apply.
  • Another program on the server stopped working: its port is closed. Open it by hand as shown above.
  • A port you opened by hand is closed again after a reboot: you did not save the rules. Run netfilter-persistent save.

docs.title: How to transfer files between a server and a computer
How to transfer files between a server and a computer
docs.text:
This page shows you how to copy files from your server to your computer and back, for example to keep a copy of a HiddifyManager backup or to upload a file to the server.

Only need a panel backup?

You do not need any commands for that. In the HiddifyManager admin panel, open the Backup & restore page and click Download backup. See How to back up and restore the panel.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You know your server's IP address and SSH username (usually root), and you can connect to it over SSH.
  • Open a terminal on your computer:
    • Windows: PowerShell
    • macOS: Terminal
    • Linux: Terminal

This page uses scp, a command that copies files over SSH. It is already included in Windows 10 and 11, macOS and Linux.

If Windows says scp is not recognized

Open PowerShell as administrator (right-click PowerShell, then Run as administrator) and run this command to install the OpenSSH client:

Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0

Then close PowerShell and open it again.

docs.title: Find the file on the server
docs.text:
Hiddify Manager saves an automatic backup of the panel every 6 hours in /opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup/. To see the list, connect to the server over SSH and run:

ls /opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup/

You will see files named by date and time, like 2026_10_20__06_00_03.json:

Pick the file you want to copy and note its name.

docs.title: Copy a file from the server to your computer
docs.text:
Run this on your own computer, not on the server. The general form is:

scp <user>@<server-ip>:<path/on/server> "<folder on your computer>"

Example: your username is root, the server IP is 1.1.1.1, and you want to copy a backup into the folder C:\Backup:

scp root@1.1.1.1:/opt/hiddify-manager/data/backup/2026_10_20__06_00_03.json "C:\Backup"

Type your server password (or key passphrase) when asked. It worked if the file now appears in C:\Backup.

docs.title: Copy a file from your computer to the server
docs.text:
Run this on your own computer. Example: the file C:\File\text.txt should go to the /root/ folder on the server:

scp "C:\File\text.txt" root@1.1.1.1:/root/

To check, connect to the server over SSH and run:

ls /root/

It worked if text.txt is in the list.

docs.title: If it does not work
docs.text:
• No such file or directory: the path is wrong. Check it with ls on the server, and remember that Linux paths are case-sensitive (hiddify-manager, not Hiddify-Manager).
  • Permission denied: the username, password or key is wrong, or the user cannot read or write that folder. Use root or a folder your user owns.
  • Connection timed out: the server IP or SSH port is wrong. If you changed the SSH port, add -P with the port number (capital P for scp), for example scp -P 2222 ....

docs.title: Use the web panel instead
docs.text: In Hiddify Manager v14, the admin panel has an SSH terminal page with a built-in file browser. You can upload files to the server and download files from it there, without a separate program. Avoid entering your server password on third-party websites.

docs.title: TLS setting for increased security
docs.text:
This page shows you how to make TLS connections that go through a CDN harder to detect. You need it if you use a Cloudflare CDN domain with HiddifyManager and your connections are unstable on some Internet providers.

TLS is the encryption that protects https connections. Filtering systems can study patterns in TLS traffic, and older TLS versions show more of these patterns. TLS 1.3, the newest version, encrypts more of the connection setup and is harder to recognise.

docs.title: Set the minimum TLS version on Cloudflare
docs.text:
Symptom: your CDN (Cloudflare) configs connect on some operators but are unstable or don't connect on others.

Likely cause: Cloudflare still accepts older TLS versions for your domain.

Fix: tell Cloudflare to accept only TLS 1.3.

  1. Log in to your Cloudflare account and select your domain.
  2. In the menu, open SSL/TLS, then Edge Certificates.
  3. Find Minimum TLS Version and set it to TLS 1.3.

What to check: reconnect from a device on the operator that had problems.

If it still doesn't work: try a new subdomain. The filtering system may have already detected the old subdomain.

docs.title: TLS 1.3 on your device
docs.text:
The Hiddify app and other Xray or sing-box based apps have their own built-in TLS. They don't use your operating system's TLS settings, so you normally don't need to change anything on your phone or computer.

Windows 11, macOS and most recent Linux versions already have TLS 1.3 turned on for their own programs.

Optional: turn on TLS 1.2 and 1.3 in Windows 10 settings

This only affects programs that use Windows' built-in TLS. Microsoft does not officially support TLS 1.3 in Windows 10, so this may have no effect. Change the Windows registry only if you know what you are doing.

  1. Open Notepad and paste the text below:

    Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Client]
"DisabledByDefault"=dword:00000000
"Enabled"=dword:00000001
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Server]
"DisabledByDefault"=dword:00000000
"Enabled"=dword:00000001
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.3\Client]

docs.title: Troubleshooting connectivity issues with HiddifyManager and proxies
Troubleshooting connectivity issues with HiddifyManager and proxies
docs.text: Configs do not connect, or they connect on one ISP and not on another? The Hiddify Manager panel (v14.5) has tools that find and fix most of these problems. This page tells you which tool to use for each symptom.

docs.title: First, find where the problem is
docs.text: The key question is: does it fail for everyone, or only for some users and ISPs? If it fails for everyone, something is broken on the server or in the configs, and the panel tools find it directly. If it fails only on some ISPs, it is filtering, and you must test from that ISP.

docs.title: 1. Nobody can connect: the server and the configs
Check config health
docs.text:
On the Dashboard, find the Config Health card and click Check now. The panel tests every config of a subscription from the server itself, the way the Hiddify app and the Xray apps receive it.

Click a row with failing configs to see the reason in plain words:

Reason What to do, usually Connects, but traffic does not reach the internet Check the config’s outbound (for example WARP) or the server’s IPv6. Connection refused That protocol or port is off: turn it on in Protocols and apply. TLS handshake failed Check the domain’s certificate or its Reality setting in Domains. No answer in time A service or port does not answer: check the services and the firewall in the next steps.

Disable failing removes the configs that work for no app from everyone’s subscription, so users do not waste time on them; Restore turns them back on. All about config health

docs.title: Check the services
docs.text:
Open Actions in the menu. On the Apply & Status page:

  1. Check Status › Check now: shows whether each service runs. It changes nothing.
  2. If a service is down, click Restart. If you just changed settings, click Apply now.
  3. In Logs, click the eye icon to read that service’s error.

docs.title: Make sure the ports are open in the firewall
docs.text: If the services run but no config connects from outside, usually the server’s firewall or the provider’s firewall blocks the ports. On the same Apply & Status page, click Public Ports: it lists every port the server needs open, with ready Firewall Commands (ufw). Open these ports in the server’s firewall and in your provider’s panel.

docs.title: 2. Only one user cannot connect
docs.text:
1. In Users, check that the user still has days and traffic left and is not disabled.

  2. In Tools › Config Tester, click the link box and pick that user, set App to the app the user has, and click Start Test. The panel tests exactly what that user’s app receives.

  3. If the configs work here, the problem is the user’s app or internet: ask them to update the subscription in the app. The Hiddify app understands every panel protocol; some other apps do not. The app log shows the exact reason.

docs.title: 3. It fails or is slow on some ISPs: filtering
docs.text:
The tools of part 1 test from the server, so they do not see the filtering in your users’ country. For this part, open the panel’s Scanner (Tools › Scanner) on the ISP that has the problem, with your VPN off; for example once on a phone with one mobile ISP and once with another. The scanner runs in your browser, on your own internet at that moment.

CDN domainTLS / FragmentReality

The Cloudflare IP your users get is blocked or slow on that ISP. In the IP Scanner tab, choose the CDN domain and the ISP, click Start, then Save to the Domain. Users get the working IPs with their next subscription update.

If IPs are found but the connection drops after a little upload, use Full test with upload, from another device.

The ISP reads the site name in the first TLS packet. In the Fragment tab, Apply a preset to the CDN domain and check it with an app on that ISP. Hiddify app users can also turn fragment on in the app themselves.

A Reality config looks like a visit to another site (its SNI); if the ISP filters that site, the config fails. In the REALITY SNI tab, click Make the Command and run it on a device on that ISP to find the filtered SNIs. With Automatic Switch, a filtered SNI is replaced by a working Spare SNI by itself.

docs.title: If the server’s own IP is blocked
docs.text:
Confirm it with How to check if the server IP or domain is clean. The panel cannot unblock a blocked IP: either change the server’s IP (many providers sell a new one), or reach the server through something that is not blocked:

RealityLooks like visiting a normal site; works where TLS is blocked. Cloudflare CDNThe filter sees only the CDN’s IP, not your server’s. Relay serverA server inside the country passes the traffic to yours. A new or fake domainWhen the current domain has been found and blocked.

docs.title: 4. The panel does not open either
docs.text:
Connect to the server with SSH and use these commands:

Command What it does hiddify status The status of every service hiddify admin The current admin links (they may have changed after a change) hiddify restart Restart the services without changing the settings hiddify apply Apply the settings saved in the panel

Or just run hiddify to open the Hiddify Manager menu, with status, admin link and logs.

docs.title: Still not working?
docs.text: If another tool connects to the same server and the same domain but the Hiddify Manager configs do not, please tell us. Send the working config link (VLESS, VMess or Trojan) in a GitHub issue so we can add that kind of config to the panel. Before you send it, open the link in Tools › Text Decoders and remove the real server address and the passwords.

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyClashAndroid app
docs.text:
HiddifyClashAndroid is no longer developed

HiddifyClashAndroid is an old Hiddify app. It is no longer developed or updated, and new protocols and features of Hiddify Manager may not work in it. The Hiddify app replaces it, on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux: see how to install the Hiddify app. This page is kept for people who still use HiddifyClashAndroid.

This software is developed based on Clash and many features are included in it.

docs.title: Download the app
docs.text:
To do this, enter the Android tab in your user panel and open the section related to Hidify Android.

  • Click on Direct Download to download the application.

docs.title: Install the app
docs.text: Run the downloaded file to install the program. It may give an error that the source of the file is unknown, which you can confirm to install the file.

docs.title: Add profile to the app
docs.text:
• Here you need to get acquainted with a concept called profile. The profile is a yml file includes all the connections that can be accessed in this section. There are two types of profiles

  • Green or lite profile for filtered sites, in which case only filtered sites are passed through the VPN and other sites, including domestic sites, are opened without the VPN, which is a better mode. So you don't need to turn off VPN to open these sites.

  • The second mode is the orange or Normal profile, which passes all traffic through the VPN to the server. If domestic sites are blocked on the server, they will not be opened, or if WARP is enabled for all traffic, domestic sites will be opened via WARP.

  • Finally, choose one of the two profiles and click on Install so that the profile is automatically added to the program.

docs.title: Add profile manually
docs.text:
• Tap on Profile in the HiddifyClash app on Android.
  • And on the screen that opens, tap the + button.
  • On this page, go to the URL section.
  • And copy the selected profile link from the user page and place it here and save it.
  • The desired profile is added to the app.

docs.title: Connect to the app
docs.text: Click on the specified button to connect.

docs.title: Update profile
docs.text: To update the profile and configs, click on the profile. Then, on the opened page, click on the update sign so that the profile is updated according to the latest server changes.

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyNG app
docs.text:
HiddifyNG is no longer developed

HiddifyNG is an old Hiddify app. It is no longer developed or updated, and new protocols and features of Hiddify Manager may not work in it. The Hiddify app replaces it, on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux: see how to install the Hiddify app. This page is kept for people who still use HiddifyNG.

This app is the best software for connecting to Xray protocols on Android operating system. Download and install the software

Enter the Android tab in your user panel and open the HiddifyNG section.

Click on Direct Download to download the application.

You can also download and install the program directly from GitHub and Google Play.

docs.title: Add config
docs.text: To do this, in the same section related to the HiddifyNG program, click on Click to Import to add the configuration to the program.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: This plate is designed for quick connection to the filter breaker, which consists of several parts.

docs.title: Profile section
docs.text:
In this section, you can see your imported profiles.

  • View the Traffic usage and the total traffic. Also see the number of days remaining in your account. (section number 1)

  • You can enter your user page in the panel through button number 2

  • You can contact your support through button number 3.

docs.title: Add new profile
docs.text:
For this, press the + button from the profile section or from the top right of the application.

You can use the copied link or scan its QR code.

docs.title: Connect to the software
docs.text:
To do this, click on the connection button in the middle of the screen.

After you connect, the result of the connection test is shown too.

docs.title: Configs
docs.text: Here are the configs that were added using the subscription link.

docs.title: Add a config by hand
docs.text: For this, use the + button number 1.

docs.title: Update configs
docs.text: For this, use the update button number 2.

docs.title: Start or stop configs
docs.text: For this, use the button number 3.

docs.title: Three-dot menu in configs
docs.text: In this menu, which is a subset of the config menu, you can do various things that are mentioned below.

docs.title: Filter configuration file
docs.text: This menu is for filtering configurations based on a specific item.

docs.title: Export non-custom configs
docs.text: This menu is used to exit the configuration added to the program and transfer it to another device.

docs.title: Remove all config
docs.text: This menu is for deleting the entire config file from the program.

docs.title: Remove duplicate config
docs.text: Sometimes, due to the large number of configurations, you need to sort and remove the duplicate imported configurations from the program. Use this option for this.

docs.title: Remove invalid config (Test first)
docs.text: Sometimes you manipulate the configs to get better results by changing the parameters. If you need to delete configs that have invalid settings, use this option.

docs.title: Real delay all configuration
docs.text: This option displays the result for actual ping test based on the connection to the configs.

docs.title: Sorting by test results
docs.text:
Sorts the list of configs based on the test result. Configurations with lower ping and better results are placed at the top of the list.

To do this, tap on the section related to the profile to open the section related to their settings.

You can edit the imported profiles or add a new profile.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: On this page, there are advanced settings that will be mentioned later.

docs.title: Proxy mode settings
docs.text: The settings of this section determine how the traffic of sites and applications pass through the VPN, which consists of three parts.

docs.title: All
docs.text: All sites and apps pass through the app.

docs.title: Blocked
docs.text: Passes detected filtered sites through the app.

docs.title: Not Opened
docs.text: In addition to the identified filter sites, it also passes through the app the sites whose filtering status is unknown.

docs.title: Fragment
docs.text:
Fragment splits the sent packets into some pieces. In this way, SNI is hidden from the GFW and filtering will be bypassed. more information

The settings in this section determine how information is transmitted in the form of fragmented packets. The purpose of applying these settings is to create resistance against the filtering system.

docs.title: Default
docs.text: Applies the fragment defined in the config or proxy link.

docs.title: Random
docs.text: It splits packets into random chunks.

docs.title: SNI
docs.text: It splits packets into two pieces.

docs.title: Connection mode
docs.text: The settings in this section determine how to connect to configs.

docs.title: Smart
docs.text: It will automatically connect to the configuration with the highest speed (lowest ping).

docs.title: Load Balance
docs.text: It connects to several configs at the same time and traffic is distributed between them. This mode is very useful when the IP related to the configs is not clean. By using this mode and spreading the load on several configs, an acceptable speed would be obtained.

docs.title: Manual
docs.text: Configs are entered manually. By clicking this button, the app opens another page that shows the list of available configs in which you can choose your desired one.

docs.title: Three-line software menu settings
docs.text: In this section, there are several general settings, the most useful parts of which are these.

docs.title: Subscription group setting
docs.text: Settings for all subscription links Select this option.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: There are general software settings in this section.

docs.title: Logcat
docs.text: Use this option if you need a log file for troubleshooting.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Use this menu if you need to report bugs and errors.

docs.title: Tutorial for Nekobox app
docs.text: This page shows you how to add your Hiddify Manager subscription to the free NekoBox app on Android, test the configs, connect, and chain two proxies. NekoBox is based on sing-box and also runs well on older phones. The pictures are from NekoBox 1.4.2 and the Hiddify Manager v14.5 user page.

docs.title: Install NekoBox
docs.text:
NekoBoxv1.4.2Android 5+FreeNov 2026

Download APK onGitHub

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

For very old phones, take the armeabi-v7a.apk file. Do not install NekoBox from Google Play: its developers say the Google Play version has been run by someone else since 2024 and is not open source. The download button on your user page also gives the GitHub APK.

docs.title: Add the subscription: the quick way (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Open your user page link on the phone and tap the big round button. If the Hiddify app is also installed and opens by itself, tap Cancel and go back to the browser.

  2. In Configure Your VPN, tap View More, then NekoBox, then Import To App.

  3. If Android asks which app to use, choose NekoBox (Import subscription), then Just once.

  4. NekoBox asks you to confirm the import; tap YES. A new group with your configs is created.

Why the quick way is better

With the quick way, the server sends the configs in Clash Meta format and only the ones NekoBox understands (75 configs in our test). The Subscription link used in the manual way gives every config (125), including XHTTP, which NekoBox does not support and shows as "Unavailable" in the test.

docs.title: Add the subscription by hand
docs.text:
1. On the user page, tap the round button, and under Import Manually tap Copy Link.

  2. In NekoBox, open the side menu (three lines) and tap Group.

  3. Tap the add group button at the top.

  4. Type a Group name (for example your server’s name). Set Group Type to Subscription. Then tap Subscription Link.

  5. Paste the copied link and tap OK.

  6. Turn on Auto Update so the configs update by themselves. Leave Force Resolve off. Then tap ✓ at the top.

  7. NekoBox lists the configs it added; tap OK. The group card shows the traffic used and left, the expiry date and the number of configs. Tap UPDATE to refresh it any time.

docs.title: Test and connect
docs.text:
1. Go back to Configuration (the main screen) from the side menu. Tap the three-dot menu and tap URL Test.

  2. Each config shows its response time in milliseconds; lower is better. Unavailable or Timeout means that config does not work. Order › By Delay in the same menu puts the best ones on top, and Clear unavailable removes the broken ones.

  3. Tap a good config (a colored line appears next to it) and tap the round button at the bottom. The first time, Android asks for VPN permission; tap OK.

  4. Tap the bar at the bottom to test the connection. You should see a message like Success: HTTP handshake took 75ms.

To disconnect, tap the round button again.

docs.title: Proxy chain: send traffic through two proxies
docs.text:
A proxy chain sends your traffic through one proxy and then through a second one. Websites only see the address of the last proxy. This is useful, for example, when a site blocks your server's IP. It is slower than a single proxy.

In this example, the first proxy is a Reality config from your server, and the second is a Cloudflare Worker config.

  1. On the main screen, tap the + button and tap Manual Settings.

  2. Choose Proxy Chain.

  3. Tap Add Profile and choose the first config, for example your Reality config.

  4. Tap Add Profile again and choose the second config, for example your Cloudflare Worker config.
  5. Save the chain, select it, and connect.

To check it, open a site that shows your IP, such as ipinfo.io. If it shows a Cloudflare IP, the chain works.

Note

  • The connection test may show an error for a chain even when the chain works. Check with the IP site instead.
  • The proxies in a chain can also be http or socks5 proxies.
  • A chain can have more than two proxies, but each one makes the connection slower.

docs.title: Tutorial for V2rayNG app
docs.text: This page shows you how to add your Hiddify Manager subscription link to the free V2rayNG app on Android, test the configs, connect and keep the configs up to date. The pictures are from V2rayNG 2.3.15 and the Hiddify Manager v14.5 user page.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Have your user page link ready. It is the link your server admin sent you; it opens your personal Hiddify Manager page.
  • A subscription link holds all your connection settings (configs). A config is the settings for one connection to the server. V2rayNG can update the subscription link later and get new configs from the server.

docs.title: Install V2rayNG
docs.text:
V2rayNGv2.3.15Android 7+FreeNov 2026

GET IT ONGoogle PlayDownload APK onGitHub

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

On GitHub, the file ending in universal.apk works on every phone. The download buttons are on your user page too (step 3 in the next part). If you downloaded the APK file, open it to install. Android may ask you to allow installs from "unknown sources" for your browser; allow it.

docs.title: Add the subscription link: the quick way
docs.text:
1. Open your user page link on the phone and tap the big round button in the middle.

    If the Hiddify app is also on the phone, the phone may open it right away and ask Add profile?. For V2rayNG, tap Cancel and go back to the browser.

  2. The Configure Your VPN window opens. Tap View More, then choose V2RayNG.

  3. If you do not have the app yet, install it from Download. Then tap Import To App.

  4. If Android asks which app to open it with, choose v2rayNG, then Just once.

  5. V2rayNG opens and puts the configs in a new tab called import sub. The app stays on the Default tab, so it looks empty: tap the import sub tab to see the configs.

Configs added this way are labeled CUSTOM: they are full Xray configs that the server makes for V2rayNG. If this way does not work, add the link by hand.

docs.title: Add the subscription link by hand
docs.text:
1. On the user page, tap the round button, and in the window that opens, under Import Manually, tap Copy Link.

  2. Open V2rayNG, tap the menu button (three lines) in the top corner and choose Subscriptions.

  3. Tap the + button at the top.

  4. Fill in the form:

    • Remarks: any name, for example your server’s name.
    • Optional URL: paste the copied link here.
    • Enable update: keep it on.
    • Enable automatic update: turn it on so the app updates the configs by itself every day (every 1440 minutes).

  5. Tap the save button (✓) at the top and go back to the main screen.

  6. Tap the tab of your link (the name you wrote in Remarks). Tap the three-dot menu and choose Update subscription. The configs appear in the list.

docs.title: Test the configs
docs.text:
1. Tap the three-dot menu and choose Test real delays.

  2. The app tests a real connection through each config and shows the result next to it in milliseconds (ms). Lower is better. A config that shows -1 does not work right now. Sort by test results in the same menu puts the best ones at the top.

The first row of the list (with the remaining traffic and days) is not a real config; it only shows your subscription’s details. The card above the list also shows the traffic used and the date your subscription ends.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Tap a config with a good test result to select it (a colored line appears next to it).
  2. Tap the ▶ button in the bottom corner. The first time, Android asks for permission to set up a VPN; tap OK. If the app asks for access to nearby devices, you do not need it to connect.
  3. The button turns orange. Tap the bar at the bottom of the screen to test the connection: you should see Connection succeeded.

To disconnect, tap the same button again.

docs.title: Update the subscription link
docs.text:
When the admin changes something on the server, update the subscription link to get the new configs:

  • In your link’s tab, tap the three-dot menu › Update subscription, or the ↻ button on the card above the list.
  • If you turned on Enable automatic update, the app updates by itself every day. It does not always work on every phone; if a config stops working, update by hand.

After the update, test the configs again and connect.

docs.title: If it does not connect
docs.text:
• Update the subscription link, test the configs again and choose another config with a good result.
  • Some configs, for example ones with newer protocols, do not work in V2rayNG. Try the Hiddify app.
  • See Troubleshooting connectivity issues.

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyClashDesktop software
docs.text:
HiddifyClashDesktop is no longer developed

HiddifyClashDesktop is an old Hiddify app. It is no longer developed or updated, and new protocols and features of Hiddify Manager may not work in it. The Hiddify app replaces it, on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux: see how to install the Hiddify app. This page is kept for people who still use HiddifyClashDesktop.

This software is developed based on Clash and many features are included in it.

docs.title: Downloading the software
docs.text:
For this, enter the Desktop tab in your user panel and open the section related to HiddifyClash.

You can download the software based on your operating system from the section number 3 indicated in the image above.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Installing the program is very simple and is completed with a few next steps.

docs.title: Mac
docs.text: For Mac, you must confirm the program in the privacy section.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text: For Linux, you only need to give executable access to the downloaded AppImage file and run it.

docs.title: Adding a profile to the app
docs.text:
For this, enter the Desktop tab in your user panel and open the section related to HiddifyClash.

  • Here you need to get acquainted with a concept called profile. The profile of a yml file includes all the connections that can be accessed in this section. There are two types of profiles

  • Green or lite profile for filtered sites, in which case only filtered sites are passed through the filter breaker and other sites, including Iranian sites, are opened without the filter breaker, which is a better mode. So you don't need to turn off VPN to open these sites.

  • The second mode is the orange or normal profile, which sends all traffic from the filter breaker to the server. If Iranian sites are blocked on the server, they will not be opened, or if warp is enabled for all traffic, Iranian sites will be opened with warp.

  • Finally, choose one of the two profiles from section number 4.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
Click on install profile, the profile will be automatically added to the program. You can also import the copied link in the profile section manually in section 1.

In section number 2, the information related to the imported profile, including the expiration date and the total traffic volume and the traffic volume consumed, can be seen.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: In this menu, you can turn the filter breaker on or off with the Enable anti-censorship button.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text: In this menu, you can specify how to run proxies (configs), which includes 3 main sections.

docs.title: Rule
docs.text: This mode executes proxies based on the rules in the imported profile, which contains several sections.

docs.title: PROXY
docs.text: This subsection executes the proxies in the profile and connects to the first config that pings.

docs.title: automatic
docs.text: In this case, it connects to the best configuration that has a lower ping.

docs.title: sequential
docs.text: In this case, the proxies are connected in turn, that is, the load is divided in a way, but the main difference with Load-balance is that in Load-balance, it is connected to several configurations at the same time, but in this case, it is connected to one configuration at the moment.

docs.title: Sort by location
docs.text: By using button number 1, you can sort the configurations based on location.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: You can test connections by using button number 2.

docs.title: Global
docs.text: This mode is for manual configuration selection and is useful when you want to use a specific configuration.

docs.title: Sort by location
docs.text: By using button number 1, you can sort the configurations based on location.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: You can test connections by using button number 2.

docs.title: Direct
docs.text: This mode sends the traffic directly to the Internet and the traffic does not pass through the filter breaker.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
In this menu, the general settings of the software are made.

  • Button number 1 or TUN Mode is for tunneling the entire system traffic.

Note: To activate this button, the software must be run with admin access in Windows, i.e. Run as Administrator. It should also be run on Mac and Linux with admin or root access.

  • Button number 2 activates the proxy system and is used for software that has proxy capabilities. That is, after activating this button, you should be able to connect to the filter breaker in the proxy section of the software on IP 127.0.0.1 and the default port of the program is 7890.

This mode is useful when you don't want to pass all your traffic through the VPN.

  • Button number 3 or Auto Launch runs the software automatically after the system boots up.

  • Button number 4 or Silent Start makes the software run inconspicuously and its icon is displayed in the task bar.

  • You can turn off IP version 6 using button number 5.

  • In section 6, you can determine the software port, the default of which is 7890.

  • In section 7, you can determine the core of the software, the default of which is Clash Meta.

  • In section number 8, you can determine the language.

  • In section number 9, you can change the theme related to the software.

  • The software version can be seen in section 10.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: In this section, the connections established in the software are displayed. That is, if a program uses a filter, it will be displayed in this section, which is very useful for troubleshooting.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: This menu is related to the rules in the imported profile, which can be seen in this file.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: In this section, the log related to the software can be seen, which is very useful during troubleshooting.

docs.title: Traffic graph
docs.text: In the specified section below, the graphic related to the traffic passing through the filter breaker is also displayed.

docs.title: Tutorial for HiddifyN software
docs.text:
HiddifyN is no longer developed

HiddifyN is an old Hiddify app. It is no longer developed or updated, and new protocols and features of Hiddify Manager may not work in it. The Hiddify app replaces it, on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux: see how to install the Hiddify app. This page is kept for people who still use HiddifyN.

This software is developed based on Xray and has many features that will be reviewed below.

docs.title: Software download
docs.text: To download the program in your user panel, open the desktop tab and open the section related to HiddifyN and then click on the Windows icon (button number 3) to download the program.

docs.title: Software installation
docs.text: Installing the program is very simple. Just install the Runtime 6 program first and then extract the downloaded file and run the HiddifyN file in the corresponding folder.

docs.title: Add a profile to the app
docs.text: In the user panel, go to the HiddifyN section again and Click to import so that the configurations are automatically added to the program.

docs.title: Proxy modes
docs.text: One of the most important parts of this application is the proxy modes, which will be explained about each part below.

docs.title: Auto/Smart
docs.text: It will automatically connect to the configuration with the highest speed (lowest ping).

docs.title: Load-Balance
docs.text: It connects to several configs at the same time and traffic is distributed between them. This mode is very useful when you have several configurations with dirty IP, by spreading the load on several configurations at the same time, an acceptable speed is obtained.

docs.title: Manual
docs.text: It is used to set the configs manually. By clicking on it, the advanced settings of the program will be returned, which will be explained further.

docs.title: Changing the language of the software
docs.text: To change the language of the software, click on the menu shown in the image below and select the language. Then close the program once and open it again.

docs.title: Changing the theme of the software
docs.text: Click on the specified button to change the software theme.

docs.title: User profile information
docs.text:
In the section displayed below, the information related to the imported user profile is displayed, including the expiration time and the total traffic as well as the consumed package.

In this section, you can also add new profiles manually. Just click on Import and add the user to the copied link from the panel.

docs.title: Connection to the VPN
docs.text: You need to click on the middle circular button to connect to the app. The software connects to the configurations based on the selected proxy mode, and the ping related to the configuration is displayed next to this button.

docs.title: Advanced settings
docs.text:
This section is opened by pressing the Manual button in the proxy mode section.

The advanced settings of the program are located in this section.

In this subsection, there are optional settings of the program, which includes several different sections.

  • Core: basic settings

that do not need to be changed for everyday use. The only widely used option is the port used for the program, which can be changed in this section.

If you need to use proxy, you can set socks5 proxy on this port.

*V2rayN Settings

This section contains the default settings of the V2rayN program, which is the main basis of the HIddifyN program.

  • which Start on boot runs the program when the system boots.
  • Auto hide startup automatically hides the program running at the beginning of the work, and only the program icon is visible in the Notification Area.
  • Check for pre release update gives unofficial updates to the program.
  • Also, in the settings you see in the picture below, which of course are not used for everyday use.

  • System proxy settings

This section shows the settings related to the proxy system.

  • Tun mode settings

This section contains Tun mode settings that do not need to be changed for everyday use.

  • Core type settings

In this section, you can set kernels for different protocols, the default of which is Xray.

docs.title: Routing setting
docs.text: In this section, you can view the routing related to the profile imported to the program and make changes to it if needed. But it is suggested not to touch it if possible.

docs.title: DNS setting
docs.text: In this section, you can enter your desired DNS into the software.

docs.title: Reboot as administrator
docs.text: With this option, you can restart the program and open it with admin access, which is required to use Tun mode.

docs.title: 2. Reload
docs.text: This button is used to reload the program core.

docs.title: 3. Channel
docs.text: By pressing this button, you will be redirected to our Telegram channel.

docs.title: 4. Check Update
docs.text: You can check program updates using this button.

docs.title: 5. Servers
docs.text: In this section, you can enter manual configurations.

docs.title: 6. Subs group
docs.text: This section is related to subscription links. By pressing this button, you can see the links added to the program and edit them.

docs.title: 7. Configs imported into the program
docs.text: In this section, the configurations imported to the program can be seen.

docs.title: 8. Connection log
docs.text: In this section, the log related to connections to the filter breaker is displayed, which is very useful for troubleshooting.

docs.title: 9. Enable Tun
docs.text:
This button is used to enable Tun mode or tunneling the entire system traffic.

Note: To use this mode, the program must be run with admin access level, or in other words, Run as Administrator.

docs.title: 10. Current connection specifications
docs.text: In this section, the current connection specifications and its ping are displayed.

docs.title: Reality configs do not work
docs.text:
If Reality configs do not work, or show a ping of -1, after you add the subscription link, open the advanced settings and set TLS to 1.3:

Settings > Option Setting > v2rayN settings > Enable Security Protocol TLS v1.3

Then click Confirm.

docs.title: Better performance with pre-release updates
docs.text:
To keep the cores the program needs (Xray, sing-box) up to date and working better, go to the same place.

Turn on Check for pre-release update, then update the cores with Check update.

docs.title: Fix DNS leaks
docs.text:
• Turn on TunMode. It needs the sing-box core, so first download the sing-box core with the Check update button on the main page.
  • Then go to:

Settings > Option Setting > TunMode settings

  • Turn on Strict Route.
  • Set Stack to System.
  • Now turn on the TunMode button on the main page.

Note: to turn on TunMode, the program must be started with Run as administrator.

Note: if TunMode does not work for any reason, set Stack to gvisor.

docs.title: Send local sites directly, without the VPN
docs.text: Even with the panel's Lite (green) profile, you may want the traffic of other sites to go straight to them, without the VPN. There are two ways.

docs.title: With the System proxy settings
docs.text:
Go to:

Settings > Option Setting > v2rayN settings > System proxy settings

Type the addresses that should not go through the VPN. Separate them with ;.

Note: write tamin.ir, not https://tamin.ir.

docs.title: With the Routing settings
docs.text:
Go to:

Settings > Routing setting

When you import the Lite (green) profile, the rules for local sites are already added here. To do it by hand with your own sites:

  • Turn off Enable advanced function.
  • Choose direct domain or IP.
  • Type the domains you want. Separate several sites with ,.
  • With block domain or ip you can block the domains you choose.

docs.title: Tutorial for QV2ray software
docs.text:
Qv2ray is no longer maintained

Its developers stopped Qv2ray in August 2021 (the last release is v2.7.0, "The End"). It does not support newer protocols such as Reality, Hysteria2 or TUIC, and it gets no security fixes. We recommend the Hiddify app instead, on Windows, macOS and Linux: see how to install the Hiddify app. This page is kept for people who still use Qv2ray.

One of the programs that can be used to connect to Xray protocols on the desktop is the QV2ray program.

docs.title: Download software
docs.text:
• You can download this program from hhere.

  • Proceed here to download the Trojan plugin.

  • Copy the downloaded dll file of the plugin in the installation path of the QV2ray software in the Plugins folder. From within the software, in the Plugins section, by clicking on Open Local Plugin Folder, the mentioned path will be opened.

  • Close the software and run it again. In the Plugins path, an option called Trojan-GFW Plugins is added.

docs.title: Add subscription link
docs.text:
• Just go to your user section in the panel.
  • In the All Configurations section, copy the Subscription Link.
  • Enter the Groups section in the software.
  • In the Subscription Setting tab, enter your copied sub link in the Subscription Address field.
  • By clicking the Update subscription button at the bottom of the page, the configurations will be loaded into the program.

docs.title: Test connections
docs.text: • After loading the configurations in the previous step, you can take a connection test from them on the main page of the program.

docs.title: Update the subscription link
docs.text:
• Go to the Groups section
  • For automatic update, enter the desired value in the Update Interval section.
  • By clicking the Update subscription button at the bottom of the page, the configurations will be updated according to the latest information on the server.

docs.title: Tutorial for Fair VPN app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager subscription to the free Fair VPN app on iPhone and iPad, test the connections, and share your VPN with other devices.

Fair VPNv1.3.4iOS 12+FreeNov 2026

Download on theApp Store

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Fair VPN from the App Store. It is free.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). A config is the settings for one connection to the server.

docs.title: Get your subscription link
docs.text:
On the user page, tap the big round button. At the bottom of the window, under Import Manually, Copy Link copies your subscription link. This app is not in the user page’s app list, so use this button.

Fair VPN is not in the app list on the HiddifyManager user page, so you add the link by hand.

  1. Open your user page link.
  2. Open the menu and tap All Configs.
  3. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link b64 and tap Get Link. A small window opens with a QR code and a Copy Link button.

Note

The screenshots of the user page come from an older panel version. The current page looks different, but the link is the same.

Now you can either copy the link or scan its QR code.

docs.title: Option 1: Copy the link
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.

  2. Open Fair VPN. In the VPN tab, tap Import VPN Configs.

  3. Paste the link and tap OK.

After a few seconds, your configs appear in the app.

docs.title: Option 2: Scan the QR code
docs.text:
Use this if the user page is open on another screen, such as a computer.

  1. In Fair VPN, open the VPN tab and tap Add VPN by QR Code in the bottom menu.

  2. Point your phone's camera at the QR code on the user page. The configs are added, just as with option 1.

docs.title: Test the connections
docs.text:
1. Tap Test VPN Latency.
  2. Tap Test Web Latency.

The app makes a real test through each config and shows the result next to it. Latency is how long a reply takes; lower is better.

docs.title: Sort configs by test result
docs.text:
1. Tap Test VPN Latency.
  2. Tap Sort by Latency.

The configs are now sorted by their test result, best first.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text:
Fair VPN cannot refresh a subscription by itself. To get the latest configs:

  1. Tap Delete All VPN to remove all configs.
  2. Add the subscription link again, as shown above.

If your admin uses Auto CDN

To get a new clean IP, delete all configs with Delete All VPN. Then turn the VPN off, reload your user page, and add the subscription link again.

docs.title: Share your VPN with other devices
docs.text:
You can share your phone's VPN with another device on the same Wi-Fi network, for example a device that can't install a VPN app.

  1. In Fair VPN, turn on Local Sharing. The app shows an IP address and a port.

  2. On the other device, open its network proxy settings.

  3. Enter the IP address and port shown by Fair VPN, and save.

The other device now uses your phone's VPN connection.

docs.title: Tutorial for FoXray app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager subscription to the FoXray app on iPhone and iPad and how to use its main settings. FoXray comes from the team behind the WingsX app, and replaced WingsX after WingsX was removed from the App Store.

FoXray is no longer on the App Store

As of October 2026, FoXray's App Store page (id6448898396) no longer exists, so you can't install it any more. If you already have it, the steps below still describe how it works. For a new install, use the Hiddify app (App Store, see How to install Hiddify app) or another app from the iOS client list.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• FoXray already installed on your iPhone or iPad.
  • Your user page link. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). FoXray can refresh it later to get new settings from the server.

docs.title: Add your subscription link
docs.text:
1. Open your user page link.
  2. Open the menu and tap All Configs.
  3. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link b64 and tap Get Link.

  4. Tap Copy Link.

    The screenshot shows an older version of the user page, which had an iOS tab. The current page looks different.

  5. Open FoXray and tap Subscriptions in the bottom menu.

  6. Tap the + button.

  7. Type any name you like.

  8. Paste the link into the URL field.

  9. Tap Subscribe. Your configs are added to the app.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text: In the Subscriptions menu, tap the ↪️ icon. Your links are updated.

docs.title: Add a subscription with a QR code
docs.text:
1. In the FoXray menu, tap the QR code button.
  2. Point the camera at the QR code of the link or config. It is added to the app.

If the QR code is saved as a photo on your phone:

  1. In the FoXray menu, tap the photo button.
  2. Choose the photo. The configs are added.

docs.title: Add a single config
docs.text:
We don't recommend this, because a single config can't be updated. Use it only if you need to.

  1. On your user page, open All Configs and copy one config from Individual Configs.
  2. In FoXray, tap the Clipboard icon in the FoXray menu. The copied config is added.

docs.title: Test the connections
docs.text:
First choose the test type:

  1. Go to Setting, then the Speed Test section.
  2. Under PingType, choose TCPPing, TLSPing or RealPing. RealPing gives the most realistic result.

Then, on the main page of the app, tap the connection test icon.

docs.title: Limit memory use
docs.text: Go to Setting, then ToolBox, and turn on Limit Memory Usage.

docs.title: Add a DNS server
docs.text:
A DNS server turns website names into IP addresses.

  1. In the FoXray menu, open the DNS section.
  2. Tap +.
  3. Type any name.
  4. Enter the DNS address you want in the Default DNS Address field.
  5. Leave the other fields as they are and save.

docs.title: Premium features
docs.text: The following features are only available if you bought the premium version of the app.

docs.title: Update subscriptions automatically
docs.text: Go to Setting and turn on Auto Update Subscription.

docs.title: Always On
docs.text: Go to Setting, then Pro ToolBox, and turn on Always On. Your VPN then stays on all the time.

docs.title: Show the server location
docs.text: In Setting → Pro ToolBox, turn on Show Location. After you connect, the app shows where the server is.

docs.title: Pin the connected config
docs.text: In Setting → Pro ToolBox, turn on Pin Outbound. The connected config is pinned to the top of the main page.

docs.title: Test configs before connecting
docs.text: In Setting → Pro ToolBox, turn on Test Outbound before Start. The app tests the configs before it connects.

docs.title: Turn on fragment
docs.text:
Fragment splits the first TLS packet into small pieces, which can help get past filtering. Read more in How the TLS trick works.

  1. Tap the connection in the app.
  2. Turn on Fragment.

  3. Enter these suggested values:

    packets: tlshello
length: 100-200
interval: 10-20

Depending on your internet provider, you may need other values. You can also change the packet type from tlshello to TCP segments 1-3, although filtering may detect this mode sooner:

packets: 1-3

docs.title: Tutorial for ShadowRocket app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager subscription to Shadowrocket on iPhone and iPad, and how to use its most useful settings. Shadowrocket is a paid app that works with Xray-based configs.

Shadowrocketv2.2.93iOS 13+PaidNov 2026

Download on theApp Store

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Buy and install Shadowrocket from the App Store.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). Shadowrocket can refresh it later to get new settings from the server.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.

  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap Shadowrocket. If you don't see it, tap View More. You can also download the app from here.

  4. Tap Import To App. Shadowrocket opens and adds your subscription.

If that doesn't work, add the link by hand as shown below.

Lite and Normal configs no longer exist

Older versions of the user page offered two kinds of configs in an iOS tab: Lite (only blocked sites go through the VPN) and Normal (all traffic goes through the VPN). The current user page has no iOS tab and no Lite/Normal choice. If you want local sites to open without the VPN, ask your admin; this is set on the server. If your admin turned on WARP, local sites can open through WARP.

docs.title: Add your subscription by hand
docs.text:
First get the link:

  1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link and tap Get Link. A window with a QR code and a Copy Link button opens.

Then add it to Shadowrocket in one of two ways.

docs.title: Copy and paste the link
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.

  2. Open Shadowrocket and tap the + button in the top-right corner.

  3. Set Type to Subscribe.

  4. Paste the link into the URL field.

  5. Tap Save.

All your configs now load in the app.

docs.title: Scan the QR code
docs.text:
1. On the Shadowrocket home screen, tap the scanner button.

  2. Scan the QR code shown on your user page. Your configs are added to the app.

docs.title: Test the configs
docs.text:
On the home screen, tap Connectivity Test. The app tests each config.

For more realistic results:

  1. Tap Settings in the bottom menu.
  2. Set Test Method to Connect.
  3. Run the test again.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text: Tap the update icon above the configs of a subscription. The configs are updated with the latest settings from the server.

docs.title: Subscription settings
docs.text: Go to Settings and tap Subscribe near the bottom. Here you can set:

docs.title: Update when the app opens
docs.text: Turn on Update on Open.

docs.title: Update automatically in the background
docs.text: Turn on Auto Background Update. The app then refreshes your subscriptions at regular intervals.

docs.title: Sort by ping
docs.text: Turn on Sort by ping to list the configs by their test result, best first.

docs.title: Prevent IP leaks
docs.text:
An IP leak means a website can see your real IP address even though the VPN is on.

  1. Go to Settings, then UDP.
  2. Turn on Disable STUN.

docs.title: Fix missing sound in some apps
docs.text:
If some apps (for example Clubhouse) play no sound:

  1. Go to Settings, then TCP.
  2. Change the Fingerprint value.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text: Go to Settings, then Shortcuts. Here you can set a voice command for an action, for example to start the VPN.

docs.title: Keep the VPN on (On Demand)
docs.text: Go to Settings, then On Demand.

docs.title: Always On
docs.text: When this is on, your VPN always stays on.

docs.title: On Demand
docs.text: When this is on and your connection drops, Shadowrocket blocks all internet traffic so your real IP address is not exposed.

docs.title: Disconnect on Sleep
docs.text: When this is on, the VPN disconnects when the phone goes to sleep.

docs.title: Share your VPN with other devices
docs.text:
You can share your VPN with another device on the same network, for example a device that can't install a VPN app.

  1. Go to Settings, then Proxy.
  2. Tap Proxy Share.

  3. Turn on Enable Share. The app shows an IP address and a port.

  4. On the other device, open its network proxy settings and enter that IP address and port.

The other device now uses your VPN without installing anything.

docs.title: Create a load balancer
docs.text:
A load balancer spreads your traffic over several configs, so one slow or blocked config doesn't stop you.

  1. On the home screen, hold your finger on the screen and swipe down. A hidden menu opens.

  2. Tap the + button.

  3. Type any name.

  4. Set Type to load-balance.
  5. Under Policy, select the configs to use: the ones with the best ping, or all of them.
  6. Leave Interval (time between tests) and Timeout (how long a config may fail and still count as working) at their default values, unless you know what you need.

  7. Tap Save.

  8. Tap the new load balancer, then tap Test. This tests it and connects through it.

When you turn Shadowrocket on or off, the load balancer turns on or off with it.

docs.title: Fix sites or apps that don't open
docs.text:
If some sites or apps don't open, or Telegram GIFs don't load:

  1. Go to Settings.
  2. Open TCP.
  3. Set TLS to Network.
  4. Set Fingerprint to Safari15_5.
  5. Set Max Read Length to 16384.
  6. Go back to Home.
  7. Set Global Routing to Proxy.

docs.title: Tutorial for SingBox app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager subscription to the official sing-box app on iPhone and iPad, and how to connect. It is for users of a Hiddify Manager server who want to use sing-box instead of the Hiddify app.

This page used to be about the SSH proxy

Older versions of this page showed how to add the HiddifyManager panel's SSH proxy to sing-box. The SSH proxy service was removed in Hiddify Manager v13, so that part no longer applies. The steps below add your normal HiddifyManager subscription instead.

sing-boxv1.14.8iOS 15+FreeNov 2026

Download on theApp Store

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• An iPhone or iPad with iOS 15 or later.
  • Your user page link. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page, where your subscription links are.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). The app can refresh it later to get new settings from the server.

docs.title: Download the app
docs.text:
The official sing-box app for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV is now called sing-box MT. The old App Store listing (id6451272673) no longer exists.

  • iOS / iPadOS (App Store: sing-box MT)
  • Android (Google Play)
  • Other platforms: see the official sing-box download page.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.

  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap sing-box. If you don't see it, tap View More.

  4. Tap Import To App. The sing-box app opens and asks to add the profile.

  5. Confirm. The new profile now appears in the app's Profiles list.

If the app doesn't open, use the manual way below.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the manual way
docs.text:
1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Hiddify / Singbox and tap Get Link.
  3. Tap Copy Link.

  4. Open the sing-box app and go to the Profiles menu.

  5. Tap New Profile.

  6. Set Type to Remote.

  7. Type any name you like in the Name field.

  8. Paste the link you copied into the URL field.

  9. Tap Create.

The profile now appears in the list of profiles.

Note

The screenshots on this page come from an older version of sing-box. Menu names in the current app may look slightly different.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Go to the Dashboard menu.
  2. Select the profile you added.
  3. Turn on the Enabled switch. If iOS asks to add a VPN configuration, tap Allow.

When it works, the VPN icon appears at the top of your iPhone screen and websites open normally. If it doesn't connect, go back to Profiles, update the profile, and try again. If it still fails, ask your server admin to check your account.

docs.title: Tutorial for Stash app
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager profile to Stash on iPhone and iPad and how to use its main modes. Stash is a paid app based on Clash.

Stashv5.0.0iOS 16+PaidNov 2026

Download on theApp Store

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Buy and install Stash from the App Store. The App Store lists iOS 16 or later.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page.

In Stash, a profile is a file (in YAML format) that holds all your connections (configs) and the rules for which traffic goes through the VPN.

docs.title: Add your profile: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.

  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap Stash. If you don't see it, tap View More. You can also download the app from here.

  4. Tap Import To App. Stash opens and adds your profile.

If that doesn't work, add the profile by hand as shown below.

Lite and Normal profiles no longer exist

Older versions of the user page had an iOS tab with two Stash profiles: a green Lite profile (only blocked sites go through the VPN) and an orange Normal profile (all traffic goes through the VPN). The current panel offers a single Clash Meta subscription instead. If you want local sites to open without the VPN, ask your admin; this is set on the server.

docs.title: Add your profile by hand
docs.text:
First get the link:

  1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Clash Meta and tap Get Link. A window with a QR code and a Copy Link button opens.

docs.title: Copy the link into Stash
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.
  2. Open Stash. On the Settings page, tap Config File.

  3. Tap Download from URL.

  4. Paste the link and tap Download. The profile is added to the app.

docs.title: Add the profile with a QR code
docs.text:
1. Keep the QR code from the user page on screen (for example on a computer).
  2. Open Stash. On the Settings page, tap Config File.

  3. Tap Download from QRcode.

  4. Scan the QR code. The profile is added to the app.

docs.title: The Policy menu
docs.text:
This menu shows the policies, that is the configs in the profiles you imported.

Each mode in the Policy menu works together with a mode in the Outbound section, which is explained further down.

docs.title: Proxy mode
docs.text: Uses one config that you choose. It is used with the Global outbound mode.

docs.title: Automatic mode
docs.text: The app connects to the config with the best test result. It is used with the Rule outbound mode.

docs.title: Sequential mode
docs.text: The app uses the configs one after another, switching from time to time. This spreads the load over time. It is different from load-balance mode, which uses several configs at the same time. It is used with the Rule outbound mode.

docs.title: Auto mode
docs.text: The automatic config selection used by Automatic mode.

docs.title: Load-Balance mode
docs.text: Uses several connections at the same time, which spreads the load over them. This can help when the server's IP is partly blocked and single connections work badly. It is used with the Rule outbound mode.

docs.title: Connection test
docs.text: Tap the lightning icon to test the connections.

docs.title: Update your profiles
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings, then Config File.
  2. Hold your finger on a profile.
  3. In the menu that appears, tap Update Now.

docs.title: Update your profiles automatically
docs.text:
1. In Settings, tap More Settings.

  2. In the CONFIG FILE section, set the time between updates in Update Interval.

  3. Turn on Auto Update.

Stash also updates your profiles each time you open the app.

docs.title: Choose the Outbound mode
docs.text: On the Home page of the app, the Outbound section has three modes.

docs.title: Rule mode
docs.text: Uses the rules in the profile to decide which traffic goes through the VPN. For example, if the profile has rules for local sites, their traffic does not go through the VPN.

docs.title: Global mode
docs.text: Ignores the rules. You pick one config in the Policy menu under Proxy mode, and all your phone's traffic goes through it. This is useful when you want to use one specific config.

docs.title: Direct mode
docs.text: Nothing goes through the VPN. It is as if the VPN were off.

docs.title: On Demand
docs.text: Go to Settings, then On Demand.

docs.title: Always On
docs.text: When this is on, your VPN is always on.

docs.title: On Demand
docs.text: When this is on, the VPN is active only while the phone is unlocked and turns off at other times.

docs.title: Troubleshoot connections
docs.text: To see more details about your connections, open the Utilities menu and tap Network Diagnosis. It shows a log of all connections, which helps you find problems. The Connectivity and Proxy subsections are the most useful.
