docs.title: Tutorial for Streisand
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager subscription to the free Streisand app on iPhone and iPad, test the connections, and use its most useful settings: DNS and TLS fragment. Streisand works on iOS 14 and later.

Streisandv1.7.1iOS 15+FreeNov 2026

Download on theApp Store

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Streisand from the App Store. It is free.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). A config is the settings for one connection to the server. Streisand can refresh the subscription later to get new configs from the server.

Note

The user page pictures are current (Hiddify Manager v14.5). The app screenshots come from older versions of the app; the current screens look a little different, but the steps are the same. The current screens look different, but the steps are the same.

docs.title: Add your subscription: the quick way
docs.text:
1. On your iPhone, open your user page link in Safari.
  2. Tap the large round button in the middle of the page. A window called Configure your VPN opens.

  3. Under Choose one of the apps below, tap Streisand. If you don't see it, tap View More. You can also download the app from here.

  4. Tap Import To App. Streisand opens and adds your subscription.

If that doesn't work, add the link by hand as shown below.

docs.title: Add your subscription by hand
docs.text:
First get the link:

  1. On your user page, open the menu and tap All Configs.
  2. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link and tap Get Link. A window with a QR code and a Copy Link button opens.

Then add it to Streisand in one of two ways.

docs.title: Copy and paste the link
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.

  2. Open Streisand and tap the + button. Streisand reads the link from the clipboard, adds the subscription and loads your configs.

docs.title: Scan the QR code
docs.text:
Use this if the user page is open on another screen, such as a computer.

  1. Show the QR code of the subscription link on the other screen.

  2. In Streisand, tap +, then Scan QRCode, and point the camera at the QR code. The subscription is added and your configs load.

docs.title: Test, update and manage the subscription
docs.text:
Touch and hold the subscription in Streisand. A menu opens with these options:

  • Latency: tests each config with a real connection. This is the most useful test. Lower is better.
  • TCP Ping: only checks that the server's port answers. It is quick, but a config can pass it and still not work.
  • ICMP Ping: a normal ping to the server. Many servers don't answer it, so a failed ICMP ping does not mean the config is broken.
  • Update: gets the latest configs from the server. Do this when the admin changes something, or when configs stop working.
  • Edit: change the name or the link of the subscription.
  • Delete: remove the subscription and its configs.

To connect, tap a config that tested well, then turn on the switch on the main screen. The first time, iOS asks you to allow a VPN configuration; tap Allow.

docs.title: DNS settings
docs.text:
On the main screen, open the DNS settings. Here you choose which DNS server Streisand uses to look up website addresses, and how it talks to it:

  • DoH (DNS over HTTPS): DNS requests are encrypted and look like normal web traffic. Usually the best choice.
  • DoT (DNS over TLS): DNS requests are encrypted with TLS, on a separate port (853). Easier to block than DoH.
  • DoU (DNS over UDP): plain, unencrypted DNS. Your internet provider can see and change it, so use it only if the others don't work.

docs.title: App settings
docs.text:
The Settings page has the general settings of the app:

  • Import Configuration: load a Streisand settings file from your device.
  • Export Configuration: save your Streisand settings to a file, for example to move them to another device.

  • Subscription: turn on Update On Open so that your subscriptions update every time you open the app.

  • Reset: set the app's settings back to the defaults.

docs.title: Turn on TLS fragment
docs.text:
Fragment splits the first packet of a TLS connection into small pieces, so the filter has a harder time reading the website name in it. It can help when TLS configs don't connect. To learn more, see How the TLS trick works.

  1. Tap the config to open its settings.
  2. Turn on Fragment.

  3. Enter these values as a starting point:

    packets: tlshello
length: 100-200
interval: 10-20

The best values depend on your internet provider. If it doesn't help, try other lengths and intervals, or set packets to 1-3 (the first three TCP segments) instead of tlshello. The 1-3 mode may be detected by the filter sooner.

docs.text:
This page shows you how to add your HiddifyManager subscription to the free V2Box app on iPhone and iPad, test the connections, connect, and keep your configs up to date. V2Box works with Xray-based configs.

V2Boxv10.2.0iOS 15+FreeNov 2026

Download on theApp Store

Our suggestion: the Hiddify appFree, simpler, and supports every Hiddify Manager protocolInstall →

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install V2Box from the App Store. It is free.
  • Have your user page link ready. This is the link your server admin sent you. It opens your personal HiddifyManager page.

A subscription link is one link that holds all your connection settings (configs). A config is the settings for one connection to the server.

Note

The user page pictures are current (Hiddify Manager v14.5). The app screenshots come from older versions of the app; the current screens look a little different, but the steps are the same. The current screens look different, but the steps are the same.

docs.title: Get your subscription link
docs.text:
On the user page, tap the big round button. At the bottom of the window, under Import Manually, Copy Link copies your subscription link. This app is not in the user page’s app list, so use this button.

V2Box is not in the app list on the HiddifyManager user page, so you add the link by hand.

  1. Open your user page link.
  2. Open the menu and tap All Configs.
  3. In the Subscription Links section, find Subscription link b64 and tap Get Link. A small window opens with a QR code and a Copy Link button.

Now you can either copy the link or scan its QR code.

docs.title: Option 1: Copy the link
docs.text:
1. Tap Copy Link.

  2. Open V2Box and tap Configs in the bottom menu.

  3. Tap the + button.

  4. Tap Add Subscription.

  5. Type any name, for example the name of your server, and paste the link into the URL field.

  6. Tap Add Subscribe. Your configs appear in the list, and V2Box tests them by itself.

docs.title: Option 2: Scan the QR code
docs.text:
Use this if the user page is open on another screen, such as a computer.

  1. In V2Box, open Configs and tap +.
  2. Tap Scan QR.
  3. Point your phone's camera at the QR code on the user page. The configs are added and tested, just as with option 1.

docs.title: Test the connections
docs.text: In the Configs list, tap Ping All. The result appears next to each config. Lower numbers are better; a config with an error or a timeout does not work right now.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. In Configs, tap a config that tested well to select it.
  2. Go to Home and slide the button at the bottom to the right. The first time, iOS asks you to allow a VPN configuration; tap Allow.

While you are connected, the Home screen shows your upload, download and memory use.

docs.title: Update your subscription
docs.text:
When the admin changes something on the server, update the subscription to get the new configs:

  1. In Configs, tap +.
  2. Tap Update All Subscriptions.

To let V2Box update by itself, tap the menu (three lines) at the top of the Configs screen and turn on Auto Update.

docs.title: Add a single config
docs.text: You can also add one config instead of the whole subscription: copy the config link, then in Configs tap + and Import V2ray URL from Clipboard. This is not recommended, because a single config is not updated when the server changes.

docs.title: If it doesn't connect
docs.text:
• Update the subscription and test again. Pick another config that shows a good result.
  • Some configs, for example those using newer protocols, may not work in V2Box. Try the Hiddify app.
  • See Troubleshooting connectivity issues.

docs.text: These guides explain the settings of the Hiddify Manager admin panel: WARP, Reality, the Telegram proxy and bot, backups, updates and more. Choose a guide from the menu.

docs.title: Automatic config health checks on Hiddify Manager
Automatic config health checks on Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The pictures and steps on this page are from Hiddify Manager v14.5.

A user's subscription link has many configs: one for each protocol, transport and domain. If one of them is broken (a wrong template, a core that rejects it, a missing inbound), it does not work for anyone, and users only see "it does not connect".

Config Health finds these configs for you. The panel tests every config of a subscription from the server itself, the same way the apps get it, and shows which ones work.

What it does not test

The test runs on your server, not in Iran. A config that works here can still be blocked by filtering in your users' country. But a config that fails here never works for anyone, so these are the ones to fix first.

docs.title: The Config Health card
docs.text:
The card is on the Dashboard.

  1. Check now: runs a check right away. It takes a minute or two; meanwhile the button says Checking…. This button always works, even when the automatic checks are off.
  2. Disable failing: turns off, for every user, the configs that fail in both kinds of apps. It is greyed out until a check finds such configs (configs that work in at least one kind of app stay on). You see the list and confirm before anything changes.
  3. Restore: turns back on the configs that Disable failing (or the config tester) turned off.

  4. The result for each kind of app:

    • Hiddify / Sing-Box: the subscription as the Hiddify app gets it.
    • XRay (v2rayN, v2rayNG, Happ, …): the subscription as the Xray apps get it.

    For example, 99 of 142 work means 43 configs failed.

The test uses the subscription of one active user (the card says whose) and checks that traffic really gets out to the internet through each config.

docs.title: See which configs fail
docs.text:
Click a line with failures to open its list.

For each config you see its name, the reason in plain words, and the technical message. The reasons:

Reason What it usually means It connects, but traffic does not get out to the internet The config reaches the server, but the server cannot send the traffic on: check the outbound it uses (for example WARP or an IPv6-only exit) No answer in time The server, or that port or protocol, did not answer The connection was refused Nothing listens on that port: the protocol or inbound is off or broken The server closed the connection The server accepted and then dropped it: often a wrong setting of that protocol The TLS handshake failed A certificate or TLS (SNI, Reality) problem on that domain

In the picture, the failing configs shown are IPv6 configs (their names end with IP6): on this test server, configs that use IPv6 do not get out to the internet. In such a case, check the server's IPv6, or turn off the IPv6 configs.

If the whole check could not run, the card says why instead, for example: the panel could not open its own subscription because the certificate of the domain is not valid, the domain could not be found, or it did not answer in time. Each message says what to check; Technical details shows the exact error.

docs.title: Turn on the automatic checks
docs.text:
By default only Check now works. To check automatically:

  1. Open Settings → General Settings. This is an advanced setting: click Show advanced settings if you do not see it.
  2. Turn on Automatic config health checks (1).

  1. Save.

Then the panel checks after every start of the panel and every 6 hours. A config that fails is tested again after a short time, so a moment's hiccup is not reported. When configs fail in two checks in a row, the super admins get a message from the Telegram bot (if the bot is set up), and the Dashboard shows a notice such as 12 of 142 configs do not work from the server.

Why it is off by default

Each check starts a client for every config and connects through it to your own server: on a big subscription that is hundreds of connections in a few minutes. Some hosting providers take this for an attack (a flood) and can suspend the server. Turn the automatic checks on only if your provider is fine with that; otherwise use Check now when you need it.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• After you change protocols, domains or the proxy templates, press Check now to see that every config still works.
  • To test any subscription link (also one from another panel) from the server, use Tools → Config Tester.

docs.title: How to Reset HiddifyManager to default
How to Reset HiddifyManager to default
docs.text:
This guide brings HiddifyManager back to the state of a fresh install: the panel, its database, users, domains and settings are all removed, and you start again from the quick setup. It is written for Hiddify Manager v14.5.

Do you really need a full reset?

  • You forgot the admin password: no reset needed. Run hiddify reset-password on the server (see below).
  • Something misbehaves: first try Actions › Restart or Reinstall in the panel. Neither of them deletes your users or settings.
  • You want to move to a new server: make a backup on the old one and restore it on the new one (Backup and restore).

docs.title: Before you start: make a backup
docs.text: A full reset cannot be undone. In the panel, open Backup and click Download Backup, then keep the file somewhere safe. With it you can bring everything back later. More: How to backup and restore HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Full reset
docs.text:
1. Connect to your server with SSH.

  2. Open the HiddifyManager menu with this command (it may already be open when you log in):

    hiddify

  3. Choose advanced (Uninstall, Remote Assistant, Downgrade,...), then purge (Uninstall completely and remove database). It stops and removes every Hiddify service, the panel and its database.

    Warning

    purge also removes the MariaDB database server and everything in /opt/hiddify-manager. Do not use it on a server where other programs keep their data in MariaDB.

  4. Install HiddifyManager again with the install command:

    bash <(curl https://i.hiddify.com/release)

  5. When the install finishes, open one of the new admin links it shows. The panel starts with the Quick setup wizard, exactly like after the first install. See Main installation guide.

To restore your old data instead of starting empty, open Backup in the new panel and drop your backup file on Restore.

docs.title: Reset only the admin password
docs.text:
If you only lost the admin password, run this on the server:

hiddify reset-password

The owner's password is cleared. Sign in on one of the admin links with an empty password (the command hiddify admin shows the links), then set a new password on the Admins page or in My account.

docs.title: How to activate WARP on HiddifyManager
How to activate WARP on the HiddifyManager panel
docs.text: Many websites, including Google, restrict the access of users through VPN. Because several different connections go from the same IP to Google's server at the same time, this behavior is similar to cyber malicious behavior, and because of this, the connection is disrupted, and Google gives a 403 error, for example. Other websites do not allow communication and use of the service. Here is one way to solve the problem using Cloudflare's WARP service.

docs.title: What is WARP?
docs.text:
Warp is a Cloudflare service that provides secure and encrypted communication over its network. After performing security checks on the target client and making sure there is no malicious behavior, it opens the connection to the Internet. It assigns an IP to that system and communicates through it. In fact, Warp is a tool that hides your server IP from the sites that your users visit. Because the IP of the server is hidden, so access is established.

The free WARP service has no traffic limit. WARP+ (with a paid key from the 1.1.1.1 app) is optional: it routes traffic through Cloudflare's faster network. HiddifyManager can use both.

This guide is for Hiddify Manager v14.5. Since v14.5, WARP is one of the panel's Outbounds: you can turn it on in Settings (the simple way, below) or choose exactly which sites go through it on the Outbounds page.

docs.title: Setting up WARP on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
Click Settings in the panel sidebar and find the WARP card. (You can also type "WARP" in the search box at the top of the page.)

  1. Choose a WARP+ Mode other than Disable.
  2. The first time, the panel shows Cloudflare WARP terms: traffic that leaves through WARP is handled by Cloudflare under their Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Read them, tick the box and click Accept. Until you accept, WARP does not run.
  3. Save the settings, then click Apply now on the Actions page (or in the banner that appears) so WARP starts.

To use WARP Plus, enter its key in the Warp Plus Key field (an advanced setting: turn on Show Advanced Settings at the top of the page); you can buy the original key from Cloudflare in the 1.1.1.1 app. There are also different bots in Telegram that give you this key, but none of them are approved by us.

In Additional WARP Sites (also advanced) you can add more sites that should pass through WARP. Since v14.5 the same list is on the Outbounds page (see below), which is the easier place to edit it.

docs.title: Mode "All"
docs.text: It passes all traffic through the warp, even the sites that don't have problems pass through the warp. On the Outbounds page this makes WARP the default outbound (the last one).

docs.title: Mode "Only Domestic and Blocked Sites"
docs.text:
Only domestic sites and Google, Spotify, Netflix, OpenAI, ipinfo.io (and the other sites in WARP's lists) use Warp. Everything else leaves directly.

  • Note: If there is an error in the Warp Plus key, the WARP will be disabled. So make sure to use the key correctly. Select and copy the key correctly and place it in the field.

docs.title: The Outbounds page
docs.text:
Click Outbounds in the sidebar. Each row is a way out of the server: Block, WARP, Direct (and any Socks, Tor or Psiphon exit you add). They are checked from top to bottom: a site leaves through the first outbound whose lists contain it, and the last enabled outbound (Default) gets everything else.

  1. The WARP row.
  2. Its switch turns WARP on or off (the same as the WARP+ Mode setting).
  3. The pencil opens What goes through it: add or remove sites, geosite: lists and rule-sets that should leave through WARP.

To send all traffic through WARP, drag the WARP row to the bottom so it becomes the default.

docs.title: How to check if warp is active or not?
docs.text:
Click Actions in the sidebar. On the Apply & Status page, click Check now in the Check Status card.

The status check shows whether each service is running, plus the server's public IP and the status of the warp connection with the IP allocated for the warp traffic. Its output is also kept in the status.log file in the Logs list at the bottom of the same page.

  • The status shows the WARP account and the IP, country and network (Cloudflare) that WARP traffic leaves from. The same output is in warp.log in the Logs list.

  • When the WARP outbound is off, no traffic goes through WARP, even if the WARP service itself is running.

  • On the server, the HiddifyManager menu has the same check: run hiddify, then advanced › warp (Check Warp Status).

You can also use the ipinfo site. If the IP displayed on this page belongs to Cloudflare despite the filter breaker being turned on; In this case, the warp is activated correctly.

You can also use the ip.gs website, and if Cloudflare's IP is displayed, it means that Warp is activated.

docs.title: How to reinstall WARP service?
docs.text:
From the panel: click Actions in the sidebar and click Reinstall. This reinstalls all HiddifyManager services, WARP included. It does not delete your users or settings, but all users are disconnected for a few minutes.

From the terminal (only WARP): if you only want to reinstall WARP, connect to your server with SSH, leave the HiddifyManager menu with Ctrl+C (or Cancel), and run:

cd /opt/hiddify-manager/services/warp && bash install.sh

docs.title: How to change IP WARP?
docs.text:
The panel has no button for this; it is done in the terminal.

  1. Connect to your server with SSH and leave the HiddifyManager menu with Ctrl+C (or Cancel).

  2. Run:

    cd /opt/hiddify-manager/services/warp && bash change_ip.sh

It registers a new WARP account, so WARP gives the server a new IP. Check the new IP with Check now on the Actions page, as shown above.

docs.title: How to backup and restore HiddifyManager
How to backup and restore panel on HiddifyManager
docs.text: Many times you need to backup the panel and restore it on another server. For example, your server is filtered or there is a problem that you cannot continue on that server. In this case, continue the following steps until the end to learn how to do this.

docs.title: Backup current panel via web
docs.text:
In the admin panel sidebar, under Settings, click Backup. In the Make a Backup card, click Download Backup.

The backup is one .json file with everything in it: settings, users, admins, domains, proxies and certificates. Choose where to save it on your computer. The file holds passwords, user links and private keys, so keep it somewhere safe.

You can also click Save on the server to keep a copy on the server, or Save on the Telegram to get the file from your Telegram bot.

docs.title: Sending the backup file to Telegram
docs.text: The panel automatically makes a backup for you every 6 hours, and if you have activated the Telegram bot, each automatic backup is also sent to you in the bot.

docs.title: Backups on the server
docs.text:
Automatic backups, and the ones you save with Save on the server, are listed in the Backups on the server card of the same page. For each backup you can download it, restore it, or delete it with the buttons on its row. Backups are also made when updating or reinstalling the panel.

Note: If for any reason the Telegram bot was not available to you and you were not able to backup via the web, you can access the previous backups of the system from the following path.

/opt/hiddify-manager/hiddify-panel/backup

and then transfer the file to your PC. More info here

Finally, keep the backup file somewhere safe on your computer.

docs.title: Restoring backup file
docs.text:
Now install the panel on the new server. When the Quick setup wizard opens, do not set anything up: click Skip for now.

In the sidebar, under Settings, click Backup.

In the Restore card, drop the backup file that you saved in the previous step, or click the box to choose it. Then choose which parts to restore: Settings, Users and Domains. For example, if you want to restore the entire panel, select all 3 options, click Restore and wait for the operation to finish. It takes a few minutes. If the backup comes from another panel, the admin link changes; the new links are shown when it finishes.

docs.title: Changing subdomain settings
docs.text:
After the restore, your domains and subdomains still point to the old server's IP. Where you manage your domain's DNS, change the records to the new server's IP. Only the IP changes; keep the record name and everything else as it is.

In Cloudflare:

  1. Sign in to the Cloudflare dashboard and choose your domain.
  2. In the sidebar, open DNS, then Records.
  3. Next to each record that points to the old server, click Edit.
  4. In IPv4 address, enter the new server's IP and click Save. If the new server has IPv6, change the AAAA records to its new IPv6 too.
  5. Keep Proxy status (the orange cloud) as it was. CDN domains stay Proxied and direct domains stay DNS only.

Other DNS services work the same way: find the A (and AAAA) records and change only the IP.

Tip

A DNS change usually takes a few minutes to reach everyone. If the panel does not open on the domain right away, wait a little.

The work is done. The panel comes up on the new server with your admin link. If the backup came from another panel, use the new links shown after the restore.

docs.title: How to configure HiddifyManager properly (Getting familiar with its different parts)
How to configure HiddifyManager properly
docs.text:
This page walks you through the first setup of the HiddifyManager admin panel and gives a tour of every menu, in the order of the panel's own menu. Each part says what the page is for and what matters most on it, and links to the full guide of that part. Read it right after you install the panel, or whenever you want to know what a menu or setting is for.

Written for HiddifyManager v14.5

The menu names and screenshots on this page are from HiddifyManager v14.5. Every option of the Settings page is listed, with the panel's own explanation, in All HiddifyManager settings, which is made from the panel's code for each release.

The panel makes running proxies easier, but it cannot fix a blocked server or a broken domain. If you finish this page and your users still cannot connect, read Troubleshooting connectivity issues.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  1. A server with a clean IP. A clean IP is one that is not blocked in your users' country. Check it with How to make sure the server's IP or domain is clean. If the IP is blocked, get a new IP or a new server.
  2. HiddifyManager installed, as described in the installation guide. At the end of the install you get your admin links. The admin link contains your secret path and your admin ID, so it works like a password. See the correct format of the admin link.
  3. A registered domain that is reachable. A domain is a name such as example.com that points to your server. See domain types and how to register them, then check that the domain is clean.

If a word on this page is new to you, see Basic concepts.

docs.title: Open the admin panel for the first time
docs.text:
• If you used a one-click install link from a provider such as Vultr or OVH, wait about 10 minutes. You then get a one-time link that opens the admin page.
  • If you installed over SSH, the admin links are printed in the terminal at the end of the install. Open one of the Secure (https, domain) links in your browser. Use the Not Secure IP link only if no domain link works.
  • If you lost the links, connect to your server over SSH and run:
hiddify admin

Your admin link has the form https://<domain>/<admin proxy path>/<admin UUID>/, for example https://sub.example.com/DrtGho0n4b8H9D/8bncvfb5-8193-vv76-ab97-4c35965l250m/. When you open it, the panel signs you in and opens Admin V2, the new admin panel, and the address in your browser changes to https://sub.example.com/DrtGho0n4b8H9D/admin/v2/. Keep the link private: it works like a password. See The correct format of the admin link.

The first time you open the admin page, the Quick setup wizard starts.

docs.title: Quick setup
docs.text:
The wizard has six short steps: Welcome → Password → Domains → Protocols → Nodes → Finish. Use Next and Back to move between them, or Skip for now to leave the wizard. You can change everything later in Settings.

  1. Welcome: choose the Admin panel language and the Country your users are in (Iran, China, Russia or Others). The country applies settings that suit its filtering.
  2. Password: set a password for the admin area (at least 8 characters).
  3. Domains: point your domain to the server IPs shown on the page (an A record for IPv4, AAAA for IPv6). Then type your domain and press Enter. The panel detects the domain type by itself; tap the type to change it. You need at least one direct, CDN or subscription-only domain.
  4. Protocols: pick the protocols you want to offer. Choose as few as you need.
  5. Nodes (optional): connect other HiddifyManager servers to manage them from this panel. You can skip this.
  6. Finish: review your choices and click Finish. The panel applies the configuration and reinstalls the services. This takes a few minutes. The log and your new admin links are shown while it runs.

When it finishes, the panel is ready to use. Copy the new admin links and keep them somewhere safe.

docs.title: The admin menu
docs.text:
The sidebar on the left has these groups. The sections below follow the same order.

  • Manager: Dashboard, Users, Admins, Inbox, Nodes and Tools (Config Tester, Scanner, Text Decoders, QR Code, SSH Terminal).
  • Settings: Domains, Protocols, Outbounds, Settings, Proxy Editor (Proxies, Base Configs, Templates, Template Variables), Backup, Actions (the Apply & Status page), Telegram Bot and API.
  • Help and Donation.

Your own account (password, passkeys, language and the defaults for your users) is under the person icon at the top: see My account.

Install the panel as an app

The first time you open the panel, it offers to install itself as an app on your phone or computer (Install the panel as an app). It then opens in its own window, one tap away. Tick Do not show this again if you don't want it.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard shows traffic, users and server health at a glance: online users, today's, this week's and this month's usage, and charts of usage and users over time (7, 30, 90 or 180 days). If you use several servers (nodes), pick one in the node filter. Further down, Config Health tests every config from the server, and Node Health shows CPU, RAM and network for each node. See Automatic config health checks.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Here you create an account for each person who will use your proxies.

  1. Open Users and click Add user.
  2. In the New user window, enter a Name (and, if you like, a Note that only admins see).
  3. Under Data, set the Usage limit (or pick 10 GB, 50 GB, 100 GB …) and the Reset period: Without reset, Monthly, Weekly or Daily.
  4. Under Time, set the Package length (or pick 1 week, 1 month, 3 months …). The days start at the user's first connection.
  5. Click Add user. The user's link and QR code open, ready to send.

Click Add user to open the New user window:

The Users page lists everyone with their usage, expiry date and last connection. Use the search box and the filters (Online, Active, Expiring soon, Low on data, …) to find users.

Each user has their own user page. Open it with the QR code button in the user's row, which shows the user's link. On the user page the user sees the remaining traffic and time and a big connect button. Tapping it opens Configure Your VPN, where the user picks an app or uses Copy Link. The menu of the user page also has All Configs, with every config of the user.

Under All Configs the user finds every config and subscription link:

You can give users access in three ways:

  1. The user page link (recommended). The user opens it and finds everything there.
  2. The subscription link. A subscription link is one address that the app re-reads to get the latest configs. If you change your settings, the user's app updates itself.
  3. A single config link. It does not update. If you change your settings, you must send the user a new link.

For help connecting client apps, see the client tutorials on the HiddifyManager tutorials page.

docs.title: Admins
docs.text:
Here you create accounts for other people who help you manage the panel. Click Add admin and fill in the form. The admins are shown as a tree: each admin's limits cover their own users and everyone below them. Each admin has an Admin link button.

There are three admin types:

  • Super admin: full access to the whole panel and all settings.
  • Admin: can manage users and some settings.
  • Agent: can only manage users.

For each admin you can:

  • limit the number of users and active users;
  • allow or forbid adding sub-admins;
  • reset their password.

Note

Each admin's link contains their secret ID. If you change it, that admin's panel address changes completely. See the correct format of the admin link.

Each admin can also set a password and passkeys, a default outbound, extra configs and a custom user page for their own users on their My account page: see My account.

docs.title: Inbox
docs.text:
The Inbox gathers the people who write to your Telegram bot, their requests for a free test, and the messages you send to your users. Here you make free test packages (a link that gives whoever opens it a test account, given automatically or after you approve it), answer conversations, and use Send Message to write to all your users, or to the active or expired ones, through the bot. It needs the Telegram bot.

Full guide: Inbox, free test packages and messages to users.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
Nodes are other HiddifyManager servers connected to this panel. Users and admins are shared with them automatically, so one account works on every server, and the usage of all servers is added up here. The page shows each node's state and lets you add, ping and manage them. The Dashboard can show each node on its own.

Full guide: Multi-server with nodes.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
The Tools menu has helpers that run from the panel:

  • Config Tester: runs every config of a subscription in its own core and checks that it connects.
  • Scanner: finds Cloudflare IPs that work on your internet (with Fragment and REALITY SNI tests too), to give to the users of your ISP.
  • Text Decoders: decodes and edits share links, subscriptions, Base64 and URLs, in your browser.
  • QR Code: makes a QR code from any text, or reads one with the camera or from an image.
  • SSH Terminal: opens a terminal on any server, and its files, right from the panel.

Full guide: The panel's tools.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text:
Open Domains (in the Settings group of the menu) to add or edit your domains. The list shows each domain with its mode, its TLS and certificate state, its custom proxies and Show configs of. The order matters: drag the handle to sort. Configs list domains in this order, and the first one is used for panel links.

Each domain has a mode, which says how users reach your server, and a TLS choice, which says which certificate or disguise it uses.

To add a domain, click Add domain. The Add a domain window has four steps: Domain → Mode → Name → Certificate.

  1. Domain: type the domain or subdomain, or an IPv4 / IPv6 address. Under Point it at this server you see the A (IPv4) and AAAA (IPv6) records to add in your DNS. Click Check: the panel checks the DNS and suggests the right mode.
  2. Mode: answer How is it set up? and Which TLS? (see below).
  3. Name and Certificate: finish the remaining steps.

In the next step you choose the mode:

Modes (How is it set up?):

  • Direct: the domain points straight to your server's IP. If the domain is on Cloudflare, keep the cloud off (DNS only).
  • CDN: the domain goes through a CDN such as Cloudflare (orange cloud on). A CDN is a network of servers that sits between your users and your server, so your server's IP stays hidden.
  • Relay: users connect to another server in between, which forwards the traffic to this one.
  • Subscription only: used only for subscription links, with no proxies.

TLS (Which TLS?): Valid TLS (a real certificate, issued automatically), Fake (decoy TLS with a fake site's name; not recommended) and Reality (borrows another site's TLS with the Reality protocol). Some modes always use a valid certificate; the window tells you when.

Changed in v13

The old separate types Auto CDN IP, Fake and Reality are no longer domain types. On upgrade, Auto CDN IP domains became CDN domains, and Fake and Reality domains became Direct domains with the Fake or Reality TLS mode.

docs.title: Direct domain
docs.text:
Click Add domain, type the domain, and choose Direct with Valid TLS. The settings of a direct domain:

  • Display name: shown in the users' apps instead of the domain. Use it if you don't want the domain to appear in the configs.
  • Force configs to use these IPs / domains: leave it empty for a direct domain. It is mainly for CDN domains.
  • Show configs of: choose which domains' configs users see when they open their user page through this domain.

Tip: if you have a domain on a separate IP that is not blocked, select all the other domains (but not itself) in Show configs of for it. Because this IP is not used for the proxies and is just a plain site, it is unlikely to be blocked, and users can always update their profiles.

docs.title: Subscription-only domain
docs.text:
A subscription-only domain only serves subscription links. Because no proxy traffic goes through it, it is less likely to be blocked, so users can always update their configs.

After you link the subscription-only domain to your connection domains in Show configs of, open a user page through it. The configs on that page use your connection domains.

Tip: a subscription domain works best behind a CDN, so users can still update when your proxy domains are blocked. You can also use a PHP website for subscription links: see How to use a PHP site for sub links.

docs.title: CDN domain
docs.text:
Click Add domain, type the domain, and choose CDN. The settings of a CDN domain:

  • Display name: shown in the users' apps instead of the domain.
  • Force configs to use these IPs / domains: put a clean Cloudflare IP here, or better, a normal DNS record (cloud off) that points to a clean IP. Then, when you need a new clean IP, you only update that DNS record and the panel and configs stay the same. To find clean IPs, see Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP. This field replaces the old Auto CDN IP mode: see Guide for using mode Auto_CDN_IP.
  • Domain fronting: optional. Users' apps show another site's name (SNI) instead of your domain, so a filter only sees that other site. Use sites on the same CDN as your domain. In older versions this was a global setting; now it is set per CDN domain. See Guide for domain fronting.
  • ECH: uses Encrypted Client Hello for this CDN domain. Turn on Enable TLS ECH in Settings first.
  • Show configs of: choose which domains' configs users see on this domain's user page.

If you have many users and want to give each group its own domain, read How to use multi-CDN domains.

docs.title: Other domain setups
docs.text:
• Relay domain: see How to add a relay domain.
  • Fake TLS mode: see How to create and use a fake domain.
  • Reality TLS mode: see How to use Reality.
  • Cloudflare workers: see How to set up and use Cloudflare workers.

docs.title: Proxies and protocols
docs.text:
Open Protocols to turn protocols, transports and TLS tricks on or off for the whole panel. Tap a card to switch it, then save. The cards are grouped into Protocols, Transports, Security & tricks and Other, and each group has Enable all and Disable all. Each card's Settings link opens its settings. The same switches are also in Settings → Proxies Settings. The Proxy Editor lets advanced users edit each built-in proxy template.

Further down the same page, the transports:

Note: plain HTTP connections are not encrypted. TLS connections are encrypted.

docs.title: Outbounds
docs.text:
Outbounds decide where your users' traffic leaves your server: directly, through WARP, blocked, or through a Socks, Tor or Psiphon exit. They are checked from top to bottom: traffic goes out through the first outbound that lists its site, and the last enabled one gets everything else. Each admin can also pick a default outbound for their own users in My account.

Full guide: Outbounds. For WARP itself, see How to activate WARP.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open Settings. It is one long page of cards; common settings are shown first. Turn on Show Advanced Settings at the top to see the rest, or type in the search box. Settings marked Reinstall take effect only after a reinstall (see Actions).

What each card is for. Click a card to see every setting in it, with a picture, in All HiddifyManager settings:

Card What it is for Admin Settings panel language, parent panel for multi-server, node name Customizing User Page title, support link and text, language of the user page General Settings DNS, country, decoy site, firewall, auto update, backups Proxies Settings which transports and protocols go into the configs, domestic-site blocking Telegram Configs Telegram proxy (MTProxy / web proxy) HTTP / TLS ports and TLS options of the configs MUX, TLS Trick connection tricks; see MUX and TLS trick SSH Proxy, Mieru, TUIC, Hysteria, WireGuard, Shadowsocks, DNSTT options of those protocols WARP see How to activate WARP Reality see How to use Reality Advanced / Very Advanced proxy paths, Cloudflare API, update channel and other expert options

docs.title: Proxy Editor
docs.text:
The Proxy Editor is for advanced users who want to change how the configs are built:

  • Proxies: every built-in proxy (protocol, transport, TLS layer and core) with its own switch and settings.
  • Base Configs and Templates: the server and client configs the proxies are made from.
  • Template Variables: values that the templates use.

A wrong change here can break all configs; Reset all to defaults brings back the built-in ones. Full guide: Proxy Editor.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Open Backup to make a backup of your panel or restore one. The page is called Backup & Restore.

  • Under Make a Backup, Download Backup saves everything in one .json file: settings, users, admins, domains, proxies and certificates. Keep the file safe: it contains passwords, user links and private keys. Save on the server and Save on the Telegram keep the copy on the server or send it to you on Telegram.
  • The panel also makes automatic backups on the server every 6 hours. They are listed under Backups on the server, where you can download, restore or delete each one. If your Telegram bot is connected, each one is also sent to you on Telegram.
  • To restore, drop a .json backup file on Restore (or click it to choose one). You choose which parts to bring back: Settings, Users and Domains.

Details: How to back up and restore.

docs.title: Telegram bot
docs.text: Telegram Bot in the menu opens your panel's bot in Telegram. With it you and your users get their links, usage, alerts and backups in Telegram, and the Inbox works through it. To set it up, see How to set up and use the Telegram bot.

docs.title: Actions (Apply & Status)
docs.text: Open Actions in the menu. The Apply & Status page lets you put changes into effect, update the server and see how everything is doing. Each card shows how long the action takes and when it last ran. Each action shows its log while it runs. You can leave the page; the action keeps running on the server. Below the cards are Reset Cache, Public ports and Live connection test.

docs.title: Check Status
docs.text: Click Check now. It shows whether each service is running, plus the server's public IP and WARP. It changes nothing.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: The Logs section lists what each action did (for example hiddify_panel.log, status.log, warp.log). Click the eye icon to read a log; the other icons download it or send it to Telegram.

docs.title: Apply Changes
docs.text:
Click Apply now. It puts your settings, users and domain changes into effect. It is quick, and it is the usual choice after you change something.

  • When it finishes, the page shows your admin links on your domains. They may have changed, so copy them before you leave.
  • If the panel no longer opens after a change, connect to your server over SSH and run hiddify admin to see your current admin links:
hiddify admin
  • If that does not help, see How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH.

docs.title: Update Hiddify
docs.text: Click Update. It downloads and installs the latest version, then applies it. It takes a while, and the panel restarts at the end. See How to update HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Reinstall
docs.text: Click Reinstall. It installs everything again and rebuilds all services. Your users and links are not changed. Use it when Apply changes is not enough, for example after you change the panel path, protocols or a setting marked Reinstall. Connections may drop for a few minutes.

docs.title: Restart Services
docs.text: Click Restart. It restarts all HiddifyManager services without reinstalling anything. It is a good first try when something misbehaves. Connections drop for a moment.

docs.title: API
docs.text: API opens the documentation of the panel's REST API, to manage users and admins from your own programs or bots. See How to use the API.

docs.title: My account
docs.text: Click the person icon at the top to open My account: your admin link, your limits, your language, password and passkeys (sign in without a password), and for your users (and your sub-admins' users): the default outbound, configs for my users that are added to their subscriptions, and my users' page, a custom user page. Full guide: My account and admin security.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: All tutorials and videos are listed on the HiddifyManager tutorials page. Every setting is explained in All HiddifyManager settings.

docs.title: How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH (Working with HiddifyManager Menu)
Connect over SSH and use the Hiddify Manager menu
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Installing SSH on Windows (click)

Windows 10 and 11 usually already include the SSH client. If the ssh command does not work in PowerShell, install it like this:

  1. Open the Start menu and search for PowerShell.

  2. Right-click PowerShell and choose Run as Administrator.

  3. Run this command in PowerShell:

    Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client

  4. When it finishes, you should see something like this:

The SSH client is now installed.

This page shows you how to manage Hiddify Manager from your server's command line when the web panel does not open, or when you have lost your admin link. It also explains each option of the HiddifyManager menu.

SSH is a secure way to open a text terminal on your server from your own computer or phone. Everything you type runs on the server.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your server's IP address.
  • The server's username (usually root) and password or SSH key. Your server provider gives you these.
  • An SSH app on your device:
    • Android: Termius
    • Windows: PowerShell (or PuTTY)
    • macOS: Terminal
    • Linux: Terminal

For a full guide, see How to connect to the server via SSH.

docs.title: Connect to the server
docs.text:
1. Open your SSH app.

  2. Run this command on your device. Replace user with your username and <IP_Address> with your server's IP:

    ssh user@<IP_Address>

    For example, if your username is root and your server's IP is 1.1.1.1:

    ssh root@1.1.1.1

  3. Type yes if you are asked to trust the server, then enter your password. (The password is not shown while you type. This is normal.)

If the connection works, you see the server's command prompt, and the HiddifyManager menu may open by itself.

docs.title: Open the HiddifyManager menu
docs.text:
Run this command on your server to open the HiddifyManager menu:

hiddify

The menu looks like this (Hiddify Manager 14.5):

Use the arrow keys to move, and press Enter to choose an item. The sections below explain each item.

If you see a warning first

If password sign-in is on for the server, the menu shows this warning before it opens. Press Ok to open the menu, and to keep the server safe turn off password sign-in.

Commands instead of the menu

Most menu items are also available as direct commands, for example hiddify status, hiddify admin, hiddify restart, hiddify apply and hiddify upgrade release. Run hiddify --help to see them all.

docs.title: Cancel or Quit
docs.text:
Choose Quit (or press Cancel / Esc) to leave the menu and go back to the normal server terminal.

To open the menu again, run this command on your server:

hiddify

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Shows whether each HiddifyManager service is running. If everything is fine, the result looks like this:

Press q to return to the main menu.

When to use it: to check quickly whether all services are running.

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
Shows your admin panel links. The links are shown in three groups: Secure (a trusted certificate on your domain; open these), Self-signed (the browser warns; use only if the Secure ones do not open) and Insecure (not encrypted, http; avoid). A QR code of the link is shown above them.

On this screen you can also press r to reset the owner admin password. Press any other key to return to the main menu.

The same links are printed by this command:

hiddify admin

When to use it: you installed the panel but forgot to copy the admin link.

docs.title: Log
docs.text:
Shows the system logs. After you choose it, pick the log file you want to read.

For example, choose 0-install.log (the install log) to see what happened during installation. At its end, it shows the system status and the admin links.

Press q to close the log. The log files are stored on the server in /opt/hiddify-manager/data/log/.

When to use it: one of the services is not working and you need to see why.

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
Restarts all HiddifyManager services without changing any settings.

Press any key to return to the main menu.

When to use it: a service has stopped and you want to restart all services at once.

docs.title: Apply configs
docs.text:
The menu no longer has an "Apply Configs" item. To apply the settings you saved in the panel, run this command on your server:

hiddify apply

When to use it: you saved changes in the panel but lost web access before you could apply them.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
In the menu it is called Reinstall the server. It reinstalls Hiddify Manager on the server. Your panel data (users, settings, domains) is kept.

When to use it: an install step failed and the panel does not open.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
Updates Hiddify Manager to the latest version. It offers these options:

  • default: updates to the channel chosen in the panel settings.
  • release: updates to the latest stable version (recommended).
  • beta: updates to the latest pre-release version. It may have bugs.

You can also update with a command, for example:

hiddify upgrade release

While it runs, the terminal shows something like this:

When to use it: an update from the web panel failed and you lost access.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: This submenu has several options.

docs.title: warp
docs.text: Shows the status of the WARP service.

docs.title: add_remote
docs.text: Gives the Hiddify support team SSH access to your server, through the Hiddify bot. Use it only when the support team asks you to.

docs.title: remove_remote
docs.text: Removes the SSH access you gave to the Hiddify bot.

docs.title: enable
docs.text: Shows the HiddifyManager menu automatically every time you log in to the server over SSH. Use it if you turned this off before.

docs.title: disable
docs.text: Stops the HiddifyManager menu from opening automatically when you log in. You can still open it with hiddify.

docs.title: uninstall
docs.text: Removes Hiddify Manager services from the server. It does not remove everything that was installed. If you want the server exactly as it was before the installation, rebuild it from your provider's control panel.

docs.title: purge
docs.text:
Removes Hiddify Manager and its database completely. All users and settings are deleted, so take a backup first.

If this does not work for any reason, you can Rebuild the server from your provider's control panel. This deletes all data on the server.

docs.title: How to set up Telegram proxy on HiddifyManager
How to set up Telegram proxy on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
One of the good features of the HiddifyManager panel is providing a Telegram proxy. There are two kinds, explained below.

  • MTProxy FakeTLS: a Telegram MTProxy hidden as TLS (tg://proxy links). It needs a Direct or Relay domain.
  • Telegram Web Proxy: a Telegram proxy over HTTPS on every domain with a real certificate, CDN included (tg://webproxy links).

docs.title: Telegram proxy activation
docs.text:
• To do this, click Protocols in the panel sidebar and turn on MTProxy FakeTLS Enable and/or Telegram Web Proxy Enable, then save.
  • The same switches are also in the Telegram Configs card of the Settings page.

  • If the message about applying changes is displayed, be sure to press the button so that the changes are applied to the server. You can also do it from Actions in the sidebar: click Apply now in the Apply Changes card.

  • Now your users can find the proxies on their user page: in the menu at the top they open Telegram Proxy. The page lists one proxy per server address and, when Telegram Web Proxy is on, a Web proxy for each domain. Tapping a row shows its QR code, the link with a copy button, and Open Telegram, which adds the proxy to Telegram in one tap.

docs.title: Advertising activation
docs.text:
• For this, search for MTProxybot.

  • Now enter the created proxy into the bot. It may take some time to fully activate.

  • Then, in the panel settings, enter the address you want to advertise in the Telegram advertising tag field. For example, you can give your support account address.

  • The work is done.

docs.title: How to set up and use Telegram bot on HiddifyManager
How to set up and use Telegram bot on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
This page shows you how to connect your Hiddify Manager panel to your own Telegram bot. With the bot you can create and manage users from Telegram, check the server status, and receive the panel's automatic backups. Your users can also link their Telegram to get notices when their package is about to end.

Prerequisites

  • Admin access to your Hiddify Manager panel.
  • A Telegram account.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Telegram bot
docs.text:
1. Open Telegram and search for @BotFather. This is Telegram's official bot for creating bots.

  2. Tap Start.

  3. Send /newbot (or choose it from the menu).

  4. Send a name for your bot. Then send a unique username for it.

    • The username must end with bot (for example my_vpn_bot).
    • You can use _ in the username.

  5. BotFather now sends you a token: a long code like 123456789:AA.... Copy it. Keep it secret: anyone with the token can control your bot.

docs.title: Step 2: Add the token to the panel
docs.text:
1. Open your admin panel.
  2. In the sidebar, under Settings, click Settings.
  3. Find the Telegram Bot Token field in the Telegram Configs section. (You can also type "Telegram" in the search box at the top of the page.)
  4. Paste the token you copied.

  5. Click Save.

If it worked, the panel shows "Telegram bot connected: @your_bot_username", and a Telegram Bot item appears in the sidebar under Settings.

If you see "Telegram bot could not connect", check that you pasted the whole token with no extra spaces, and that your server can reach Telegram.

docs.title: Step 3: Link your admin account to the bot
docs.text:
1. In the panel sidebar, click Telegram Bot. Telegram opens your bot.
  2. Tap Start.

For security, the bot only recognises you as an admin when you open it from this link. Each admin can link their own Telegram account in the same way. You can also link it from My account → Connect Telegram.

docs.title: Using the bot
docs.text:
After you start it, the bot shows your admin menu with these buttons:

  • 👥 Users: list your users. You can filter them (for example, users whose package is ending soon) or type a name to search. Open a user to renew their package, add days or data, reset their usage, enable, disable or delete them, and see their links and QR code.
  • ➕ New user: create one or more users.
  • 📊 Server status: CPU, RAM, disk, uptime, traffic and online users.
  • 🩺 Check status: the server's public IP with its country and provider, and whether each service (Xray, sing-box, HAProxy and the others) is running. Not shown to agent admins.
  • 🎁 Free test: the link you share so people can ask for a free test account (see Free test below).
  • 💾 Backup: get a backup file of the whole panel right now (super admins only).
  • 🖥 Open panel: open your admin panel inside Telegram. You are signed in with your linked Telegram account, without the admin link.

Send /menu at any time to bring the admin menu back.

docs.title: Create a user from the bot
docs.text:
1. Tap ➕ New user.

  2. Choose how much data the package has.

  3. Choose how many days the package lasts.

  4. Choose how many users to create with these limits.

  5. Optional: tap ✏️ Name and send a name for the user.

  6. Tap ✅ Create.

The bot sends you one card per new user, with the user's links. You can forward the card to the user.

The new user also appears in the panel's Users page.

Tap 🔄 Refresh on a user's card to see their latest data usage and remaining days. Tap ⚙️ Manage to get the user's links and QR code, add days or data, renew the package, reset usage, or disable or delete the user.

docs.title: Search for a user
docs.text: In 👥 Users, tap 🔍 Search and send a name, UUID, comment or Telegram ID. Tap ✖️ Clear to go back to the full list.

docs.title: Check status
docs.text: 🩺 Check status shows where your server's public IP is located (country, city, provider) and a ✅ for every service that is running. A ❌ means that service is down: open Actions in the panel and restart, or see How to connect and troubleshoot via SSH.

docs.title: Daily notices
docs.text:
Once a day the bot checks every user:

  • A user whose package ends in 3 days or less, or who has used 85% or more of their data, gets a reminder in the bot (if they linked their Telegram).
  • You get one summary message listing your users that are ending soon (up to 15 names), with a button that opens the Ending soon list.

docs.title: Free test
docs.text:
With 🎁 Free test you can let people get a test account from the bot by themselves. Set the package (data and days) and the mode in the panel: in the sidebar, under Manager, open Inbox → Free test.

  • Automatic: the account is given right away, once per Telegram account.
  • Manual: each request comes to you in the bot with ✅ Approve and ✖️ Decline.

Tap 🎁 Free test in the bot to get the link to share. Whoever opens it sees the package and can ask for it.

docs.title: Messages from users
docs.text: A user can type a message in the bot. It comes to you as "name wrote:" with a ↩️ Reply button; type your answer and it goes back to the user. The same conversations are in the panel's Inbox.

docs.title: Automatic backups
docs.text: When your admin account is linked to the bot, each automatic backup of the panel is also sent to you in Telegram. You can manage backups in the panel: in the sidebar, under Settings, click Backup. See How to backup and restore the panel.

docs.title: Users and the bot
docs.text:
Your users can link their own Telegram to the bot. To do this, a user opens your bot and taps Start, then sends their subscription link or UUID, or taps the Telegram button on their account page. After that:

  • They can see their remaining data and days, and their links, in the bot.
  • The bot warns them when their package is about to end.
  • You can send them messages from the panel: in the sidebar, under Manager, click Send Message. Choose who gets it (for example Everyone or Active), write the message, optionally add an image, and click Send. Only users who have started your bot receive messages.

docs.title: How to update HiddifyManager
docs.text: There are 2 ways to update the panel.

docs.title: Update through admin panel
docs.text:
In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Actions. On the Apply & Status page, click Update in the Update Hiddify card.

This may take between 5 and 10 minutes. HiddifyManager downloads and installs the latest version, then applies it; the panel restarts at the end.

docs.title: Change the update mode
docs.text:
If you need to change the update mode, go to Settings in the sidebar and find Package Update Mode in the Advanced Settings card. Choose one of the Release, Beta and Develop versions and then update.

For example, set the update mode to Beta and save the settings.

Then open Actions in the sidebar and click Update in the Update Hiddify card. After about 5 minutes, the panel will be updated to the version you want.

docs.title: Automatic update settings in the panel
docs.text:
The panel updates itself daily with the latest released version on the project's GitHub. Its setting is Auto Update in the General Settings card of the Settings page.

When Auto Update is on, the panel checks for a new update every day at 3:00 AM and, if there is one, updates itself automatically.

docs.title: Update via SSH
docs.text:
Connect via SSH to the server and run hiddify to open the HiddifyManager menu. Choose update and then one of the 3 modes:

  • default: updates to the channel set in the panel (Package Update Mode in Settings > Advanced Settings).
  • release: updates to the latest stable version. This is the suggested option.
  • beta: updates to the latest pre-release version. It may have bugs.

docs.title: How to use Hiddify Reality Scanner
docs.text:
The Hiddify Reality Scanner helps you find good websites to use as a Reality domain. It tests a list of website names (SNIs, the website name a client sends when it opens an encrypted connection) from your own network, and tells you which ones work best. This page is for Hiddify Manager admins who are comfortable running commands on a server and on a computer. For more about the project, see its Contribution Guidelines.

This tool is not actively maintained

The scanner's last release on PyPI is version 1.8.0, from November 2023. It was written for older Hiddify Manager versions and has not been updated for v13 or v14. It may not work as described here. In Hiddify Manager v14, the Add domain wizard also checks whether a website is Reality friendly (TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2), see How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The scanner has two parts:

  • Server side: a temporary test Reality server that runs on your server.
  • Client side: a Python program that runs on your computer, inside the network you want to test (for example, your home internet in Iran).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A server you can reach over SSH (see How to connect to the server via SSH).
  • A computer with Python installed.

Your users lose Xray connections during the test

If Hiddify Manager is installed on the same server, the steps below stop the hiddify-xray service. While it is stopped, your users' Xray configs don't work. Do the test at a quiet time, and start the service again when you finish (last step of this page).

docs.title: Server-side setup
docs.text:
Run these commands on your server, over SSH.

  1. Remove any old Xray installed with the official XTLS installer, stop HiddifyManager's Xray, and install Hiddify's custom Xray core:

    # remove old xray
bash -c "$(curl -L https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-install/raw/main/install-release.sh)" @ remove

# only if you have Hiddify Manager on this server
systemctl stop hiddify-xray

# install hiddify custom xray
bash -c "$(curl -L https://github.com/hiddify/Xray-core-custom/raw/main/install-release.sh)" @ install

  2. Download the scanner's server config and print your test links (one for IPv6, one for IPv4):

    curl -o server_config.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hiddify/Hiddify_Reality_Scanner/main/server_config.json

echo "---------------IPV6---------"
echo "vless://hiddify@$(curl -6 ip.sb):11443/?fp=chrome&security=reality&pbk=Z84J2IelR9ch3k8VtlVhhs5ycBUlXA7wHBWcBrjqnAw&sid=6ba85179e30d4fc2&sni=www.google.com&type=tcp&flow=xtls-rprx-vision&encryption=none#Hiddify"
echo "---------------IPV4---------"
echo "vless://hiddify@$(curl -4 ip.sb):11443/?fp=chrome&security=reality&pbk=Z84J2IelR9ch3k8VtlVhhs5ycBUlXA7wHBWcBrjqnAw&sid=6ba85179e30d4fc2&sni=www.google.com&type=tcp&flow=xtls-rprx-vision&encryption=none#Hiddify"

    Copy the printed vless:// link. This is your test config. It looks like this, with your server's IP instead of SERVER_IP:

    vless://hiddify@SERVER_IP:11443/?fp=chrome&security=reality&pbk=Z84J2IelR9ch3k8VtlVhhs5ycBUlXA7wHBWcBrjqnAw&sid=6ba85179e30d4fc2&sni=www.yahoo.com&type=tcp&flow=xtls-rprx-vision&encryption=none#Hiddify

  3. Start the temporary test server. Leave this window open while you scan:

    xray run -c server_config.json

    The test server listens on port 11443. If the scan can't connect, make sure this port is open in your server's firewall.

docs.title: Client-side setup
docs.text:
On your computer, open a terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows) and install the scanner:

pip install -U hiddify_reality_scanner

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
On your computer, run one of these commands. Replace vless_link with the test link you copied from the server, and keep the quotes:

python -m hiddify_reality_scanner "vless_link"

or

hiddify_reality_scanner "vless_link"

To stop a scan early, press Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Advanced usage
docs.text:
To choose which SNIs to test and how many results to keep, run:

hiddify_reality_scanner --jobs 10 --limit 100 --sni yahoo.com,google.com "vless_link"

To test a list of SNIs from a file instead, put the file's path after --sni:

hiddify_reality_scanner --jobs 10 --limit 100 --sni path_to_the_list "vless_link"

The options mean:

  • --jobs 10: how many SNIs to test at the same time. Default: 10.
  • --sni: the SNIs to test, separated by commas, or the path of a file that lists them.
  • --limit 100: how many working SNIs to keep in the results. Default: 10.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: The scanner saves its results on your computer, in results.txt and results.json. Use the best SNIs as Reality domains and server names on your server: see How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Finish: start HiddifyManager's Xray again
docs.text:
If Hiddify Manager is installed on the server, stop the test server (press Ctrl+C in its window). Then run this on your server, over SSH:

systemctl start hiddify-xray

Check that your users can connect again.

docs.title: How to use Outbounds on Hiddify Manager
How to use Outbounds on Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The pictures and steps on this page are from Hiddify Manager v14.5.

When a user opens a website through your server, the traffic has to leave the server toward that site. The Outbounds page decides how it leaves:

  • Direct: straight from your server, with your server's IP.
  • WARP: through Cloudflare WARP, so sites see a Cloudflare IP instead of your server's IP. Useful, for example, for sites that show captchas or block data-center IPs.
  • Block: dropped. Useful for domestic sites: connections from your server to them can reveal it to the filtering system.
  • Socks: through another proxy server (SOCKS5), for example a server in another country.
  • Tor and Psiphon: through the Tor network or Psiphon.
  • Your own JSON: a hiddify-core (sing-box) outbound or endpoint (for example WireGuard), or an Xray outbound.

docs.title: How the order works
docs.text:
Outbounds are checked from top to bottom. Traffic leaves through the first outbound that lists its site. The last enabled outbound is the default (3): everything that no outbound above lists goes there.

In the picture, the order is:

  1. Block with the domestic sites of Iran: Iranian sites are blocked.
  2. WARP with a list of sites (Netflix, Spotify, Google…): those go through WARP. Here WARP is off, so it is skipped.
  3. Direct, the default: everything else leaves directly.

To change the order, drag the handle (2) or use the up and down arrows (5). To make an outbound the default, open its ⋮ menu and choose Make default (move to the end). The switch (4) turns an outbound on or off; a turned-off outbound is skipped. The pencil (5) edits its lists.

An outbound with no sites

An outbound above the default with no sites, geosites or rule-sets is marked Not used: nothing goes through it. Add some sites, or move it to the end to make it the default.

docs.title: What goes through an outbound
docs.text:
When you add or edit an outbound, the What goes through it part has four lists:

  • Domestic sites of Iran (2): one switch for all Iranian sites (.ir, geoip:ir and Iran's rule-sets). The region follows the Country setting of the panel.
  • Sites (3): one domain per line, for example example.com. Subdomains are included.
  • Geosites / GeoIPs (xray): one Xray entry per line with its prefix, for example geosite:google or geoip:ir. A tag Xray does not know stops Xray, so use only known ones.
  • Rule-sets (hiddify-core): one rule-set URL per line (.srs or a .json source). If you type a SagerNet name such as geosite-netflix, it turns into its URL. Browse rule-sets shows the list.

The default outbound needs no lists: it already gets everything else. Its lists are used again if you move it up.

docs.title: Add an outbound
docs.text:
1. Click Add outbound and choose a type.

  2. Give it a Name.

  3. For Socks, fill in Host and Port of the SOCKS5 server, and Username and Password if it needs them (1 in the Socks picture above).
  4. Choose what goes through it (the lists above).
  5. Click Add outbound. The new outbound is put just above the default.
  6. Apply the changes (Actions → Apply now) to put it into effect.

Notes on each type:

  • WARP, Direct and Block are built in: you can turn them on or off, reorder them and edit their lists, but not delete them.
  • Psiphon and Tor run inside hiddify-core on your server; there can be one of each. For Tor, the tor program must be installed on the server (for example apt install tor); the page warns you when it is missing.
  • Socks and the JSON types can be added more than once.
  • hiddify-core (sing-box) outbound / endpoint and xray outbound: paste one outbound (or endpoint) object as JSON. Insert an example fills in a sample. The panel checks it with the core before saving, and gives it its own tag; the other core reaches it through a local Socks bridge.

docs.title: WARP
docs.text:
The WARP outbound comes with lists of sites that usually need it (streaming, AI and some Google services). When you change them, the row shows Edited here: upgrades keep your lists. Reset to defaults in the ⋮ menu brings back the built-in lists, which upgrades then keep up to date.

WARP only runs after you accept Cloudflare's terms: when you turn it on, the panel asks you to read Cloudflare's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy and accept them. Until then, traffic is not sent through WARP. Then apply the changes.

The WARP settings under Settings → WARP still work and follow this page:

  • WARP+ Mode All = WARP is on and is the default (everything goes through WARP).
  • Only domestic and blocked sites (custom) = WARP is on, with its own sites, and Direct is the default.
  • Disable = WARP is off.
  • Sites you add in Additional WARP Sites are added to the WARP outbound.

More about WARP: how to activate WARP.

docs.title: A different outbound for some users or admins
docs.text:
• For one user: in the user's window, Preferred outbound sends all of that user's traffic through one outbound. Automatic follows the order on this page.
  • For an admin and their users: in the admin's window, Default outbound sets where that admin's users (and their sub-admins' users) leave through, unless a user chooses another.
  • For yourself: on My account, Default outbound does the same for your own users.

In the user window, Preferred outbound is under Advanced (1):

On My account, Default outbound (1):

An admin can change these only with the Change preferred outbound permission, and can edit this page only with Manage outbounds.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• After you change outbounds, apply the changes (Actions → Apply now).
  • On a multi-server setup, the outbounds are set on the main panel and copied to the nodes. See multi-server with nodes.
  • Blocking domestic sites is also the Block Domestic Sites switch in Settings → Proxies Settings: it moves the domestic sites between Block and WARP.

docs.title: How to use Reality on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
• Short IDs: used for encryption.
  • Private Key: used to encrypt the connection.
  • Public Key: given to the client apps so they can talk to your server.

The panel creates these values for you. Each field says Do Not Change It: don't change them. If you change them, all your users' existing Reality configs stop working.

For example, say your subscription domain is t1.hiddify.com and your Reality domain is www.yahoo.com:

  1. In the sidebar, under Settings, click Domains, and click the pencil (edit) icon of t1.hiddify.com.
  2. In the Show configs of field, select www.yahoo.com (or all domains).
  3. Click Save and apply the changes.

Now open the subscription link on t1.hiddify.com. You should see the Reality configs in it.

docs.title: How to use Reality on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add a Reality domain in the Hiddify Manager panel, so your users get Reality configs. It is for panel admins who already have a working Hiddify Manager.

Reality is a security layer from Xray. Your server borrows the TLS identity (the "fingerprint" of the encrypted connection) of another real website, for example www.yahoo.com. To a filter, the traffic looks like a normal visit to that website. You don't need your own domain or certificate for Reality. HiddifyManager does most of the work behind the scenes.

What changed in Hiddify Manager v13 and v14

  • Reality is no longer a separate domain type. You now add a domain with the mode Direct and the TLS mode Reality.
  • The old panel-wide "Reality Server Names" and "Reality Fallback Domain" settings were removed. You now set them per domain, in the domain's Server names field.
  • Reality now also works with other transports (TCP, HTTP, gRPC and XHTTP), and with Trojan as well as VLESS.

Important

Reality can't go through a CDN (a network of servers, such as Cloudflare, that sits between your users and your server). It only works in Direct or Relay mode, so your server needs a clean IP (an IP that is not blocked in your users' country). To check your server, see How to make sure the server's IP or domain is clean.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You can log in to your panel as the owner (super admin).
  • Your server's IP is clean.
  • You have chosen one or more Reality-friendly websites. A good one supports TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2, is not blocked in your country, and ideally is hosted in the same data center as your server. The Hiddify Reality Scanner can help you find one.

docs.title: Panel-wide Reality settings
docs.text: In the panel's sidebar, under Settings, click Settings and find the Reality card. You can also type Reality in the settings search box. You will see these fields:

docs.title: Add a Reality domain
docs.text:
1. In the panel's sidebar, under Settings, click Domains.
  2. Click Add domain.

  3. In the Domain step (Which domain?), type the address of the website you chose, for example www.yahoo.com, and click Check. The panel checks the domain's DNS. If it says the site "Points to another server (…): good for Reality, a relay or Fake TLS", you can go on. If it says the site is "not Reality friendly (needs TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2)", go back and choose another website. You don't need to set the DNS record shown under Point it at this server: a Reality domain is someone else's website.

  4. In the Mode step, under How is it set up?, choose Direct.

  5. Under Which TLS?, choose Reality, then click Next.

  6. In the Name step (What should users see?), type a short name that users will see in their apps, or tap one of the suggestions. Use plain letters and numbers. Then click Add domain. A Reality domain needs no certificate.

  7. To see the domain's other fields (see below), click the pencil (edit) icon of the new domain in the Domains list. Change them only if you need to, then click Save.

  8. Apply the changes: when the panel shows "Saved. Apply the configs to put the changes into effect.", click the button to apply. You can also click Actions in the sidebar (under Settings) and, in the Apply Changes card, click Apply now.

If the steps worked, the new domain appears in the Domains list with the badges Direct and Reality, and your users see new Reality configs after they update their subscription.

docs.title: Fields of a Reality domain
docs.text: Open a domain's fields with the pencil (edit) icon in the Domains list.

docs.title: Server names
docs.text:
The websites whose TLS identity Reality borrows. Separate several names with commas, for example www.yahoo.com,blog.yahoo.com. If you leave this field empty, the panel uses the domain itself.

Use names that belong to the same website and server as the domain. For example, if your domain is www.yahoo.com, blog.yahoo.com is a good server name, but www.google.com is not.

To spread your traffic over many names of one website, see How to use subdomains of a website in Reality.

docs.title: Display name
docs.text: An optional name that users see in their apps instead of the domain.

docs.title: Force configs to use these IPs / domains
docs.text:
This field is in the Advanced section at the bottom of the window. Put an IP here if you want the configs to use it instead of your server's main IP. Separate several IPs with commas or new lines. This is mainly for relay servers (a server in between that passes your users' traffic on to your main server). If you use Reality through a relay server, put the relay server's IP here. For more about relays, see How to add a relay domain.

When you save, the panel checks your fields and may show messages. Red messages are errors: fix them before you go on. Yellow messages are only warnings. It is best to change your settings until they go away, but you can ignore them and continue.

docs.title: Turn Reality on or off
docs.text:
Reality is controlled by a panel-wide switch:

  1. In the sidebar, under Settings, click Protocols.
  2. In the Security & tricks section, turn Reality on or off. (The same switch is also in the Proxies Settings card of the Settings page.)
  3. Click Save, then apply the changes.

If Reality doesn't work on your network

Reality can behave differently on different networks. If it doesn't work, first make sure your server's IP is clean. Then try another website as the domain and as the server names.

docs.title: Why don't my users see the Reality configs?
docs.text: Users see the configs of the domain they open their user page on. By default, each domain shows the configs of All domains: you can see this under Show configs of in the Domains list. If you limited the Show configs of field of the domain that your users' subscription link uses, you must add the Reality domain to it.
