docs.title: How to use subdomains of a website in Reality
How to use subdomains of a website in Reality
docs.text: This page shows you how to spread your Reality traffic over many subdomains of one website. A subdomain is a name under a main domain, for example blog.yahoo.com under yahoo.com. When your traffic uses many names instead of one, it is harder for the filtering system to notice your server.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • You already have a Reality domain in your panel. If not, first follow How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Find the subdomains of the website you use for Reality. You can use subdomainfinder.c99.nl: search for the website's name. For example, here are all the subdomains of speedtest.net.

    You can also use crt.sh. For example, here are the subdomains of mozilla.org, the Firefox website.

  2. In the panel's sidebar, under Settings, click Domains and open your Reality domain.

  3. In the Server names field, enter the subdomains, separated by commas. For example: sub1.example.com,sub2.example.com,sub3.example.com. Use only subdomains that really open as websites.
  4. Click Save, then apply the changes (in Settings → Actions, click Apply now).

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Each time a user's subscription link updates, one of these subdomains is chosen as the address. This splits the traffic over the subdomains. For example, if a user's app updates the subscription every hour, it uses a different subdomain each hour. This makes it less likely that the filtering system detects your server.

docs.title: How to use the Proxy Editor in Hiddify Manager
How to use the Proxy Editor in Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The menus and names on this page are those of version 14.5. In older versions some of them do not exist.

The Proxy Editor is where Hiddify Manager keeps the recipe of every config it builds: what runs on the server, and what goes into your users' subscriptions. Most people never need to change it: the built-in proxies are tested and updated with each release. Use it when you want something the normal settings can't do, for example a proxy on a special port, an extra outbound, or a change to the configs of one app.

Open Settings › Proxy Editor in the menu. It has four pages:

Page What it holds Proxies Every proxy (protocol + transport + TLS) the panel can build, with its server part and its client part. Base Configs The full config "shell" of each core: the file a proxy's pieces are put into. Templates Reusable pieces (a protocol, a transport, a security layer…) that proxies and base configs include. Template Variables Every value you can use inside a template, with its current value.

Before you change anything

  • The items marked SYS are built in. They follow the catalog of the panel and are updated with each release. Prefer Duplicate and edit the copy, instead of changing a built-in item.
  • Make a backup first (Backup page).
  • After you save, the panel asks you to Apply the configs. Server changes take effect only after Apply (Actions › Apply now).

docs.title: Proxies
docs.text:
1. Filters: show only some proxies, by protocol, transport, mode, server core, TLS or domain mode. Modified shows the built-in proxies you have changed.
  2. The row of a proxy: the switch turns it on or off; the pencil opens it; the copy icon duplicates it; custom proxies also have a delete icon. A star means Common: this protocol exists on both Xray and Hiddify Core, and the Common Proxy Core setting decides which core serves it. The SYS icon marks a built-in proxy (it is highlighted when you changed it).
  3. Generate all configs: builds every server and client config for one domain and one user, without saving or applying anything (see below).
  4. Reset all to defaults: drops every change you made to the built-in proxies and brings back the catalog version. Proxies you created yourself are not touched.
  5. New Proxy: makes an empty proxy of your own.

A proxy can only be turned on when its protocol is on in Settings. If it is off there, the panel offers to turn it on for you.

docs.title: The proxy page
docs.text:
Click the pencil of a proxy. The page has three tabs: General, Server and Client.

  1. A built-in proxy shows this note: it follows the catalog. To edit its server or client side, turn on Override on that tab.
  2. The three tabs.
  3. Duplicate: an editable copy of the proxy. This is the safest way to change a built-in proxy.
  4. Validate: checks the templates of the proxy for mistakes.
  5. Generate example: shows the configs this proxy makes for one domain and one user.
  6. Domain modes: the kinds of domain this proxy is built for (Direct, Relay, CDN, REALITY…). A domain that is not in this list gets no config of this proxy.

The other fields of General:

  • Enabled and Common proxy.
  • Name: the label of its links in the users' apps. Custom path is the path of HTTP-based proxies; it is made automatically and the round arrow makes a new one.
  • Slug and Categories: an ID and tags, used by the filters and by templates.
  • Protocol, Transport and TLS layer: what the proxy is.
  • Link settings: the Mode (how traffic reaches the core: through a domain gateway, on its own ports, by IP…), the reverse proxy protocol and the Inbound port (empty means automatic, per domain).

On a built-in proxy, fields with an Override box keep the catalog value until you tick the box.

docs.title: Server tab
docs.text:
1. Server core: the program that serves this proxy on the server (Xray or Hiddify Core).
  2. Override: tick it to edit the server template of a built-in proxy.
  3. Insert variable: adds a template variable at the cursor. Preview shows the result for one domain and user.
  4. The Templates panel lists the pieces this template includes. Click one to see it.

Templates are JSON with Jinja tags: {{ proxy.port }} puts in a value, {% include 'xray/server/streams/xhttp' %} puts in another template, {% for … %} repeats a part.

docs.title: Client tab
docs.text:
1. Client core configs: what this proxy adds to the subscription of each app format.
  2. One tab per format: sublink (share links), xray, singbox, hiddify-core and clash. A format with no config here gives no config of this proxy to the apps that read that format.
  3. The Templates panel of the selected format.

Each format can have a Version (the lowest app core version that gets it) and its outbound template.

docs.title: Generate all configs
docs.text:
This is the safe way to see what your changes do. Nothing is saved or applied.

  1. Domain: one of the panel's domains, a domain you type, or all domains.
  2. User: a sample user or one of your users.
  3. User-Agent: the app to build for (for example the Hiddify app on Android). The panel builds a different format for each app.
  4. The result: success, or warnings and errors. Click an error to see the template line that caused it.
  5. Render context: what it was built with. Below it, every server and client config, and the Warnings. A skipped (SKIP) warning is normal: that proxy does not apply to this domain or app.

docs.title: Base Configs
docs.text:
A base config is the whole config file of one core, with a place where the proxies are put in.

  1. Side: Server configs run on your server; Client configs are the shell of a subscription.
  2. Core: server ones are Xray, Hiddify Core, HAProxy, the L4 gateway (rust-rpxy-l4), the DNS router, WireGuard, the Telegram MTProxy (Telemt), the firewall rules, and the scripts of the Scanner page. Client ones are Xray, sing-box, Hiddify Core, share links (sublink) and Clash/Mihomo.
  3. New Base Config: makes your own.

For a built-in base config only the name and the switch can change. To edit its content, tick Override on its page, or Duplicate it. Version decides from which core version a base config is used.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Templates are the small pieces the proxies and base configs are made of.

  1. Slug: the name a template is included by, for example xray/client/protocols/vless: core, side, category, name.
  2. Category: what kind of piece it is (protocol, stream, security, outbound…).
  3. New Template: makes your own piece.

A change to a template changes every proxy that includes it. That is useful (fix it once), and also the reason to be careful: check with Generate all configs afterwards.

  1. A built-in template follows the catalog.
  2. Slug: only the part after core/category can be changed.
  3. Override: tick it to edit the content of a built-in template. To keep the original, use Duplicate (clone as custom) instead.

Example: the Additional Config template

The built-in Additional Config proxy and its templates add the configs of another subscription to your users' subscriptions. It is off by default. Turn the proxy on, tick Override on its client side and put your subscription address in place of example.com. The download("json", "1h", …) function fetches it (and keeps it for an hour).

docs.title: Template Variables
docs.text:
This page lists every value a template can use.

  1. Search and Group: find a variable by name or by group (panel settings, the proxy, the domain, the user…).
  2. Access: how to write it in a template, for example hconfig.block_iran_sites is the Block Domestic Sites setting.
  3. Current value: its value on this panel.

A template can also output SKIP (or call skip()) to leave a proxy out when a condition is not met, for example when a user has no address in their extra parameters.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Use the Config Tester (Tools › Config Tester) after a change: it connects through every config of a subscription and shows which ones work. See Panel tools.
  • Reset all to defaults on the Proxies page, or Reset to catalog default on one proxy, undoes your changes when something goes wrong.
  • More examples (a subscription for one user, one user through WARP, the whole server through a SOCKS proxy) are in help_customize_proxies (Persian).

docs.title: How to use the panel tools in Hiddify Manager
How to use the panel tools in Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The menus and names on this page are those of version 14.5. In older versions some of these tools do not exist.

The Tools menu of the panel has five helpers for everyday work:

Tool What it does Config Tester Connects through every config of a subscription, from the server, and shows which ones work. Scanner Finds Cloudflare IPs that work on your users' internet, tunes TLS Fragment, and checks your REALITY SNIs. Text Decoders Opens up share links, Base64 and URL-encoded text so you can read and edit them. QR Code Makes a QR code from any text, or reads one. SSH Terminal A terminal and file manager for any server, inside the panel.

docs.title: Config Tester
docs.text:
The Config Tester runs each config of a subscription in its own core and checks that it connects. Use it after you change domains, protocols or the Proxy Editor, or when a user says "nothing works".

  1. What to test: a Subscription link, or Contents you paste (share links, a base64 subscription, an Xray, Hiddify Core or sing-box JSON, or a Clash Meta YAML).
  2. Subscription link: paste a link, or click the box to pick one of your users: their link is filled in.
  3. Application: the app the subscription is for. The panel gives each app its own format, so the test checks exactly what that app gets. A format the app can't read is shown as an error.
  4. Start test.
  5. More options: the User agent sent when the link is fetched, the Test URL, how many configs are tested at the same time (Parallel workers), Tests per config and the Timeout.

The test runs on the panel's server and goes on even if you close the page (results are kept for an hour).

  1. Subscription received: what the panel sent (format, size, number of configs). View opens it, so you can read or edit a link and test it again.
  2. Working: configs that connected, with their delay.
  3. Not working: configs that failed. Click a config to see why (its log) and its ping history.
  4. Sort: fastest first, by name, or in subscription order. Test failed again and Test all again are on the same line.

This panel's configs

Under the results, This panel's configs lists the configs of this panel that failed on every link. You can turn them off in one click: they leave the users' subscriptions after Apply. They don't come back by themselves; Restore all at the top of the page turns them on again. Only do this when you are sure the problem is not your own internet.

The panel can also run this test by itself every 6 hours and warn you on Telegram: Settings › General Settings › Automatic config health checks. It is off by default, because some hosting companies take the many connections of a test for an attack.

docs.title: Scanner
docs.text:
The Scanner has three tabs. The first two run in your browser, on the internet you are on now: the panel's server is abroad and can't see how your users' internet behaves. So open this page on the operator you care about (for example a phone on MCI, then on Irancell), with the VPN off.

  1. Your network (as the panel sees it): your operator and its AS number. If a VPN is on, the page warns you: then you would be testing the VPN, not your operator.
  2. The three tabs: IP scanner, Fragment and REALITY SNI.
  3. The IP scanner needs a CDN or worker domain. If the panel has none, add one on the Domains page first (Cloudflare CDN, worker domain).

docs.title: IP scanner
docs.text:
With a CDN domain, the tab walks you through three steps:

  1. Where and for whom? Pick the CDN domain, and the operator whose users get the IPs.
  2. Find IPs that work: Scan tests random IPs from Cloudflare's ranges. Scan settings changes the ranges, the number of IPs per range and the timeout per IP.
  3. Add them to the domain: the fastest IPs are saved in the domain's CDN IP field as IP operator pairs. The IPs of other operators stay as they are. Users get them with their next subscription update.

Full test with upload, from another device is for operators that cut a connection after a little upload, which a browser can't test. It makes a command (Python) to run on a phone (Termux) or a computer on that operator. The command is valid for 24 hours and saves its results here by itself.

More about clean IPs: What is Cloudflare's clean IP and using your own clean IPs.

docs.title: Fragment
docs.text:
CDN domains often need their own TLS Fragment values.

  1. CDN domain: pick the domain.
  2. Presets: ready values (Default, Fine, Coarse, Multi lengths, Packets 1-3, Tight). Apply puts one on the domain; Off turns fragment off for it.

A browser can't measure fragment. After you apply a preset, check it with the Config Tester or an app on that operator. More: How the TLS trick works.

docs.title: REALITY SNI
docs.text:
A REALITY config looks like a visit to another site (its SNI). If an operator filters that site, the config stops working there.

  1. REALITY SNIs: the SNIs your REALITY domains use, and on which operators each one is filtered. Switch changes an SNI to another one.
  2. Test the SNIs: Make the command gives a command to run on a device on the operator to check (VPN off). It connects to your server with each SNI, as a REALITY app does, and records here which ones that operator filters. The list of SNIs to test comes from OONI (sites seen reachable in Iran); you can edit it.
  3. Spare SNIs: ordinary sites (up to 300) to switch to when an SNI is filtered.
  4. Automatic switch: when on, a filtered SNI is changed to a working spare by itself.

See also the Hiddify Reality Scanner and setting up REALITY.

docs.title: Text Decoders
docs.text:
Everything here happens in your browser; nothing is sent to the server.

  1. Three tabs: Sublink, Base64 and URL.
  2. Share links: paste one or more vless://, vmess://, ss://, trojan:// links, or a base64 subscription (it is opened into links).
  3. Decoded: each link as fields (server, port, user, path, name), its Query parameters as rows, and extra as JSON. Change a field and the link on the left is rewritten. Handy to fix a link by hand, or to see why an app rejects it.

  1. Text and 2. Base64: type in either side, the other updates. URL-safe uses the URL-safe Base64 alphabet; Swap exchanges the sides. The URL tab does the same for percent-encoded text (%20…).

docs.title: QR Code
docs.text:
1. Make a QR code, or Scan one (with the camera, or from an image or a pasted screenshot).
  2. Text or link: any text, for example a subscription link.
  3. Style: Hiddify (dots and the Hiddify logo, like the user page) or Plain (holds about twice as much text).
  4. Download PNG or copy the image.

The camera works only when the panel is open on https. A scanned code can be opened in the Text Decoders with Inspect in Text Decoders.

docs.title: SSH Terminal
docs.text:
A terminal and a file manager for any server, without an SSH app. Useful on a phone, or to manage your nodes and relay servers.

  1. Server and Port of the server (and a Name for it, and the User, usually root).
  2. Sign in with a Password or a Private key.
  3. Save this connection in this browser: it is kept in this browser, encrypted for your admin account. Then click Connect.

The connection is made from the panel's server, not from your device. The first time you connect to a server, the panel shows its key and asks Trust this server?: check it is your server's key before you send your password.

Each connection opens in a tab with a Terminal and Files (browse, upload, download, edit, extract archives). On the right, Commands are saved commands you can run on one or several open connections at once; Install Hiddify Manager is built in. Copy link makes a link that opens the same connection again, for your account only.

Careful

Anyone who can open your admin panel can use this terminal. Protect your account with a password or a passkey: see My account and admin security. More about SSH: How to connect to server via SSH.

docs.title: IPv6 Usage Guide
docs.text: This page shows you how to give your users configs that connect to your server over IPv6. It is for panel admins whose server has an IPv6 address and whose users' internet supports IPv6.

docs.title: What is IPv6?
docs.text:
IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) is the newer kind of internet address. It replaces the older IPv4 addresses (like 1.2.3.4). An IPv6 address is longer and looks like 2001:db8::1.

There are far more IPv6 addresses than IPv4 addresses, so blocking them one by one is harder and costlier for filtering systems. For this reason, IPv6 connections are often blocked less than IPv4 ones.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Your server has IPv6. Your provider (data center) must enable IPv6 on your server. Ask them if you are not sure. To see your server's IPv6 address, run this command on your server over SSH:

    ip -6 addr show scope global

    The address is on the line that starts with inet6. If nothing is shown, your server has no public IPv6 address.

  2. IPv6 is not turned off in the panel. In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Settings. In General Settings, make sure Only IPv4 is off. (If it is on, IPv6 is disabled on the server.)

  3. Your users' internet supports IPv6. Only some internet operators support IPv6. In Iran, for example, it was available on Irancell and Rightel, and on Hamrah-e Aval and Mokhaberat only in some regions. Check with your users.

Tip

The Max Proxy IPs Per Version setting (in General Settings) controls how many IPv4 and how many IPv6 addresses the panel uses to build proxies for each domain.

docs.title: Method 1: Direct domain (recommended)
docs.text:
1. In your DNS provider (for example Cloudflare), create a record of type AAAA for a subdomain (for example v6.example.com). Put your server's IPv6 address as its value. In Cloudflare, turn the proxy (orange cloud) off, so it says DNS only.
  2. In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Domains.
  3. Click Add domain.
  4. Type the subdomain you created and continue.
  5. For the mode, choose Direct. For TLS, choose Valid TLS.
  6. Finish the wizard. The panel gets a certificate for the domain.
  7. Apply the changes when the panel asks you to.

Leave Custom proxies on Automatic so the panel uses every proxy that fits this domain.

docs.title: Method 2: Reality
docs.text:
1. In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Domains, then Add domain.
  2. As the domain, type a Reality-friendly site, for example www.speedtest.net.
  3. For the mode, choose Direct. For TLS, choose Reality.
  4. In Server names, enter the same site (for example www.speedtest.net).
  5. Open Advanced. In Force configs to use these IPs / domains, enter your server's IPv6 address.
  6. Save, then apply the changes.

For more about Reality, see How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

Legacy Direct XTLS mode was removed

Older versions had a separate "Legacy Direct XTLS" domain mode. Since Hiddify Manager v13 it no longer exists: such domains were turned into Direct domains. Use Method 1 instead.

docs.title: Turn on IPv6 on your users' devices
On Android
docs.text:
1. Open the phone's Settings and search for APN.
  2. Open the APN in use and set APN protocol (or "Internet Protocol") to IPv4/IPv6.

docs.title: On Windows
docs.text:
1. Open Control Panel.
  2. Go to Network and Internet, then Network and Sharing Center.
  3. In the side menu, click Change adapter settings.
  4. Right-click your connected network and choose Properties.
  5. Tick Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6) and click OK.

docs.title: On iOS
docs.text:
1. Open this website.
  2. Enter google.com in the first two fields and tick IPv4/IPv6.
  3. Download the profile. Install it from Settings → Profile Downloaded.
  4. In Settings, search for APN, and reset the network settings from the bottom of that page.

When these steps are done, your users can connect to your server over IPv6. If you do not want IPv6 at all, see How to disable IPv6 on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Inbox, free test and messages to users on Hiddify Manager
Inbox, free test and messages to users on Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The pictures and steps on this page are from Hiddify Manager v14.5.

The Inbox page brings together everything that goes through your Telegram bot:

  • Free test: a link you share; whoever opens it in Telegram can ask for a free test account, and gets it automatically or after you approve it.
  • Conversations: messages people send to your bot, which you can read and answer from the panel.
  • Send Message: a message from you to your users in Telegram.

You need the Telegram bot first

All of this works through the panel's Telegram bot. If it is not set up, the page asks you to do it first. See how to set up the Telegram bot.

docs.title: Free test packages
docs.text:
A free test package says how much a free test gives: how many days and how much data. You can have several packages:

  • The Default package is the one everyone in the bot sees. It has Your Free Test Link (3): share it in your channel, group or website.
  • Every other package is Private: it has its own Private Link, and only the people you give that link to can ask for it. Everyone else in the bot still sees the default package. Make Default (4) makes a private package the default.

Under each link: Copy, QR Code (to show or print the link as a QR code) and Telegram (opens the link in Telegram).

docs.title: Make or edit a package
docs.text:
Click Edit Package (2) on a package, or Add Package at the bottom of the page.

  1. Offer a Free Test: on or off. When it is off, people who open your link are told the free test is not available (they can still write to you).
  2. Name: only you see it, in the panel. In the bot, every package is called Free Test.
  3. Duration in days and Data in MB or GB.
  4. How It Is Given:
    • You Approve Each Request: every request waits in your Inbox until you approve or decline it.
    • Given Automatically: the account is made at once, but only for a Telegram account that never had a free test or an account on your panel. Everyone else waits for your approval. This stops the same person from taking free tests again and again.
  5. What People See in the Bot: a preview of the package as it appears in Telegram.

Click Save.

A person can get the free test once. If you have reached your user limit (for admins with a limit), requests wait until there is room.

Sub-admins have their own packages and links. A sub-admin can also choose Use My Parent's Package; then the package says set by the parent admin.

docs.title: What happens in Telegram
docs.text:
1. The person opens your link. The bot shows the package (days and data) and a button.
  2. With Given Automatically, they tap Get my free test and their account arrives in the chat in a few seconds.
  3. With approval, they tap Request the free test. The request appears in your Inbox, and the bot also sends it to you in Telegram with Approve, Decline and Reply buttons, so you can answer from either place. When you approve it, the account is sent to them in Telegram. If you decline it, they are told, and they can still write to you.

New messages from people also reach you in Telegram, with a Reply button.

docs.title: Conversations
docs.text:
When someone opens your free test link or writes to your bot, a conversation appears on the Inbox page. Open it to:

  • read the messages and answer: your answer goes to them in Telegram;
  • for a free test request: Approve or Decline. The request shows whether it is the person's first time or whether they already had a free test, or have an account;
  • Give a Free Test to someone who did not ask for one;
  • Delete Conversation (the person's account stays).

You can filter the list by Unread and Requests.

docs.title: Send a message to your users
docs.text:
Click Send Message (1 in the first picture).

  1. Who gets it: Everyone, Active, Expired or disabled, or the users who have been offline for more than an hour, a day or a week. The number on each choice is how many users will get it. Only users who started your bot are counted, because Telegram lets a bot write only to them.
  2. Message: write it as Plain text, Markdown or HTML. The toolbar adds bold, italic, links, code, quotes, spoilers and lists. Up to 4096 characters.
  3. Image and options: add one image (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 10 MB). Add each user's usage and buttons adds each user's remaining data and days after your text, with buttons to their usage and their page.
  4. The preview shows the message as users will see it in Telegram.

Click Send and confirm. The message cannot be taken back. A progress bar shows how many were delivered and why some were not (for example, a user who blocked the bot).

To a few users or admins

On the Users page, select some users and send the message only to them. On the Admins page you can do the same for admins (only admins with a Telegram ID who started your bot get it).

docs.title: Multi-server with nodes on Hiddify Manager
Multi-server with nodes on Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The pictures and steps on this page are from Hiddify Manager v14.5.

With nodes you run several Hiddify servers as one service. One server is the main panel (the parent). The other servers are nodes connected to it. You add users and admins only once, on the main panel, and they work on every node. The traffic your users use on the nodes is added up on the main panel.

For example, you can have a main server in Germany and nodes in Finland and the Netherlands. A user gets one subscription link, and it has configs for all three servers.

docs.title: What is shared, and what stays on each node
docs.text:
Managed on the main panel Managed on each node Users and admins Yes: added, edited and deleted here, and copied to every node automatically No: the node only shows them Users' traffic Added up here from all nodes Each node sends its users' traffic every few minutes Dashboard Here No Outbounds (WARP, Socks, Tor…) Here, copied to the nodes No Domains, protocols, server settings Each server has its own Yes

On a node, the panel opens to a short Node page. It says that users, admins and the dashboard are managed on the parent panel, and it has an Open parent dashboard button. On a node you manage only that server's domains, proxies and server settings.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install Hiddify Manager on every server, all with the same version. The Nodes page warns you when a node runs another version.
  • The node needs a main domain with a valid certificate (Domains page). A node with only an IP cannot be added.
  • Open the main panel through its own domain, not through an IP. The node uses the address you opened to reach the main panel.
  • The two servers must reach each other on port 443. A firewall or filtering between them breaks the link.

docs.title: Add a node
docs.text:
1. On the server you want to add, open its admin panel. Copy the full address from the browser's address bar. It looks like https://node.example.com/…/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-…/admin/.
  2. On the main panel, open Nodes and click Add node (1).
  3. Paste the address into Node admin link (1 in the next picture). Give it a Name if you like, for example Germany 1 (2). Without a name, the node's own name is used.
  4. Click Connect node (3) and wait. Connecting can take up to a minute.

When it works, the node appears on the Nodes page, and the main panel's users and admins are copied to it. When it fails, the window says which side has the problem (the main panel, the node, or the connection between them) and What to do. For example:

  • The node has no main domain with a valid certificate: add a domain on the node and wait for its certificate.
  • The node's panel is too old: update the node (on the node: Actions → Update Hiddify).
  • The node does not know this panel's address: open the main panel through its domain, not its IP, and try again.
  • This is the link of this same panel: you pasted the main panel's own link. Paste the node's link.

If it still fails, click Copy technical details and send them to support.

docs.title: The node card
docs.text:
Each node has a card on the Nodes page (picture above):

  • Status (2): Online means the node sent a report recently. Late means its last report is old, and Offline means it stopped reporting. Not connected yet means it never reported.
  • Connection (3): whether the main panel can reach the node right now. Reachable is good. Not reachable shows a red mark; click it to see why and what to do (see below).
  • The node's addresses, the last time it sent its users' traffic, today's traffic and online users, and when the last message went each way.
  • The buttons (4):
    • Open: opens the node's admin panel in a new tab.
    • Ping: pings the node from the main panel until you close the window (when ICMP is not possible, it uses TCP).
    • Sync now: asks the node to sync now (users, admins and its domains), instead of waiting for the next automatic sync.
    • Sync details: what the node holds and when each kind of data last came from the main panel. It is read only, for finding problems.
    • Check connection: checks again whether the node is reachable.
  • Remove (5): removes the node and its domains from the main panel. The node becomes a standalone panel again. If the node cannot be reached at that moment, it still has the main panel as its parent: clear Parent Panel (Multi Server) in the node's settings, or it keeps trying to sync.
  • Show more (6): live charts of the node's network, CPU and RAM.

To rename a node, click its name. On the node itself, the name is the Node name setting (Settings → Admin Settings).

docs.title: When a node is "Not reachable"
docs.text:
Click Not reachable on the node's card. A box explains the reason in plain words and says what to do.

The most common reasons:

What it says What to do The node did not answer in time Check that the node's server is on and its panel opens with Open. Make sure its firewall lets the main server in on port 443. The node refused the connection Restart the services on the node (its Actions page) and check that port 443 is open. Secure connection to the node failed The node's certificate is expired or not issued yet: check it on the node's Domains page. The node's domain cannot be found The domain's DNS record does not point to the node any more. Fix the record, or remove the node and add it again with its new link. The node does not recognise this panel The node was reinstalled, restored from a backup or linked to another panel. Remove it here (the trash button) and add it again. The CDN could not reach the node The node's address goes through a CDN, and the node's panel is stopped or restarting. Wait a minute; if it stays, restart the node's services.

Online but Not reachable

A node can be Online and Not reachable at the same time. The node can still send its reports to the main panel, but the main panel cannot call the node. Users then work, but changes you make on the main panel do not reach that node until you fix the connection.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Keep all servers on the same version. Update the main panel and the nodes together.
  • Each node needs its own domains (Domains page on the node). The users' subscription link has the configs of every server.
  • Back up the main panel (it has the users and admins) and each node (for its own domains and settings). See backup and restore.

docs.title: My account and admin security in Hiddify Manager
My account and admin security in Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The menus and names on this page are those of version 14.5. Passwords, passkeys and sign-in usernames for admins do not exist in older versions.

Every admin of the panel (you, and the admins and agents you add) has a My account page: your role and limits, how you sign in, and a few things that apply to all of your users. Open it from the person icon at the top of the panel, then My account.

  1. Copy my admin link: your personal link to the panel. Anyone who has it can sign in as you, unless you set a password (see below). Keep it private. More: the admin link.
  2. Your role and limits. Next to your name is your role (Super admin, Admin or Agent) and whether you can add sub-admins. My limits shows how many users are online, active and in total, and the traffic used, against the limits the admin above you gave you. Your users and all your sub-admins' users count toward them. Super admins have no limits.
  3. Settings: your language, password, passkeys and sign-in username (below).
  4. Default outbound: where your users' traffic leaves the server (for example through WARP or directly), unless a user, or an admin nearer to them, picks another. Outbounds are made on the Outbounds page. If an admin above you set it, you see it but can't change it. Apply the configs after a change.
  5. Configs for my users: extra configs added to the subscription of all your users and your sub-admins' users (below).
  6. My users' page: your own branding on your users' page (below).

At the bottom, a card shows whether your Telegram is connected to the panel's bot. With it you get notifications and backups, and can manage users from Telegram (Telegram bot).

docs.title: Password
docs.text:
Out of the box an admin has no password: the admin link alone signs you in. Set a password so that a leaked link is not enough.

  1. Generate makes a strong password and copies it.

A password needs at least 10 characters, a lowercase and an uppercase letter and a digit, and must not be a common password or your name or ID: the list under the box turns green as each rule is met. After saving, you sign in with your admin link and this password. If you forget it, the admin who added you can reset it.

docs.title: Passkeys
docs.text:
A passkey lets you sign in with your fingerprint, face or the screen lock of your phone or computer, with nothing to type and nothing to steal. Click Add passkey and confirm on your device.

  • Passkeys work only on a domain, not on an IP address: open the panel on one of its domains first.
  • Each domain of the panel needs its own passkey. Add passkey goes through them one by one; you confirm once on each.
  • To remove a device, click Remove next to it.

docs.title: Sign-in username
docs.text: Admins and agents (not super admins) can set a Sign-in username. Then they sign in with that username and their password, and the links they share carry no ID. It needs a strong password first. Super admins sign in with their admin link only.

docs.title: Configs for my users
docs.text:
Use it to give all your users one more server, for example the subscription of another panel or a config you made yourself.

  1. Add subscription: a link (https://…) that is fetched for each user.
  2. Add offline config: a config you paste (a vless://… link, or a JSON or YAML config).

For each one, choose which app format it is for, or Auto (All Formats). They are added on top of each user's own configs. Configs set by the admins above you are added too (the page shows how many). The same can be done for one admin on the Admins page, and for one user in the user's settings.

docs.title: My users' page
docs.text:
What your users (and your sub-admins' users) see on their page. Leave a field empty to keep what they get now (shown in the field).

  1. Brand title: shown at the top of the user page.
  2. Support link: for example your Telegram channel or chat.
  3. Support box text: shown in the support box (HTML is allowed).
  4. User page language: for users who have not picked their own.

Advanced has Custom user page: the address of your own static user page (for example your build of hiddify-user-front), which the panel then serves from its own domain.

docs.title: How this relates to the Admins page
docs.text:
On the Admins page you add admins under you (they are created as agents). Each one gets a link and a password, made for them when you save (shown only once: copy it then). For each admin you set:

  • Limits: max online users, max active users, max total users and max used traffic, counted over the admin and all of their sub-admins. The traffic limit can be for all time or reset every day, week or month. You can only give what you have.
  • Can add sub-admins, and the Permissions: add extra subscription links, add sub-admins, manage domains, define the free test, manage outbounds, customize the user page, change the preferred outbound. You can only give permissions you have yourself.
  • Their Default outbound and Configs for this admin's users: the same as on My account, for their branch.

What you set there is what they see on their own My account page.

Keep the panel safe

  • Set a password, and add a passkey if you open the panel on a domain.
  • Give each person their own admin, with only the permissions and limits they need, instead of sharing your link.
  • If a link leaked, change the admin's link (a new UUID) or reset their password on the Admins page.

docs.title: How to setup SSH proxy on HiddifyManager
SSH proxy setting on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
As you know, in version 8 of the HiddifyManager, a proxy for the SSH service has been created, which does not have any access to the server and can only be used as a proxy. This proxy is completely secure and has no fingerprints for identification. (except the SSH protocol itself, which is in general use)

Continue with this tutorial to learn how to make its settings on HiddifyManager panel.

docs.title: Configure SSH proxy settings
docs.text:
First, click Settings in the panel sidebar and find the SSH Proxy card.

Here you can enable or disable this protocol with the SSH Proxy switch. With Multiplex SSH on TLS Port on, SSH shares the TLS/HTTPS ports (such as 443) instead of using a dedicated public SSH port; clients connect to the same TLS port.

docs.title: Enable or disable proxy
docs.text:
You can also do this from the Protocols page: click Protocols in the sidebar, turn the SSH Proxy card on or off, and save.

If the panel asks you to apply the changes, do it so that they are applied to the server.

docs.title: Use config to connect
docs.text: After you apply the changes, the SSH configs are added to your users' configs automatically. Users can get them in two ways.

docs.title: Through the subscription link (recommended)
docs.text:
The SSH configs are included automatically in these subscription links of the user page: Auto, Hiddify / Singbox and Subscription link (also Subscription link b64). Users who already use one of these links only need to update their subscription in their app. The SSH configs then appear in the app's list of proxies, for example SSH HC D1.

The Full Xray and Clash Meta links do not include the SSH configs, because those clients don't support SSH.

The subscription links on the user page (All Configs). Auto, Hiddify / Singbox and Subscription link include the SSH configs.

docs.title: As a single config
docs.text:
1. On the user page, open All Configs in the menu at the top and type SSH in the search box. The SSH configs are listed under Individual Configs.

  2. Click Get Link next to one of them. A window opens with the config's link, its QR code and a Copy Link button. Copy the link and add it to your client app, or scan the QR code with the app.

    The Get Link window of an SSH config. The link and QR code in this picture are examples.

To use this proxy, use the Hiddify app or the SingBox app.

docs.title: How to import X-UI to HiddifyManager
How to import X-UI to HiddifyManager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The importer has no page in the admin panel: you run it with one command on the server, over SSH.

If you are moving from an X-UI panel (or a panel based on it, such as 3X-UI), Hiddify Manager can import its users, so they keep their accounts and their usage.

docs.title: What is imported
docs.text:
• Users: every client of the X-UI inbounds becomes a Hiddify Manager user with the same name, the same UUID (when it is a valid UUID, so the users' existing links keep their ID), the traffic limit, the traffic already used, the days left (no expiry in X-UI becomes 10 years), the Telegram ID and whether the user is enabled. The note "Imported from X-UI" is added to each one, and they belong to the admin who runs the import (the owner).
  • Reality domains: the destination site of every X-UI Reality inbound is added as a Direct domain with Reality TLS.

Inbounds, ports and other settings are not imported, because the two panels work differently. After the import, your users need their new Hiddify Manager links (their user page or subscription link).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Get the X-UI database. On the X-UI server it is usually /etc/x-ui/x-ui.db. Copy it to your Hiddify Manager server, for example into /tmp/. See How to transfer files between a server and a computer.
  2. Back up your panel first: Backup › Download Backup. See How to back up and restore.

  3. Connect to the Hiddify Manager server over SSH as root and run (change the path to your file):

    chmod 644 /tmp/x-ui.db
cd /opt/hiddify-manager && source scripts/common/utils.sh && hiddify-panel-cli xui-importer -x /tmp/x-ui.db

    The panel runs the command as its own user (hiddify-panel), so the file must be readable by it; that is why the file is in /tmp/ with chmod 644. The command prints success, or failed to import xui data with the reason.

  4. Open Users in the panel: the imported users are there. If Reality domains were added, open Actions and click Apply now (or Reinstall if the panel asks for it).

  5. Send each user their new link.

Note

If you run the import twice, users whose X-UI ID is a valid UUID are updated, not added again. Users with any other ID get a new random UUID each time, so they would be added twice: run the import once.

docs.title: How to contribute to this project
How to contribute to this project
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The development steps below follow the project’s own DEVELOPMENT.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. If they differ from this page, those files are right.

Hiddify Manager is free and open source, and its users help build it. You do not need to be a programmer to help.

docs.title: Ways to help without code
docs.text:
Report a bug or an ideaOpen an issue on GitHub: your version (top of the panel), what you did, what you expected and what happened, with logs or pictures. Hide your IPs, domains and links. Translate the panelThe texts are in translations.i18n/<language>.json in the Hiddify-Panel repository. Fix or add them and send a pull request. Improve this websiteThe pencil button at the top of each page opens it on GitHub. Fix a mistake or add a guide. Spread the wordTell others about Hiddify, make videos and guides, and answer users’ questions.

For other help (development, services), email hiddify@gmail.com.

docs.title: The repositories
docs.text:
Hiddify Manager is built from three repositories. Work on the dev branch in each.

Hiddify-ManagerInstall scripts, services and systemd units. Installed in /opt/hiddify-manager. Hiddify-PanelThe panel: Flask API, admin UI (admin_v2, Vue), config templates, certificates and translations. A submodule in services/panel/src. hiddify-user-frontThe user page (React). A submodule of the panel.

docs.title: Set up a development server
docs.text:
Work on a Linux server or VM (preferably Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04), as root. A development machine is a Hiddify server: the code lives where an installed Hiddify lives.

sudo -i
git clone --recurse-submodules -b dev https://github.com/hiddify/Hiddify-Manager.git /opt/hiddify-manager
cd /opt/hiddify-manager
make build
git -C services/panel/src checkout dev

make build installs everything (MySQL, Redis, HAProxy, Xray, the Hiddify core, the panel, …) in place. Then open /opt/hiddify-manager in VS Code (on a remote server, with the Remote - SSH extension). .vscode/launch.json has the run configurations.

docs.title: Day to day
docs.text:
• After changing the panel’s Python code, only restart the panel: systemctl restart hiddify-panel
  • The Admin V2 Dev (Flask + Vite) configuration in VS Code runs the panel with the debugger and the admin UI with live reload.
  • After changing a template or settings, click Apply now in the panel or run: make apply
  • data/ (server state) and generated/ (configs the panel builds) are not in git. Never edit or commit them.
  • Tests are in services/panel/tests (pytest). DEVELOPMENT.md shows how to run them.

docs.title: Send your change
docs.text:
1. On GitHub, Fork the repository you changed (the button at the top of the repository page).
  2. Make a new branch from dev, commit, and push it to your fork. If you changed both repositories, commit the panel first.

  3. Write the commit message in the Conventional Commits style, because the changelog is built from it. For example:

    fix: show the right expiry date on the user page
feat: add a Reality SNI scanner

  4. Open a pull request to the main repository’s dev branch. Describe the problem, your change and how you tested it, and add pictures for visual changes.

docs.title: How to use the API of Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5 (API v2.2)

Checked against the v14.5 panel. The endpoints can change between versions: the documentation inside your own panel (below) is always the one that matches it.

With the API you can manage the panel from your own programs or bots: create, change and delete users, read their usage, list admins and see the server's state.

docs.title: Where is the documentation
docs.text:
In the panel, click API in the sidebar (in the Settings group). It opens the panel's own interactive API documentation: every endpoint, its fields, a Try it button, and ready request code for many programming languages. Its address is:

https://<your domain>/<admin proxy path>/api/docs

The documentation page in the panel lists every endpoint by section (Api_Admin, Api_User, Api_Panel, Child for nodes):

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Your domain and the admin proxy path: the part after the domain in your admin link (https://<your domain>/<admin proxy path>/…). You can also see and change it in Settings › Very Advanced Settings › Proxy Path for Admins.
  • The API key: the UUID of an admin, the long ID in that admin's link (see the admin link and its format). Send it in the Hiddify-API-Key header. The API acts with that admin's rights: an agent only sees its own users.

Keep the key secret

The API key opens the panel with that admin's rights, even when the admin has a password. Use a separate admin with only the rights your program needs, and send the key only over https.

docs.title: The sections of the API (v2)
docs.text:
Section Base address What it is for Panel /<admin proxy path>/api/v2/panel/ info/ (the panel's version) and ping/ Admin /<admin proxy path>/api/v2/admin/ users (user/), admins (admin_user/), your own admin (me/), server state (server_status/), logs and more User /<client proxy path>/api/v2/user/ for one user, with their UUID as the key: me/ (usage and time left), all-configs/, mtproxies/, apps/, short/ (a short temporary link)

The client proxy path is in Settings › Very Advanced Settings › Proxy Path for Clients.

docs.title: Common tasks
docs.text:
Addresses below are under /<admin proxy path>/api/v2/admin/. All of them are in the documentation of your panel, with their fields.

You want to Request List, add, change or delete users GET / POST user/, then GET / PATCH / DELETE user/<uuid>/ Add many users at once POST users/bulk-create/ See the server's state (CPU, RAM, traffic) GET server_status/ Apply changes, reinstall, update or restart POST apply/apply/, apply/install/, apply/update/, apply/restart/ Download a backup GET backup/download/ See the outbounds GET outbounds/ See the nodes of a multi-server setup GET nodes/

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The panel's version:

curl "https://example.com/ADMIN_PATH/api/v2/panel/info/" \
-H "Hiddify-API-Key: ADMIN_UUID"

The list of users:

curl "https://example.com/ADMIN_PATH/api/v2/admin/user/" \
-H "Hiddify-API-Key: ADMIN_UUID"

Add a user with 30 GB for 30 days, with a monthly reset:

curl -X POST "https://example.com/ADMIN_PATH/api/v2/admin/user/" \
-H "Hiddify-API-Key: ADMIN_UUID" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"name": "Ali", "usage_limit_GB": 30, "package_days": 30, "mode": "monthly"}'

The answer has the new user's uuid. With it you can read the user (GET …/admin/user/<uuid>/), change it (PATCH, only the fields you send) or delete it (DELETE). The mode is the reset period: no_reset, monthly, weekly or daily.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use version 2 of the API (/api/v2/). Version 1 is old.
  • The fields and endpoints can change in a new version: after an update, check the documentation in your panel.
  • The paths end with /.

If you have a question or an idea for this page, write it in the comments below.

docs.title: Domain, Worker, CDN and tunneling
docs.text:
These guides help you connect domains to your HiddifyManager server: which domain type to choose, how to put your server behind a CDN such as Cloudflare, how to use Cloudflare Workers, how to find clean Cloudflare IPs, and how to keep subscription links reachable when other domains are blocked.

If you are new, start with Domain types and how to register them and What is CDN and how does it help us?.

docs.title: Domain types and how to register them
Domain types and how to register them
docs.text:
This page explains the kinds of domains you can add to HiddifyManager and how to set up each one at your DNS provider. Read it before you add your first domain to the panel.

A domain is a name such as sub.example.com that points to an IP address. A subdomain is the part you add in front of your main domain (sub in sub.example.com). A DNS record is the entry at your DNS provider that tells the internet which IP a name points to. For more basics, see Basic concepts.

Domain types changed in HiddifyManager v13

Since v13, every domain has a Mode and a TLS mode. The old modes were moved automatically when you upgraded:

  • auto_cdn_ip became CDN (with "Resolve IP" turned on).
  • fake became Direct with TLS mode Fake.
  • reality and special_reality_* became Direct with TLS mode Reality.
  • old_xtls_direct became Direct.
  • "Use only for subscription link" became the Subscription only mode.

docs.title: Domain modes in the panel
docs.text:
In the panel, open the Domains page and select Add domain. A short wizard asks for the domain, then "How is it set up?" (the mode), then "Which TLS?" (the TLS mode).

Mode When to use it What your DNS record must do Direct Users connect straight to your server. Point to your server's IP. On Cloudflare, the proxy must be off (DNS only, grey cloud). CDN Your server sits behind a CDN such as Cloudflare. This hides your server's IP and keeps working when the IP is blocked. Go through the CDN. On Cloudflare, the proxy must be on (Proxied, orange cloud). It must not resolve to your server's IP. Relay Users connect to another server in between, which passes traffic on to your server. More about relays Point to the in-between (relay) server, not to your server. Cloudflare Worker Traffic reaches your server through a Cloudflare Worker. More about workers The domain must be on Cloudflare. Subscription only Only for users' subscription links, no proxies. If your proxy domains get blocked, users can still update their subscription and get new working configs. More about subscription domains Point to your server or go through a CDN. Behind a CDN is best.

The TLS mode decides which certificate the domain uses:

TLS mode Meaning Valid TLS A real certificate that the panel gets and renews for you automatically. Use this in almost all cases. CDN, Cloudflare Worker and Subscription only domains always use it. Fake Decoy TLS with another site's name (for example soft98.ir) to pass an SNI whitelist. Not recommended, because it can get your server filtered. Only for Direct or Relay. More about fake domains Reality Borrows another real site's TLS with the Reality protocol. You do not need to own the domain. Only for Direct or Relay. DNS For DNS tunnels only.

The panel checks the DNS record when you save. For example, a Direct domain must point to your server's IP, and a CDN domain must not point to it directly. If the check fails, fix the DNS record, wait a few minutes, and save again.

Let the panel create the DNS records

If your domain is on Cloudflare, you can give the panel a Cloudflare API token. The panel then creates the DNS record for each new domain (proxy on for CDN, off for Direct). See Get Cloudflare API.

docs.title: How to register a domain
docs.text: You can get a free subdomain or use a domain you bought.

docs.title: Free subdomain (FreeDNS)
docs.text:
FreeDNS (afraid.org) lets you create a subdomain on domains that other people have shared publicly.

  1. Create an account. You need a real email address. The form asks you to confirm that you do not live in a country under U.S. sanctions (Iran is one of them).

  2. Open the domain registry. Pick a public domain that has few hosts. Domains ending in .com, .org or .net are best.

  3. Create your subdomain on that domain and set its address to your server’s IP.

docs.title: A domain you bought, on Cloudflare
docs.text:
You can manage a domain you bought with any DNS provider. These steps use Cloudflare.

  1. Create a Cloudflare account and log in.

  2. Add the domain to Cloudflare:

    • In the sidebar, open Domains › Overview (if the sidebar is collapsed, click the globe icon).

    • Click Add domain.

    • Choose Connect a domain.

    • Type your main domain (for example example.com) in Domain name. Leave the other options as they are and click Continue.

    The Add a domain card on the Account home page does the same.

  3. Choose a plan: click Select plan under Free. The free plan is enough.

  4. Cloudflare finds the domain’s current DNS records and lists them. Check them and click Continue to activation.

  5. Cloudflare shows you two nameservers. Go to the site where you bought the domain, delete its current nameservers and put these two in their place.

  6. Wait until the domain’s status in Domains › Overview changes to Active. This takes from a few minutes to a day. Until the nameservers are changed, the Status column shows a message like Invalid nameservers.

  7. Click the domain, open DNS › Records in the sidebar and click Add record.

  8. Fill in the record:

    • Type: A (for the server’s IPv4 address).
    • Name: the subdomain you want, for example sub.
    • IPv4 address: your server’s IP.
    • Proxy status: turn it off (DNS only, grey cloud). A Direct domain must not be proxied.
    • TTL: leave it on Auto.

    Above the form, Cloudflare sums up the record (for example sub.example.com points to 203.0.113.10). Click Save.

  9. If your server also has an IPv6 address, add a second record the same way, with Type AAAA and the IPv6 address.

docs.title: Check that the direct domain works
docs.text:
DNS changes can take a few minutes to spread. Then, on your own computer, run:

ping sub.example.com

You should see your server’s IP in the answer. You can also use nslookup or dig. If you see a different IP or "unknown host", check the record and wait a little longer. To learn more, read this article on DNS (Persian).

A CDN (content delivery network) is a network of servers that sits between your users and your server. Users connect to the CDN, and the CDN passes the traffic to your server. What is CDN and how does it help us?

These steps use Cloudflare. For other CDNs, see GCore and Amazon CloudFront.

docs.title: Add the direct domain to the panel
docs.text:
In the panel, click Domains › Add domain and type the domain. Under How is it set up? choose Direct, under Which TLS? choose Valid TLS, and finish the steps.

If the panel shows DNS does not match next to the option, the DNS record does not reach this server’s IP yet. Wait a few minutes; the panel checks again when you save.

docs.title: Add the CDN record on Cloudflare
docs.text:
1. Add your domain to Cloudflare as described in the direct domain section above (steps 1 to 6).
  2. Go to DNS › Records and click Add record.
  3. Use Type A (or AAAA for IPv6), a new subdomain name (for example cdn), and your server’s IP.
  4. Leave Proxy status on (Proxied, orange cloud). This is the only difference from a direct domain.
  5. Click Save.

docs.title: Check that the CDN domain works
docs.text:
When you ping this subdomain, you should see one of Cloudflare’s IPs, not your server’s IP. This hides your server. The Cloudflare IP can change over time.

Sometimes the Cloudflare IPs that your users get are blocked or slow in Iran. In that case, find working IPs with the panel’s own Scanner (Tools › Scanner), or see Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP.

docs.title: Cloudflare SSL/TLS settings
docs.text:
TLS is the encryption that protects the connection between the user and the server. A certificate proves that a server really owns a domain. HiddifyManager gets a real certificate for your domain, so Cloudflare can connect to your server over TLS.

  1. Open your domain in Cloudflare, open SSL/TLS in the sidebar and click Configure. The same page shows, under Traffic Served Over TLS, which TLS versions your traffic used; newer is safer.

  2. Choose the encryption mode Full (Strict) or Full. Do not use Flexible. If Automatic SSL/TLS (recommended) is selected, Cloudflare picks the most secure mode that works by itself, and you can leave it.

  3. Open Network in the sidebar and turn on gRPC and WebSockets. HiddifyManager’s CDN proxies use WebSocket, gRPC, HTTPUpgrade and XHTTP.

Older guides told you to turn on SSL/TLS Recommender. Cloudflare replaced it with Automatic SSL/TLS, so you do not need it.

docs.title: Add the CDN domain to the panel
docs.text:
In the panel, click Domains › Add domain, type the domain, and under How is it set up? choose CDN. CDN domains always use Valid TLS.

If the panel warns that the domain does not look like it is behind a CDN, turn the proxy (orange cloud) on in Cloudflare.

docs.title: Relay domain registration
docs.text: A relay domain is registered like a direct domain, but its record points to the in-between (relay) server instead of your main server. Read more

docs.title: Fake and Reality domains
docs.text: With the Fake or Reality TLS mode, you use the name of another site that you do not own, so you do not register anything at a DNS provider. You only add the name in the panel. See How to create and use fake domain.

docs.text: Fake domainDecoy TLS with another site's nameWildcard subdomainsA fresh subdomain for every userAutomatic subdomains on CloudflareLet the panel make your DNS recordsDomain frontingHide your domain behind another site

docs.title: How to get and use the Cloudflare API key
Get Cloudflare API
docs.text:
With a Cloudflare API token, the panel manages the DNS records of your domains for you: when you add a domain (a subdomain of a domain that is on your Cloudflare account) on the Domains page, the panel creates or updates its A / AAAA record with your server's IP, proxied (orange cloud) for CDN domains and DNS only for direct ones. This page is for Hiddify Manager v14.5.

Note

Older versions also created Cloudflare Workers with this token. v14.5 does not: see How to use the Cloudflare worker domain.

Follow the steps below to get the token.

  1. Sign in to your Cloudflare account and add your domain to it. More: Domain types and how to register them.

  2. Open My Profile › API Tokens (the profile icon at the top right › My Profile › API Tokens). The page is called User API Tokens. Click Create Token.

  3. Under Token name, type a name, for example HiddifyManager. Under Policies, click Edit zone DNS.

  4. A Zone policy with DNS Write is added. Click its pencil to choose which domains it covers.

  5. Keep Include and choose Specific zone and your domain, or All zones if you will use several domains. Under DNS & Zones, DNS must be on Edit: the template already did this.

  6. Leave Token expiration on No expiration (or choose a date), and click Continue to summary at the bottom.

  7. Check the summary (DNS: Edit) and click Create Token.

  8. Copy the token. Cloudflare shows it only once; if you lose it, create a new one.

docs.title: How to use Cloudflare API in HiddifyManager
docs.text:
After creating the token, open Settings in the panel and turn on Show Advanced Settings at the top of the page. In the Very Advanced Settings card, paste the token into Cloudflare API and save.

Now, when you add a domain on the Domains page whose main domain is on your Cloudflare account, its DNS record is created automatically. If the token is wrong or lacks the permission, saving the domain shows a Cloudflare error with the reason.

docs.title: Guide for domain fronting
docs.text:
Domain fronting is a way to bypass the filtering system through a CDN. The filter sees the name of another site (the SNI), for example discord.com, while the Host of the request points to your own domain on the same CDN; the CDN delivers the traffic to your server.

It only works when the other site is on the same CDN as your domain (for example, two Cloudflare sites), and it does not work on every CDN or every operator, so test it with a few users first. This page is for Hiddify Manager v14.5.

CDNs can turn domain fronting off

Many CDNs don't allow domain fronting. Amazon CloudFront, Google and Microsoft Azure already block it, and any CDN can start blocking it at any time, without notice. Using it may also be against the CDN's terms and can get your CDN account suspended.

  • Don't make fronting the only way your users connect. Keep at least one other config (for example Reality or a normal CDN config) in the subscription.
  • If fronting configs suddenly stop working for everyone, the CDN has probably blocked it. Clear the Domain fronting field (step 5 below) and use other configs.

docs.title: Domain registration on CDN
docs.text:
• First, you need to register on the CDN site of your choice and register a domain in it. Tutorial for domain registration

  • After that, register a DNS record and turn on its proxy (on Cloudflare: the orange cloud).

docs.title: Domain fronting settings on HiddifyManager panel
docs.text:
1. In the panel, open Domains and click Add domain.
  2. Type your subdomain (the one with the proxy turned on) and click Check.
  3. In How is it set up? choose CDN, and in Which TLS? choose Valid TLS. Finish the wizard (name and certificate).
  1. Click the pencil next to the new domain and open Advanced.
  2. In Domain fronting, enter one or more sites that are on the same CDN but not filtered, separated by commas (for example another-site.com, cdn-site.net). To check which CDN a site uses, look up its IP with a DNS lookup tool. Leave the field empty to turn fronting off.
  3. If needed, put clean IPs of that CDN in Force configs to use these IPs / domains (see finding a clean Cloudflare IP).
  4. Save, then click Apply now on the Actions page.

The work is done: this domain's configs now use domain fronting. On the Domains page the domain shows a fronting badge.

Changed in v13

Older versions had a global Domain Fronting settings group. Since v13 fronting is set on each CDN domain, as above.

docs.title: Add config to the subscription link
docs.text: As you know, it is always recommended to keep subscription links separate from configs. Therefore, if you have already created a subscription link, just add the new CDN domain in its settings so that the new domain fronting configurations are also connected to the subscription link. How to create subscription link on HiddifyManager

docs.title: What is Cloudflare's clean IP and how to find it
Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP
docs.text:
The largest CDN service provider in the world is Cloudflare, and you probably know; Due to the severe filtering of the Internet in Iran, there is a lot of disruption to its services because it is not possible for the filter to completely filter it, but it can cause disruption. Here, if you also use CDN Cloudflare services; You will be affected by these disorders. To reduce the impact of these disturbances, you should find clean IPs (IPs that are not disturbed).

Here are some ways of working for this issue.

tip

Before starting, it is emphasized that all these tests must be done on the client system without connecting to VPN.

docs.title: Using the HiddifyManager scanner (easiest)
docs.text:
Since v14.5 the panel has its own scanner: Tools › Scanner (or Open the scanner under the Force configs to use these IPs / domains field of a CDN domain). It needs a CDN domain on the Domains page first.

  1. Open the panel on the operator you want IPs for, with the VPN off (for example on a phone on MCI). The scan runs in your browser, on the internet it is on now.
  2. Which domain? Choose the CDN domain (and, if asked, the operator whose users will get the IPs).
  3. Find IPs That Work: press Start. The panel tests Cloudflare IP ranges from your browser and keeps the fastest. Scan Settings sets how many ranges and IPs are tested.

  4. Add Them to the Domain: check the list (remove some, or add your own IPs, ranges or domains) and click Save to the Domain. The IPs are written into the domain's Force configs to use these IPs / domains field for that operator; the other operators keep theirs.

  5. Click Apply now on the Actions page. Repeat on each operator (for example a phone on MCI, then one on Irancell).

The scanner has two more tabs: Fragment (try TLS fragment presets for a CDN domain) and REALITY SNI (find SNIs that work for Reality). If the IPs found still do not connect, Full test with upload, from another device gives you a command to run on a phone or computer on that operator: some operators cut a connection after a little upload, which a browser cannot test.

The external scanners below are still useful if you prefer them.

docs.title: Using Bashsiz's scanner
docs.text:
Mr. Bashsiz is an Iranian engineer who has developed a program called CFScanner, which can be used to test the list of Cloudflare IPs on different networks and reach the clean Cloudflare IPs.

This program has been released in several versions including Linux and Windows. Versions available until the date of editing this article: - Bash - Docker - Windows - Python - Golang - Android

The project is still maintained (latest Windows release: April 2026). We suggest the Bash (Linux), Windows and Android versions; the Python and Go versions have open problems on GitHub.

To do this, first download the desired version here and then follow how to run it based on the desired operating system.

Download the program files.

This program has prerequisites that must be installed in advance. jq git tput bc curl parallel

Then first clone it on your system with the following code. 

git clone https://github.com/MortezaBashsiz/CFScanner.git
Go to the app download folder and run access to it. 
cd CFScanner/bash
chmod +x ../bin/*
Download the config.real file. 
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MortezaBashsiz/CFScanner/main/bash/ClientConfig.json -o config.real
It is recommended to change the config.real file based on your configuration.

If you want to have your own configuration file, save it under a different name that will not change when the script is updated.

First, there must be prerequisites that will be explained in order:

  • Download the Windows scanner app from the project's GitHub
  • Install .NET Desktop Runtime 6 app from the main application site given below
https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/6.0
  • Checking TLS Handshake For this, you must first enter the program folder and open Command Prompt inside that folder. That is, Shift+Right click on the folder and select Open in Windows Terminal.

Run the following command in the terminal environment.

‍‍.\v2ray.exe tls ping sub.yourdomain.com

Put your subdomain instead of sub.yourdomain.com. If handshake succeeded message appears; It means that the scanner is ready to use, otherwise you should make temporary changes in the certificate settings on Cloudflare website.

Set the TLS version to TLS 1.0 and disable the TLS 1.3 option.

  • Note: Don't forget to return these options to the first state after testing.

    "protocol": "socks",
    "settings": {
...
And also apply this change in outbound.

   "settings": {

       "address": "IP.IP.IP.IP",
...

Now, for ease of work, some examples of configuration templates that iSegaro has worked hard to present; You can choose one according to your needs.

  • Be careful, in these structures, only in the outbounds part, you should change the configuration specifications including 5 parts Port, UUID, PATH, HOST, SNI, which are marked with the word xxxxx, so wherever there is the word xxxxx, change it only depending on your configuration. Finally, present your configuration according to the examples for the next step or use the default configuration.

Now suppose you have completed the prerequisites; All you need is the config file of the sample program or the config file created by yourself, which is in Json format; From the menu Tools > Add custom v2ray config, put it in the program so that the scan is done based on it, otherwise the program will scan with the default configuration.

  1. From Tools > Add custom v2ray config, you can give the desired file according to the described pattern to the software so that the scan can be done based on it.

  2. You can specify the download or upload test type or both.

  3. In this section, you can specify the number of simultaneous IPs to be tested by the scanner. It is suggested to increase this number step by step and increase or decrease it based on the CPU processing power of your system. Its default value is 4.

  4. The fastest IP will be displayed after the scan is completed

  5. The range of tested IPs is displayed

  6. From this section, you can give the software the IP range you want to scan based on it.

  7. Suggestion: You can set the software to scan the entire default IP range once. For the next time, you can just scan this output (with higher accuracy), you will probably get a better result. Also, if you take an upload test, you will probably get a better result. All this depends on your efforts and creativity.

Older scanners

The scanners by Vahid Farid (cf-ip-scanner-py) and Safa Safarian (ss-cloud-scanner) that used to be on this page have not been updated since 2024 and are no longer maintained, so they were taken out of this guide. Use the panel scanner or CFScanner instead.

docs.text: (Click here)

docs.title: Run the script
docs.text:
Go to the location of the downloaded script file and then run the script as shown below.

bash cfScanner.sh SUBNET DOWN threads tryCount config.real speed custom.subnets

For example:

bash cfScanner.sh SUBNET DOWN 8 1 config.real 100 custom.subnets
Finally, the test result is placed in the result folder, which you can view and use. More information on the program wiki.

docs.title: What to do after finding a clean IP?
docs.text:
If you used the panel's scanner, the IPs are already saved in your CDN domain. For IPs from other scanners:

  • Put them straight into the CDN domain's Force configs to use these IPs / domains field (Domains › pencil › Advanced), one per line, optionally with the operator's code after each one (for example 1.1.1.1 MCI); or
  • Better: create a DNS record on Cloudflare with the proxy off that points to the clean IP (for example mci.yourdomain.com), and put that name in the field. When you need a new clean IP later, you only change the DNS record.

More: Domain types and how to register them, CDN domain and How to use AutoCDN IP domain (the format per operator).

docs.title: How to use AutoCDN IP domain
How to use AutoCDN IP domain
docs.text:
One of the constant concerns of Cloudflare CDN users is finding clean IPs, and a clean IP that works on one operator often does not work on another. The AutoCDN IP feature solves this: you give the panel a list of clean IPs (or host names) per operator, and each user gets, in their configs, the IP for their own operator.

Since v13 there is no separate auto_cdn_ip mode

In older versions this was a domain mode called auto_cdn_ip. Since v13 it is part of the normal CDN domain: the field Force configs to use these IPs / domains. This page is for Hiddify Manager v14.5.

One big advantage: if the hostname you list the IPs with is itself blocked (for example ircf.space), a user with a normal CDN config cannot resolve it and cannot connect; here the panel resolves it itself and puts the IP in the config.

docs.title: Domain registration
docs.text:
1. Register your subdomain on Cloudflare with the proxy turned on (orange cloud). See Domain types and how to register them.
  2. In the panel, open Domains, click Add domain, type the subdomain and click Check.
  3. Choose CDN and Valid TLS, then finish the wizard. Give it a Display name if you like: it is shown in the users' apps instead of the domain.
  4. Click the pencil next to the domain and open Advanced. The field Force configs to use these IPs / domains is there (see below).
  5. Save, then click Apply now on the Actions page.

More about the CDN domain and its other fields: CDN domain.

docs.title: Force configs to use these IPs / domains
docs.text:
Whatever you put here goes into the users' links instead of the domain's own IP. You can write:

  • One or more IPs or host names, separated by commas or new lines: everyone gets them.
  • Per operator: an IP, a range (CIDR) or a host name, then the operator's code, for example 1.1.1.1 MCI. Each user gets the address of their operator. Addresses with no code are for every other operator.

For example, the list of clean-IP host names kept up to date by ircf.space (paste the lines of the operators you need):

mci.ircf.space MCI
mcix.ircf.space MCI
mtn.ircf.space MTN
mtnx.ircf.space MTN
mkh.ircf.space MKH
rtl.ircf.space RTL
hwb.ircf.space HWB
ast.ircf.space AST
sht.ircf.space SHT
prs.ircf.space PRS
mbt.ircf.space MBT
ask.ircf.space ASK
rsp.ircf.space RSP
afn.ircf.space AFN
ztl.ircf.space ZTL
psm.ircf.space PSM
arx.ircf.space ARX
smt.ircf.space SMT

Or your own records (DNS only, proxy off), or IPs:

mci.yourdomain.com MCI
mtn.yourdomain.com MTN
1.1.1.1 MKH

If the field is empty, the configs use the domain itself.

Find clean IPs with the panel's scanner

Under the field, Open the scanner opens the panel's Scanner (Tools › Scanner). It scans Cloudflare IPs on your own internet and saves the best ones in this field, per operator. See also Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP.

Key point: the panel picks the operator from the IP the user updates their subscription from. So update the subscription in the app with the VPN disconnected; after changing operator (for example from Wi-Fi to mobile data), disconnect the VPN and update the subscription again.

docs.title: Show Configs of Domains
docs.text:
Show configs of (in the same dialog) limits which domains' configs users see when they open their page on this domain. For non-commercial use you usually do not need it.

The work is done. Now you can go to the user link and view the configurations related to this domain.
