docs.title: How to add a relay server (domain) to HiddifyManager
docs.text: This page shows you how to tell your Hiddify Manager panel about a relay server, so that your users get configs that go through it. Read it after you have set up the relay server itself.

docs.title: What is a relay server and why use one?
docs.text:
A relay server (also called an intermediate or bridge server) is a second, usually cheap, server that sits between your users and your main HiddifyManager server. Users connect to the relay; the relay passes their traffic on to the main server, and the main server sends it to the internet.

You may want one when:

  • the main server's IP is blocked or very slow from your users' country, but a server inside the country can still reach it;
  • you want to hide the main server's IP from users;
  • you want an address that is cheap to replace if it gets blocked (you only change the relay, not the main server).

The relay does not run Hiddify Manager. It only forwards traffic, using one of the tunnel methods below.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A main server with Hiddify Manager installed. See the installation guide.
  • A relay server that already forwards ports 443 and 80 to the main server. Set it up with one of these methods:
    1. Hiddify Relay Builder (all methods in one menu, easiest)
    2. IP-Tables method
    3. GOST method
    4. WST method
    5. Dokodemo-Door method
    6. HA-Proxy method
  • A domain you control (for example on Cloudflare).

Why forward port 80 too?

The panel gets free TLS certificates (Let's Encrypt) by answering a check on port 80. For a relay domain, that check arrives at the relay server, so the relay must forward port 80 as well as 443 to the main server.

docs.title: Step 1: Point a subdomain at the relay server
docs.text:
1. Open your DNS provider (for example the Cloudflare dashboard).
  2. Add an A record for a new subdomain, for example relay.example.com, with the relay server's IP as the value.
  3. If you use Cloudflare, keep the proxy off (grey cloud, "DNS only").

docs.title: Step 2: Add the domain in the panel
docs.text:
1. Log in to your Hiddify Manager admin panel.
  2. In the side menu, open Domains (in the Settings group).
  3. Click Add domain. A wizard opens with four steps: Domain, Mode, Name and Certificate.

  4. In Domain, type your relay subdomain (for example relay.example.com) and click Check. The panel checks its DNS. It should say the domain points to another server (your relay's IP). That is expected.

  5. In Mode, under How is it set up?, choose Relay.

  6. Under Which TLS?, keep Valid TLS (a real certificate, issued automatically) unless you know you need something else. Click Next.

  7. In Name, enter a display name if you like. Users see this name in their apps instead of the domain.

  8. Finish the Certificate step, then apply the changes when the panel asks you to.

If the certificate step fails, check that the relay forwards port 80 to the main server and that the DNS record has had a few minutes to spread.

Fake or Reality TLS on a relay domain

If you pick a TLS mode other than a real certificate for a relay domain, the panel needs the relay server's IP. Enter it under Advanced → Force configs to use these IPs / domains, or the panel will not let you save.

docs.title: Step 3: Show the relay configs in your subscription link
docs.text:
It is good practice to keep the domain users open their subscription on separate from the domains that carry traffic. To add the relay configs to that subscription domain:

  1. In Domains, click the edit (pencil) button of your subscription domain (for example sublink.example.com).
  2. In Show configs of, select your relay domain, and any other domains you want users to get.
  3. Save, then apply the changes.

Now open a user's page using the subscription domain. You will see configs that use the relay domain. Users can add them one by one, or simply update their subscription in their app.

Screenshot from an older panel version

This screenshot comes from the older admin pages. Labels and layout in current versions differ; follow the steps above.

Showing the relay configs on the subscription domain:

docs.title: How to create and use fake domain
How to create and use fake domain
docs.text:
A fake domain is another website's domain, for example yahoo.com, whose name is only put in the configs as the SNI. The user's traffic still goes to your server's IP, but to the filtering system it looks as if the user is connecting to that website. This helps to get past an "SNI whitelist", where only connections to certain websites are allowed.

The domain is not yours, so you don't buy it or set up its DNS. You only add it in the panel.

Note

The panel itself marks fake TLS as "Not recommended". If you want to use another website's domain, Reality is usually the safer and more stable choice. Use a fake domain only when other methods do not work.

docs.title: Add a fake domain
docs.text:
1. In the side menu, in the Settings group, open Domains.

  2. Click Add domain. A wizard opens with four steps: Domain, Mode, Name and Certificate.

  3. In the Domain step, enter the website's domain you want and click Check. The domain is not yours, so its DNS does not point to your server. This is expected.

  4. In the Mode step, under How is it set up? choose Direct, and under Which TLS? choose Fake. Then click Next.

  5. Finish the Name and Certificate steps. The domain shows in the domains list with the Direct and Fake badges.

Which website should I pick?

Pick a website that is open in your users' country and answers on port 443. This list shows some websites and ports you can use.

docs.title: Use another IP or domain in the configs (optional)
docs.text:
By default, the fake domain's configs connect to your server's IP. To put another IP, or your server's direct domain, in the configs instead:

  1. On the Domains page, click the pencil icon next to the fake domain.
  2. Open Advanced.
  3. In the Force configs to use these IPs / domains card, type the IP or your server's direct domain and press Enter. Click Add to enter more than one.

  4. Click Save.

docs.title: Bring the fake configs into the subscription link
docs.text:
Users get their configs from their user page, which opens on one of your real domains. The Show configs of setting of that domain decides which domains' configs are in the subscription link.

  • If All domains is on (the default), the fake domain's configs are added to the subscription link by themselves. Nothing else is needed.

  • If you show only some domains:

    1. Edit the domain your users open their user page with.
    2. Under Show configs of, tick the fake domain.
    3. Click Save.

Then ask your users to update the subscription in their app to get the new configs.

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text:
1. In the side menu, in the Settings group, open Protocols.
  2. Make sure Allow HTTP Connection is on.

  3. If you also want to use VMess, turn on VMess.

docs.title: The fake domain's proxies
docs.text:
In the fake domain's edit window, Custom proxies decides which proxies are made for this domain:

  • Automatic (recommended): every proxy that works with this domain is made.
  • Choose: only the proxies you tick are made. A proxy from the SNI gateway group (such as Telegram FakeTLS) works alone and is never mixed with the L7 gateway proxies. If you tick nothing, it works like Automatic.

docs.title: How to create subscription link on HiddifyManager
How to create subscription link on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
HiddifyManager is based on the principle of reducing the possibility of server filtering as much as possible. One of the practical ways in this field is to separate the configs from the subscription links. In this case, your client will always receive the latest configuration information through the subscription link. The schematic related to this work is as follows.

As you can see in the figure above, the subscription link is connected separately from the server to the users, and the task of this link is to transfer information about various connections such as CDN, AutoCDN, Relay, etc. That is, the connections themselves establish the connection between the server and the client separately, and the subscription link transfers the information related to these connections from the server to the client. For example, if a new clean IP is placed in the CDN connection, the information about this new IP is transferred to your client through the subscription link. On the other hand, clients go to the free Internet through different connections that are separate from the subscription link. With this method, the information of the subscription links (subscription) is separated from the connections (configs) and because the traffic of the configs is not placed on these links, the use of the subscription links will not be filtered in any way and will always be available.

docs.title: How to create domain for subscription link on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
To do this, in the panel's sidebar, under Settings, click Domains, and then click Add domain.

  • In the Domain step, type your subscription domain and click Check.
  • In the Mode step, under How is it set up?, choose Subscription only. As the panel says, this mode is best behind a CDN: if your proxy domains get blocked, users can still update their subscription and receive new working configs.

  • In the Name step, choose a name if you wish. This name is used for display only.

Make sure to use standard characters such as letters and numbers.

  • Finish the wizard.
  • And finally, check Show configs of for the new domain in the Domains list. By default it is All domains, so the subscription link carries the configs of all the domains you created for different connections (for example, several domains for CDN or worker). If you want only some of them, click the pencil (edit) icon of the subscription domain and select those domains in the Show configs of field, then press Save.
  • Then apply the changes if the panel asks you to (or click Actions in the sidebar and press Apply now). The work is done. You created a separate domain for subscription links and attached it to the configs.

You can also use a PHP site for the subscription link, in which case the schematic will look like this.

For its tutorial, go here.

docs.title: How to setup and use Cloudflare workers (Manual way)
How to set up and use Cloudflare workers (Manual way)
What are Workers?
docs.text:
Cloudflare Workers runs a small piece of code on Cloudflare's servers. In this tutorial the worker takes your users' requests and sends them on to your HiddifyManager server. Users only see the worker's address; your server's domain and IP stay hidden behind it.

Free plan limit

On Cloudflare's free plan, Workers handle 100,000 requests a day. This is not enough for a server with many users.

docs.title: 1. Requirements on Cloudflare
docs.text:
1. Have an active domain on Cloudflare. If you don't, see How to use Cloudflare CDN.
  2. Make a subdomain for your server (for example sub.yourdomain.com): in DNS > Records, an A record with your server's IP. The worker works with this record's proxy on or off.
  3. In SSL/TLS > Overview, set the encryption mode to Full.
  4. Add the same subdomain to your HiddifyManager panel as a domain, so the panel gets a certificate for it.

docs.title: 2. Make the worker
docs.text:
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard side menu, open Compute > Workers & Pages.

  2. Click Create application. This page also shows the free plan's daily quota (100,000 requests).

  3. Choose Start with Hello World!.

  4. In Worker name, type a name for the worker (for example hiddify-worker). The worker's address is made from it: worker-name.account-subdomain.workers.dev. Then click Deploy.

  5. The worker's page opens with its workers.dev address at the top. Click Edit code to open the code editor.

  6. In the editor, delete all the default code in worker.js and put this code in its place:

    addEventListener(
"fetch", event => {
const ip = event.request.headers.get('cf-connecting-ip') || event.request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') || (event.request.socket && event.request.socket.remoteAddress);
let url = new URL(event.request.url);
const worker_domain=url.hostname;
url.hostname = "sub.yourdomain.com";
url.protocol = event.request.headers.get('x-forwarded-proto') || "https";
let request = new Request(url, event.request);
if (ip)
request.headers.set('cf-connecting-ip', ip);
request.headers.set('Host', worker_domain);
event.respondWith(
fetch(request)
)
}
)

  7. On line 7, replace sub.yourdomain.com with your server's subdomain from step 1.

  8. Click Deploy above the editor. Version saved means the code is saved and published.

Errors in the preview

If the editor's preview pane (on the right) shows an error, don't worry: publish the code.

Code format

This code uses the older Workers format (addEventListener). Cloudflare still supports it, but has marked it deprecated and recommends the newer Module format.

docs.title: 3. The worker's address
docs.text:
You can see the worker's workers.dev address on the worker's Domains tab, under Worker URL. It is better to give the worker a custom domain on your own domain instead, because workers.dev addresses can be blocked:

  1. On the worker's page, open the Domains tab.
  2. Under Custom Domains and Routes, click Add Domain.

  3. In the Connect domain window pick your domain, enter a new subdomain in Subdomain (for example w) and click Add domain. Cloudflare makes its DNS record and certificate by itself. The subdomain must not already have a CNAME record.

docs.title: 4. Add the worker's address to HiddifyManager
docs.text:
1. In the panel side menu, in the Settings group, open Domains and click Add domain.
  2. In the Domain step, enter the worker's address (the custom domain or the workers.dev address) without https:// and click Check.

  3. In the Mode step, choose CDN, keep Valid TLS and click Next.

  4. Finish the Name and Certificate steps to add the domain.

docs.title: 5. Bring the worker configs into the subscription link
docs.text:
If Show configs of on the domain your users open their user page with is set to All domains (the default), the worker's configs are added by themselves. If you show only some domains, edit that domain and tick the worker domain under Show configs of.

Then ask your users to update the subscription in their app.

docs.title: How to setup relay server using Hiddify Relay Builder (all in one app)
docs.text:
Hiddify Relay Builder is a menu-driven script that turns a fresh server into a relay server in a few steps. Use it if you want a relay but do not want to type tunnel commands by hand.

A relay server is a second server, usually inside your own country, that your users connect to. It forwards their traffic to your main HiddifyManager server abroad. This helps when the main server's IP is blocked or slow from your country. Read more about relay servers.

The script can build the tunnel between the relay and the main server with these methods (a tunnel here simply means "a way to pass traffic from one server to the other"):

  1. IP-Tables
  2. GOST
  3. Dokodemo-Door (called tunnel in current Xray)
  4. HA-Proxy
  5. Socat (old, see below)
  6. WST (old, see below)

It also has a few basic tools: DNS settings, a server update and a connectivity test.

Project status

The script lives at github.com/hiddify/hiddify-relay. Its last change was in October 2024, so treat it as "works, but not actively developed". In the current version, Socat and WST are marked "No longer supported" and are hidden under Options → DeprecatedTunnel.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A main server with Hiddify Manager already installed. See the installation guide.
  • A relay server running Ubuntu or Debian (the script also accepts CentOS, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and Fedora).
  • SSH access to the relay server as root, or as a user that can run sudo without typing a password. The script stops with "This user does not have sudo permissions" otherwise. New to SSH? See how to connect to a server via SSH.
  • The IP address (or a direct, non-CDN domain) of your main server.

docs.title: ⚙️ Installation and setup
docs.text:
1. Connect to your relay server over SSH.

  2. Run this command:

    bash <(curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hiddify/hiddify-relay/main/install.sh)

  3. Wait while it installs a few helper packages and downloads itself to /opt/hiddify-relay. When it finishes, you see the main menu:

Use the arrow keys to move, Enter to select, and Tab to jump to the OK/Cancel buttons.

To open the menu again later, log in to the relay server again and type:

relay

Forward both ports 443 and 80

Hiddify Manager uses port 443 for most configs, and needs port 80 to get its free TLS certificate for the relay domain. Whichever method you choose, make sure both ports reach the main server. In methods that ask for one port at a time, add 443 first and then use Add to add 80.

Open the section for the method you want:

In the main menu, select IP-Tables.

Install

  1. Enter the IP of your main server.
  2. Enter the ports to forward, separated by commas. The default 80,443 is right for Hiddify Manager.
  3. When you see IPTables installation completed., the tunnel is active.

Status

Shows the ports used by the IP-Tables tunnel.

Uninstall

Deletes the IP-Tables rules.

Tip!

If you added your own IP-Tables rules by hand, they may be deleted too.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

In the main menu, select GOST. The script installs the latest GOST (v3) from the official go-gost installer.

Install

  1. Wait until GOST is installed.
  2. Enter the domain or IP of your main server. If you use a domain, it must point straight to the main server (not through a CDN).
  3. Enter the port, for example 443.
  4. When you see GOST tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and whether the tunnel is running.

Add

  • Adds another port, or a connection to another main server.
  • Enter the main server's domain or IP, then the port. Use this to add port 80.
  • Check the result with Status.

Remove

Removes one port and its domain from the GOST configuration.

Uninstall

Removes the GOST tunnel from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

In the main menu, select Dokodemo-Door. This method uses the Xray core, installed with the official XTLS installer.

Dokodemo-Door is now called tunnel in Xray

Since 2025 the Xray project calls the dokodemo-door inbound tunnel. The Relay Builder script still uses the old name in its menu and config, but Xray accepts both names, so nothing breaks. To build the tunnel by hand with the new name, see Dokodemo-Door (tunnel) relay tutorial.

Install

  1. Wait for the Xray core to be installed on the relay server.
  2. Enter the IP address or domain of your main server.
  3. Enter one port, for example 443.
  4. When you see Xray installed successfully!, the tunnel is running.

Very important

Enter only one port here, so that its inbound (the entry point that listens on that port) is created correctly. To add more ports, such as 80, use Add once for each port.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Traffic

Shows how much traffic each inbound has carried.

Add

  • Adds another inbound, for another port or another main server.
  • Enter the IP address or domain of the main server, then the port.
  • When you see Additional inbound added., it worked. Check with Status.

Remove

Removes one inbound.

Uninstall

Removes the Dokodemo-Door tunnel and the Xray core from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

In the main menu, select HA-Proxy.

Install

  1. Wait for the HAProxy package to be installed.
  2. In Relay-Server Free Port, enter the port users will connect to on the relay (recommended: 443).
  3. Enter the IP address or domain of the main server.
  4. Enter the port of the main server (Hiddify Manager uses 443).
  5. When you see HAProxy tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Add

Adds another relay port and main-server port pair. Use it to add port 80 → 80.

Remove

Removes one of these pairs.

Uninstall

Removes the HA-Proxy tunnel from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

Socat is now under Options → DeprecatedTunnel → Socat. The menu labels it "No longer supported"; prefer one of the methods above.

Install

  1. Wait for the Socat package to be installed.
  2. Enter the IP and then the port of the main server.
  3. When you see Socat tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Uninstall

Removes the Socat tunnel from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the previous menu.

WST is now under Options → DeprecatedTunnel → WST. The menu labels it "No longer supported"; prefer one of the methods above. It installs an old wstunnel release (v5.0) that exists only for x86-64 (amd64) servers.

Install

  1. Wait for wstunnel to be installed.
  2. Enter the port for user traffic (for example 443), the main server's domain or IP, and the port wstunnel itself should use.
  3. Enter the SSH details of the main server (IP, user, SSH port, and password when asked). The script uses them to set up the other end of the tunnel on the main server.
  4. When you see Wstunnel tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Uninstall

Removes wstunnel from both servers. It asks for the main server's SSH details again.

Back

Returns to the previous menu.

In the main menu, select Options for basic server settings and a connection test.

DNS

Sets the DNS servers the relay server uses. Enter two public DNS servers, for example 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1.

Update

Updates all packages on the server.

Ping

Tests whether the server can reach the internet.

DeprecatedTunnel

Opens the old Socat and WST tunnels (see above).

Back

Returns to the main menu.

docs.title: How to use Amazon CDN or Cloudfront
How to use Amazon CDN or Cloudfront
docs.text:
About this guide

The HiddifyManager part is for v14.5. The AWS part follows the CloudFront console as it was when this guide was written; Amazon changes its console from time to time (for example, it now asks you to choose a pricing plan first), so some names may differ. The certificate for CloudFront must be requested in the US East (N. Virginia) us-east-1 region of AWS Certificate Manager, otherwise CloudFront does not list it.

docs.title: Domain registration
docs.text:
• To do this, first point an A record to your server address in DNS. Suppose you have pointed sub1.domain.com to the IP address of your server.

  • Go to Amazon AWS and search for Cloudfront service.

  • Create a destination by clicking create distribution.
  • Enter the values in the opened page according to the image below.

All values on this page are default except for the following which should be set as shown in the images.

Viewer protocol policy:

Cache policy:

Web Application Firewall (WAF):

  • At the end, click on create distribution to perform the creation operation.
  • In the next step, go to the location of your DNS records. Assuming that you have registered in Cloudflare, enter the DNS section of your domain and create a cname record. Suppose you create sub2.domain.com and set its value equal to the domain created in the previous step in AWS. This value can be seen in the details section under Distribution domain name.

In fact, this subdomain will be used for our CDN domain.

  • Go back to the AWS panel and click on the edit option in the General tab of the setting section and click on Add item in the Alternate domain name (CNAME) - optional section that opens. and enter the cname domain from the previous step, sub2.domain.com.

docs.title: Getting a certificate
docs.text:
• Enter the Custom SSL certificate - optional section and get an ssl certificate for the desired domain. For this, click on Request certificate.

  • In the newly opened page, continue the process of receiving the certificate and in the domain name section and the address field, enter the details of the subdomain registered in the previous step, namely sub2.domain.com and set the other values as default. and click on Request.

  • On the certificate list page, you can see that the desired domain status is pending validation. Click on the ID and see the Domains section on the opened page.

  • In this section, two values of this section, Cname name and Cname value are needed to complete the certificate status.
  • Go to your DNS records (presumably Cloudflare) and create a Cname name record and enter the values you had in the previous step in AWS. In Cloudflare, enter Cname name instead of name and Cname value instead of Target.
  • Now if you go back to AWS and the certificate list page and refresh the page, you will see that the status has changed from Pending validation to Issued, which means that our domain has received the certificate correctly.
  • Now it is back to the distribution settings page and the certificate derivation stage, and if you click the refresh button for custom ssl, you can see the certificate you received in the previous stage. Select it and leave the other values of this page as default.

[!tip] Note: Be careful not to tick the Legacy client support because this option costs $600 per month.

  • At the end, click the save changes option to save the changes.
  • Now wait until the changes are applied and according to the image below, the state of Last modified will change from Deploying to done to the date and time.

  • It usually takes between 2-5 minutes for these changes to be applied, which can be followed by refreshing the screen. Always remember that at any stage you make changes, it should change to this state, which means that the changes are fully applied and usable.

  • Congratulations, the work is done. Amazon Cloudfront CDN is successfully launched. Now just register your CDN domain in your HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Adding the CDN domain in HiddifyManager
docs.text:
• In the panel side menu, open Domains (in the Settings group) and click Add domain.
  • In the Domain step, enter the CDN subdomain, sub2.domain.com, and click Check.
  • In the Mode step, under How is it set up?, choose CDN, keep Valid TLS and click Next.
  • Go through the Name and Certificate steps, then apply the changes when the panel asks you to.

docs.title: How to use Cloudflare CDN
docs.text:
Cloudflare is the largest CDN provider. When your domain is behind Cloudflare, users connect to Cloudflare's servers instead of your server's IP, and Cloudflare passes the traffic on to your server. This hides your server's IP, and if the IP is blocked, connections through the CDN keep working.

In this article you:

  1. add your domain to Cloudflare;
  2. make a direct record and a CDN record;
  3. add the domains to HiddifyManager;
  4. set Cloudflare's SSL and network settings.

To use GCore CDN on a domain that is on Cloudflare, see this tutorial.

docs.title: 1. Add your domain to Cloudflare
docs.text:
1. Make an account on Cloudflare's sign-up page and sign in.

  2. In the side menu, open Domains > Overview and click Add domain.

  3. Choose Connect a domain (for a domain you bought somewhere else).

  4. In Domain name, enter your main domain (for example yourdomain.com, without www). Lower on the same page, keep Import DNS records on Automatic so Cloudflare finds the domain's current records by itself, and click Continue.

  5. On the plan page, click Select plan under Free. The free plan is enough for this.

  6. You see the DNS records page (see step 2). Then click Continue to activation.

  7. On Update your nameservers to activate Cloudflare, you get two Cloudflare nameservers. On the website you bought the domain from, remove the old nameservers and enter these two exactly as written.

  8. Wait (up to 24 hours). When the domain is active, Cloudflare sends you an email and the domain changes from Pending to Active on the Domains page.

docs.title: 2. Make the DNS records
docs.text:
You make the records while adding the domain, or later from the domain's DNS > Records. Cloudflare explains the two proxy modes itself:

Click Add record, fill in these fields for each subdomain, then click Save:

  • Type: A for IPv4, AAAA for IPv6;
  • Name: the subdomain, for example direct or cdn;
  • IPv4 address (or IPv6 address): your server's IP;
  • Proxy status: depends on the domain type, see the table below.
Domain type Proxy status Cloud Direct DNS only (off) grey CDN Proxied (on) orange

docs.title: Direct domain
docs.text:
Turn the proxy off (DNS only). Users connect straight to your server's IP. For DNS only records you can change the TTL; the lower it is, the sooner an IP change reaches your users.

If your server has an IPv6 address, do the same with an AAAA record.

docs.title: CDN domain
docs.text:
Do the same for another subdomain, but this time leave the proxy on (Proxied). The TTL of proxied records is always Auto and can't be changed.

At the end, the records show in the list:

docs.title: Check the CDN domain
docs.text: If you check the CDN domain with ping, nslookup or dig, you see Cloudflare's IPs instead of your server's IP. These IPs can change over time. Some Cloudflare IPs are sometimes blocked or slow in Iran; then you can use clean IPs.

docs.title: 3. Add the domains to HiddifyManager
docs.text:
1. In the panel side menu, in the Settings group, open Domains and click Add domain.

  2. In the Domain step, type the subdomain and click Check. The Point it at this server box shows the A and AAAA values (your server's IPs) for the DNS record.

  3. In the Mode step, under How is it set up? choose Direct for the direct domain (grey cloud) or CDN for the CDN domain (orange cloud). The panel checks the DNS and puts a matches badge next to the right mode. Keep Valid TLS and click Next.

  4. Finish the Name and Certificate steps to add the domain.

docs.title: 4. Set SSL/TLS on Cloudflare
docs.text:
Cloudflare encrypts the connection from the user to Cloudflare and the connection from Cloudflare to your server separately. The encryption mode must be Full so that Cloudflare connects to your server over HTTPS.

  1. In the domain's side menu, open SSL/TLS > Overview. The current mode is shown next to Current encryption mode. If it is not Full, click Configure.

  2. On the encryption mode page, choose Full. Full (Strict) also works if your server's certificate is valid. Don't choose Flexible.

Automatic SSL/TLS

Cloudflare's recommended option is Automatic SSL/TLS, which picks the most secure mode your server supports and never lowers it. For a HiddifyManager server it usually runs as Full; if not, choose Full yourself.

docs.title: 5. Turn on gRPC, WebSockets and HTTP/3
docs.text:
CDN configs use gRPC and WebSocket. These are available on all plans, including Free.

  1. Open Network in the domain's side menu:

    • Turn on gRPC. It is off by default. gRPC only works on port 443 and when the SSL mode is at least Full; otherwise Cloudflare answers with a 403 error.
    • Make sure WebSockets is on (it is on by default).

  2. HTTP/3 (QUIC) moved to Speed > Settings, Protocol Optimization tab. Keep HTTP/3 (with QUIC) on (it is on by default). HTTP/3 is only between the user and Cloudflare; Cloudflare does not yet connect to your server over HTTP/3.

docs.text:
• Worker: How to set up and use Cloudflare Workers
  • Domain fronting: Guide for domain fronting. This method does not currently work on Cloudflare.

docs.title: How to use GCore CDN on Cloudflare registered domain
docs.text:
Cloudflare is sometimes disrupted in Iran. One alternative is Gcore's CDN. In this tutorial your domain's DNS stays on Cloudflare, and only one subdomain (for example gcore.yourdomain.com) is handed to Gcore with a CNAME record.

Before you start, you need an active domain on Cloudflare. See How to use Cloudflare CDN.

Cost

According to Gcore's pricing page, the pay-as-you-go (PAYG) plan includes 1 TB of free CDN traffic a month; more than that is paid. Prices can change, so check that page before you start.

docs.title: 1. Make an account and a CDN resource on Gcore
docs.text:
1. Make an account on the Gcore website and open the dashboard.

  2. Open CDN in the side menu. The first time, you see Welcome to Gcore CDN: click Get started for free (no credit card needed).

  3. The Set up your Edge Network resource form opens:

    • Under Domain, click Use your own domain and type your subdomain, for example gcore.yourdomain.com.
    • Under Origin, choose URL / IP and enter your server's IP.

  4. Click Set up your resource.

  5. You see Edge Network resource is created!. The DNS change required box shows the CNAME record you need: Host is your subdomain and Value looks like cl-xxxxxxxx.gcorecdn.com. Copy the Value.

docs.title: 2. Make the CNAME record on Cloudflare
docs.text:
1. On Cloudflare, select the domain, go to DNS > Records and click Add record.

  2. Fill it in like this and click Save:

    • Type: CNAME
    • Name: the subdomain, for example gcore
    • Target: the value you copied from Gcore
    • Proxy status: off (DNS only, grey cloud). If it is on, the traffic goes through Cloudflare instead of Gcore.

  3. On Gcore, in the resource's Setup guide (at the top of the resource settings), click Check DNS setup status. When you see DNS record has been successfully set up, the DNS is right. This can take up to 24 hours.

docs.title: 3. Set up the CDN resource on Gcore
docs.text:
On the same page click Open resource settings (or open the resource from CDN > CDN resources) and set these three things. Click Save changes after each change; applying it on all Gcore servers takes about 15 minutes.

  1. Protocol to your server: in the OPTIONS tab > General, under Origin pull protocol, choose HTTPS.

  2. SSL certificate: in the SSL section, turn on Enable HTTPS, choose Free Let's Encrypt certificate and click Get SSL certificate. Issuing takes up to 15 minutes and only works once the CNAME record from step 2 is right.

  3. WebSockets: in Content > WebSockets, turn on Enable WebSockets and click Save changes. It is off by default, and WebSocket configs don't connect without it.

WAAP protection

Gcore turns on WAAP protection for a new resource in "monitoring mode". If you later switch it to blocking, WebSocket connections may be refused with a 403 error.

docs.title: 4. Add the subdomain to HiddifyManager
docs.text:
1. In the panel side menu, in the Settings group, open Domains and click Add domain.
  2. In the Domain step, enter the subdomain (for example gcore.yourdomain.com) and click Check.

  3. In the Mode step, under How is it set up?, choose CDN, keep Valid TLS and click Next.

  4. Finish the Name and Certificate steps to add the domain.

If Show configs of on your user-page domain is set to All domains, the new configs are added to the subscription link by themselves. Ask your users to update the subscription in their app.

docs.title: Create a PHP site to transfer information of subscription links
docs.text:
Checked for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The PHP files are unchanged. The panel part (adding the PHP domain as a Subscription only domain) is written for v14.5.

docs.title: The purpose of creating a PHP site for subscription links
docs.text: HiddifyManager is based on the principle of reducing the possibility of server filtering as much as possible. One of the practical ways in this field is to separate configurations from subscription links. In this case, your client will always receive the latest configuration information through the subscription link. Now suppose the subscription link was not available for any reason, in this case a PHP site can be brought up and used to transfer the subscription link information (and not the config). The schematic for doing this is as follows.

docs.title: Steps to do the work
docs.text:
To create a PHP site and use it for the subscription link, you must first do a Google search and find free sites that provide free PHP service. find.

  • Choose one of the sites.
  • Create your account there.
  • Then create a PHP hosting service in it. This work has similar steps in different sites and is almost simple. To create this service, you must create a unique address on one of the domains of that provider.
  • After that, your service will be created.
  • After creating the service, edit its files and place the following two files in the main path of your service.

  • Note: If you don't see any .htaccess and index.php files, you need to create these files manually.

  • Make sure that .htaccess file has a dot before its name and if you create it, consider this point.

Code for .htaccess file

RewriteEngine On
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ index.php?url=$1 [L]

Code for index.php file

<?php
if (!isset($_SERVER['HTTPS']) || $_SERVER['HTTPS'] !== 'on') {
http_response_code(403);
exit('Access Forbidden - HTTPS is required.');
}
$server_domain = "https://sub.yourdomain.com";
$domain = $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'];
$ip = $_SERVER['HTTP_CF_CONNECTING_IP'] ?? $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR'] ?? $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'];
$url = $server_domain . $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'];
$userAgent = $_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'];
$ch = curl_init();
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
CURLOPT_URL => $url,
CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => false,
CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST => 2,
CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION => function($curl, $header) {
header($header);
return strlen($header);
},
]);
$headers = [
"CF-Connecting-IP: $ip",
"Host: $domain",
"User-Agent: $userAgent",
];
foreach ($_SERVER as $key => $value) {
if (strpos($key, 'HTTP_') === 0) {
$header = str_replace('_', '-', substr($key, 5));
$headers[] = "$header: $value";
}
}
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);
$response = curl_exec($ch);
if (curl_errno($ch)) {
http_response_code(500);
exit('Internal Server Error');
}
curl_close($ch);
echo $response;
?>

Be careful:

Replace https://sub.yourdomain.com with one of your server's domains in the panel (for example your subscription-only or CDN domain).

In the PHP site settings, the PHP version should be 8 or higher.

The CURL option should be turned on in the PHP settings of your host.

  • Then save the settings.
  • At this point, if you check the ssl settings for your domain in this PHP provider; You will probably notice that it takes some time for the certificate to be assigned.

docs.title: Add the PHP address to the panel
docs.text:
The PHP site sends each request to your server with the PHP site's own name (the Host), so the panel must know that name:

  1. In the panel, open Domains › Add domain, type the PHP site's address (for example hello2freeworld.phpsite.com) and choose Subscription only.
  2. In Show configs of, pick the domains whose configs your users should get (your direct or CDN domains).
  3. Finish the wizard and click Apply now on the Actions page. The panel cannot get a certificate for this name, because it does not point to your server; that is expected: the PHP host has its own certificate.

SeeSubscription-only domain

docs.title: Use it
docs.text:
Take a user's subscription link (or user page link) from the panel and replace the domain with the PHP site's address.

For example, if the PHP address is

https://hello2freeworld.phpsite.com

and the user's link is

https://sub.yourdomain.com/<client proxy path>/<user UUID>/

the link through the PHP site is

https://hello2freeworld.phpsite.com/<client proxy path>/<user UUID>/

Open it in a browser to test: you should see the user's page. Then add it to the user's app as their subscription link.

Very important note: if the PHP host has not issued the certificate for your address yet, the address does not open with https. You can test with http, but give users only the https address, so wait for the certificate.

The work is done. Now the users have a subscription address that is not your server's, so it is much harder to filter.

docs.title: How to use desired clean IPs based on the specified format (for the forced to use host field)
docs.text:
Written for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The field this page is about is now called Force configs to use these IPs / domains. It is in the settings of each CDN domain (Domains › pencil › Advanced).

A clean IP that works on one operator often does not work on another. With the Force configs to use these IPs / domains field of a CDN domain, you give the panel a clean IP (or host name) per operator, and each user gets, in their configs, the address for their own operator. This is what used to be called AutoCDN.

docs.title: The format
docs.text:
Write one entry per line (or separate them with commas):

  • an IP, a range (CIDR, such as 104.16.0.0/24) or a host name,
  • then a space and the operator code.
1.1.1.1 MCI
mtn.yourdomain.com MTN
104.16.0.0/24 RTL
8.8.8.8 OTHER

Some codes: MCI Hamrah Aval, MTN Irancell, RTL RighTel, MKH Mokhaberat (TCI), HWB HiWeb, SHT Shatel, AST Asiatech, PRS ParsOnline. For an operator without a code, use its AS number (for example AS12345). OTHER, or an address with no code, is for every other operator. If you write only addresses without codes, every user gets them.

The panel finds a user's operator from the IP they update their subscription from. So users should update the subscription with the VPN off, and again after they change operator (for example from Wi-Fi to mobile data).

docs.title: Where the addresses come from
docs.text:
• The panel's scanner (easiest): under the field, Open the scanner opens Tools › Scanner. It scans Cloudflare IPs on your own internet and saves the best ones in this field, with the operator code. See the panel tools.
  • Your own DNS records: make a record per operator (proxy off, DNS only) that points to a clean IP, for example mci.yourdomain.com. When an IP gets blocked, you only change the DNS record; the panel and the users' configs stay the same.
  • Ready lists: the host names kept up to date by ircf.space (mci.ircf.space MCI, mtn.ircf.space MTN …). The full list is in How to use AutoCDN IP domain.
  • The ip-format tool: ip-format.hiddify.com builds the text for you: delete the operators you don't need, change an address if another one works better for you, add your own IPs with the operator's tag, and click Copy IPs.

docs.title: Put it in the panel
docs.text:
1. Open Domains and click the pencil next to your CDN domain.
  2. Open Advanced and paste the text into Force configs to use these IPs / domains.
  3. Save, then click Apply now on the Actions page.

To find clean IPs by hand, see Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP. To give groups of users their own CDN domains, see How to manage multiple CDN domains.

docs.title: How to manage multiCDN domains in HiddifyManager
Managing Clean IPs and Multiple CDN and AutoCDN Domains in Hiddify Manager
docs.text: In this article, we explore strategies for managing clean IPs tailored to different operators and setting up multiple CDN domains in Hiddify Manager. These methods optimize configuration and improve connection stability for users. This page is for Hiddify Manager v14.5, where all of this is set in the Force configs to use these IPs / domains field of a CDN domain (Domains › pencil › Advanced). Since v13 there is no separate AutoCDN domain mode: see How to use AutoCDN IP domain.

docs.title: Using Clean IPs for Different Operators
Step 1: Scanning Clean IPs
docs.text: The easiest way is the panel's own Scanner (Tools › Scanner, or Open the scanner under the field): it scans Cloudflare IPs on your internet and saves the best ones in the field, per operator. You can also use other scanners, such as the Morteza Bashsiz Scanner (it also has an Android version). See Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP.

docs.title: Step 2: Clean IP Format for Operators
docs.text:
To define clean IPs for different operators, write the address (an IP, a range such as 104.16.0.0/24, or a host name), then the operator's code: 

1.1.1.1 MCI
2.2.2.2 MTN
3.3.3.3 RTL
4.4.4.4 MKH
6.6.6.6 HWB
7.7.7.7 SHT
8.8.8.8 OTHER

Some codes: MCI Hamrah Aval, MTN Irancell, RTL RighTel, MKH Mokhaberat (TCI), HWB HiWeb, SHT Shatel, AST Asiatech, PRS ParsOnline. For an operator without a code, use its AS number (for example AS12345). OTHER (or an address with no code) is for every other operator.

docs.title: Alternative Methods for Clean IPs
docs.text:
1. Using Cloudflare IPs: Test IPs using check-host.net. If "Cloudflare" appears in the ISP or Organization field, you can use these IPs for alternative configurations.

  2. Using the Main Server IP: Direct server IPs or IPs behind subdomains can work if they perform well with specific operators.

  3. Using IPv6: If the operator supports IPv6, this can be an effective solution. Ensure the client settings are adjusted to IPv6/IPv4.

docs.title: Approach 1: Creating Subdomains with Clean IPs
docs.text:
1. Define CDN Subdomains: Set up CDN subdomains with the proxy enabled: 

    sub1.domain.com (proxy on)  
sub2.domain.com (proxy on)  
sub3.domain.com (proxy on)

  2. Assign Clean IPs for Each Operator: Create subdomains with the proxy disabled for each clean IP: 

    mci.domain.com (proxy off)  ==> Clean IP for Hamrah Aval  
irc.domain.com (proxy off)  ==> Clean IP for Irancell  
mkb.domain.com (proxy off)  ==> Clean IP for Mokhaberat

  3. Add Subdomains in Hiddify Manager: Assign each subdomain to its respective operator.

docs.title: Approach 2: Using a Second Domain for CDN
docs.text:
1. Set up CDN Subdomains for the First Domain: 

    sub1.domain1.com (proxy on)  
sub2.domain1.com (proxy on)  
sub3.domain1.com (proxy on)

  2. Set Clean IP Subdomains for the First Domain: 

    mci.domain1.com (proxy off)  ==> Clean IP for Hamrah Aval  
irc.domain1.com (proxy off)  ==> Clean IP for Irancell  
mkb.domain1.com (proxy off)  ==> Clean IP for Mokhaberat

  3. Create CNAME Records for the Second Domain: 

    sub1.domain2.com ==> sub1.domain1.com (proxy off)  
sub2.domain2.com ==> sub2.domain1.com (proxy off)  
sub3.domain2.com ==> sub3.domain1.com (proxy off)

docs.title: Approach 3: One CDN domain with operator codes (AutoCDN)
docs.text:
1. Set Up a Single CDN Subdomain: 

    sub.domain.com (proxy on)

  2. Write per-operator addresses in its Force configs to use these IPs / domains field: 

    mci.ircf.space MCI  
mtn.ircf.space MTN  
mkh.ircf.space MKH  
rtl.ircf.space RTL

docs.title: Combining Subdomains and Tags for Optimal Configuration
docs.text:
To integrate clean IPs with AutoCDN features, follow these steps:

  1. Create a Subdomain with the Main Server IP (proxy off).
  2. Define Multiple Subdomains with Clean IPs for Each Operator: Ensure that each subdomain is linked to the clean IPs you scanned.

  3. Set Up a CDN Domain in Hiddify Manager: Enter three subdomains with distinct clean IPs for different operators in the Force configs to use these IPs / domains field.

  4. Assign Compatible Operator Tags: Assign operator codes (e.g., MCI, MTN) to each subdomain. Each user then gets, in their configs, the subdomain of their own operator (detected from the IP they update their subscription from, so they should update it with the VPN off).

By applying these methods, you can efficiently manage your domains and IPs in Hiddify Manager, enhancing performance and reliability for your users.

docs.title: How to use Cloudflare worker domain on HiddifyManager
How to use Cloudflare worker domain on HiddifyManager
docs.text: A Cloudflare Worker passes your users' requests from Cloudflare's network to your server. This hides your server's IP, and connections keep working when the IP is blocked.

docs.title: What has changed?
docs.text:
Older panel versions had a Cloudflare Worker domain mode. With your Cloudflare API key, the panel made the worker in your Cloudflare account by itself.

The new HiddifyManager panel (Admin V2) no longer offers this mode for new domains:

  • Worker domains you added before keep working, and their edit window still shows the worker mode.
  • For a new worker, make the worker yourself in Cloudflare and add its domain to the panel in CDN mode. The steps are below.

docs.title: 1. Make the worker in Cloudflare
docs.text: Make the worker with How to set up and use Cloudflare Workers (manual way). At the end you have an address for the worker: either its workers.dev address, or a Custom Domain on your own domain in Cloudflare.

docs.title: 2. Add the worker domain to the panel
docs.text:
1. In the side menu, in the Settings group, open Domains and click Add domain.
  2. In the Domain step, enter the worker's address without https:// and click Check.

  3. In the Mode step, under How is it set up? choose CDN. When the domain is behind Cloudflare, the panel shows a matches badge next to CDN. CDN mode always uses a valid certificate. Click Next.

  4. In the Name step, you can enter a short name to show in the users' apps (for example Worker).

  5. Finish the Certificate step to add the domain.

docs.title: 3. Clean IPs (optional)
docs.text:
To make the configs connect to clean IPs instead of Cloudflare's default IPs:

  1. On the Domains page, click the pencil icon next to the worker domain and open Advanced.
  2. In the Force configs to use these IPs / domains card, enter your clean Cloudflare IPs. With For you can set separate IPs for each operator.

  3. Click Save.

For the format of the IPs, see this article.

docs.title: 4. Bring the worker configs into the subscription link
docs.text:
The Show configs of setting of the domain your users open their user page with decides which domains' configs are in the subscription link.

  • If All domains is on (the default), the worker domain's configs are added by themselves. Nothing else is needed.
  • If you show only some domains, edit that domain, tick the worker domain under Show configs of, and click Save.

Then ask your users to update the subscription in their app.

Free plan limit

On Cloudflare's free plan, Workers handle 100,000 requests a day. This is not enough for a server with many users.

docs.title: 4to6 Tunnel
docs.text:
This guide is for an earlier setup

The 4to6-tunnel project has had no update since September 2024. It may still work, but it is not maintained. For a relay that is easier to keep running, see Using the servers' IPv6 for a steadier tunnel or the relay methods. This page is kept for people who already use it.

The 4to6 tunnel is similar to the 6to4 tunnel with the following advantages:

  1. Your effective IP address between two servers will be IPv6.
  2. IPv6 is inexpensive and can be changed easily if blocked.
  3. Your IPv4 addresses on both sides will be protected from blocking.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The setup involves two servers: A in Iran and B abroad. A tunnel is created between them:

IPv4 packets are encapsulated within IPv6 packets and transmitted over an IPv6 network. If an IP is blocked, it will be an IPv6 address and can be easily replaced, as IPv6 addresses are generally more cost-effective than IPv4 addresses.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text: You will need two servers with IPv6.

docs.title: Server A
docs.text:
curl -o /tmp/4to6install.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshya/4to6-tunnel/main/scripts/install.sh; sudo bash /tmp/4to6install.sh; rm /tmp/4to6install.sh
Field Value E0 Server A IPv6 E2 Server B IPv6 E4 192.168.1.1/24

docs.title: Server B
docs.text:
curl -o /tmp/4to6install.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshya/4to6-tunnel/main/scripts/install.sh; sudo bash /tmp/4to6install.sh; rm /tmp/4to6install.sh
Field Value E0 Server B IPv6 E2 Server A IPv6 E4 192.168.1.2/24

docs.title: On Server A
docs.text: ping 192.168.1.2

docs.title: On Server B
docs.text: ping 192.168.1.1

docs.title: Warning
docs.text: If one of your servers is already using a 192.168.x.x network, you may need to use 172.16.x.x/12 (e.g., 172.16.0.1/12 and 172.16.0.2/12) instead. If you are unsure, open an issue and include the output of ip addr.

docs.title: Use Options
docs.text:
There are three methods to use the tunnel:

  1. IP/Port Forwarding
  2. Use Xray on Both Servers
  3. Use Custom Tunneling Methods

docs.title: IP/Port Forwarding
docs.text:
For those unfamiliar with IP/Port forwarding, it is recommended to read more about it and perform the configuration manually.

This article provides guidance on setting up port forwarding.

Here is a quick setup guide:

To forward a single port (e.g., port 80), use the following settings (assuming virtual IPs of 192.168.1.1 for Server A and 192.168.1.2 for Server B).

docs.title: Server A
docs.text: iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.1.2:80 iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -j MASQUERADE

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: If the setup works, add the commands to local.rc.

docs.title: Use Xray on Both Servers
docs.text:
Install the Xray service on both servers and configure Server A to route data through a proxy on Server B. This configuration can be simplified using 3x-ui. For assistance, contact me (I am available as meshya everywhere and meshyah on Telegram).

Note: Use 192.168.1.2 instead of the real IP of Server B when configuring Xray on Server A.

docs.title: Use Custom Tunneling Methods
docs.text:
While not recommended, you can use custom tunneling methods such as Reverse TLS or Fake TLS on top of the 4to6 tunnel if you are familiar with these techniques.

Note: Use virtual IPs (192.168.x.x) instead of real IPs.

docs.title: Tip
docs.text: When using Method 2, consider adjusting routing rules and utilizing the Iran Hosted Domain Project to direct traffic for Iran-hosted websites and services, especially Shaparak and payment services, from an Iranian IP. This setup will prevent users from needing to toggle their proxies.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
1. 4to6 tunneling - Meshya

  2. Linux document project - ip4 in ip6 tunneling

  3. RFC2437

Article and main repo by Meshya

docs.title: The admin link in HiddifyManager and its format
The admin link in HiddifyManager and its format
docs.text: This page explains what each part of your admin link means, what happens when you open it, and how to get it back if you lose it. It is for anyone who manages a HiddifyManager panel.

docs.title: The format of the admin link
docs.text:
The installer prints your admin link at the end of the installation. It looks like this:

https://sub.example.com/DrtGho0n4b8H9D/8bncvfb5-8193-vv76-ab97-4c35965l250m/

The general form is:

https://<domain>/<admin proxy path>/<admin UUID>/

The parts are separated by /:

  1. https://: the connection is encrypted with TLS. Always use https links. An http link sends everything without encryption.
  2. Domain (sub.example.com): one of the domains you added in the panel (Direct, CDN or Relay). See Domain types.
  3. Admin proxy path (DrtGho0n4b8H9D): a secret path that hides the panel from bots and filtering systems. It is the setting Proxy Path for Admins. Users have a different path (Proxy Path for Clients).
  4. Admin UUID (8bncvfb5-...): your personal secret ID. Each admin has their own. Treat it like a password.

Keep your admin link private

Anyone who has your admin link can manage your panel, unless you set a password for your admin account.

The link changes if you change your domain, the admin proxy path, or your admin UUID. Save the new link before you change any of them.

docs.title: What happens when you open the link
docs.text:
1. You open the admin link in your browser.

  2. The panel signs you in and opens Admin V2, the new admin panel. The address in your browser changes to:

    https://sub.example.com/DrtGho0n4b8H9D/admin/v2/

    The UUID is removed from the address bar, so it is not shown on your screen.

  3. Your sign-in lasts up to 10 days in that browser. After that, or in a new browser, you see the Sign in page.

On the Sign in page:

  • In Admin ID or username, enter the UUID from your admin link (or the username you were given).
  • In Password, enter your password. Leave it empty if your admin account has no password.
  • Select Sign in.

The easiest way is to open your full admin link again. It fills in your ID automatically.

After you open the link, the panel opens Admin V2 and the address in your browser looks like this. The UUID is no longer in the address:

docs.title: If you lost your admin link
docs.text:
Connect to your server over SSH and run:

hiddify admin

It prints your admin links. Use a Secure https link with your domain. The link with the server's IP is "Not Secure"; use it only if the domain links do not work.

If you set a password and forgot it, reset the owner admin's password on the server with:

hiddify reset-password

Tip

Save your full admin link somewhere safe, such as a password manager, so you always have it when you need it.

docs.title: How to change the parts of the link
docs.text:
• Admin proxy path: in the panel, open Settings and search for "Proxy Path for Admins" (it is in the Very Advanced Settings card). Change it, click Save, and apply the changes. The panel then shows the new admin address.
  • Admin UUID: open the Admins page, edit the admin, and change the UUID field. The old admin link for that admin stops working.

docs.title: Tutorial for setting up a Dokodemo-Door (tunnel) relay server
docs.text:
About this guide

This guide sets up the relay server by hand with Xray, for Xray 26 and Hiddify Manager v14.5. For an easier way that builds the relay from a menu, see Hiddify Relay Builder.

A relay server is a second server, usually in Iran, that your users connect to. It passes their traffic on to your main server (Hiddify Manager) abroad. Xray's Dokodemo-Door inbound does exactly this: whatever arrives on a port is sent on, unchanged, to the same port of the main server.

Dokodemo-Door is now called tunnel

Since 2025, Xray calls this inbound tunnel. The old name dokodemo-door still works, so older configs keep running. The examples below use the new name.

docs.title: Step 1: install Xray on the relay server
docs.text:
Connect to the relay server over SSH and run Xray's official installer:

sudo bash -c "$(curl -L https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-install/raw/main/install-release.sh)" @ install

docs.title: Step 2: write the config
docs.text:
Open the config file:

sudo nano /usr/local/etc/xray/config.json

Replace its content with the example below. Change two things:

  • 10.10.10.10: the IP of your main server.
  • 443 (all three): the port of the main server you want to reach. Hiddify Manager uses port 443 by default.
{
"inbounds": [
{
"port": 443,
"protocol": "tunnel",
"settings": {
"address": "10.10.10.10",
"port": 443,
"network": "tcp,udp"
},
"tag": "to-main-443"
}
],
"outbounds": [
{ "protocol": "freedom" }
]
}

Save with Ctrl+S and close with Ctrl+X.

Several main servers on one relay

Add one inbound per main server, each on its own port. For example, server 1 at 10.10.10.10 port 443 and server 2 at 20.20.20.20 port 8443:

{
"inbounds": [
{
"port": 443,
"protocol": "tunnel",
"settings": { "address": "10.10.10.10", "port": 443, "network": "tcp,udp" },
"tag": "to-server-1"
},
{
"port": 8443,
"protocol": "tunnel",
"settings": { "address": "20.20.20.20", "port": 8443, "network": "tcp,udp" },
"tag": "to-server-2"
}
],
"outbounds": [
{ "protocol": "freedom" }
]
}

docs.title: Step 3: start Xray
docs.text:
sudo systemctl restart xray
sudo systemctl status xray --no-pager

The status must say active (running). If not, sudo journalctl -u xray -n 30 shows why (usually a typo in the JSON).

docs.title: Step 4: add the relay to the panel
docs.text:
Register a subdomain with the proxy off (DNS only) that points to the relay server's IP. In the panel, open Domains › Add domain, type the subdomain, choose Relay (1) in How is it set up?, and finish the wizard. You can give it a Display name, which the users' apps show instead of the domain.

Step by step, with pictures: How to add a relay server (domain) to HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Step 5: add the relay configs to the subscription
docs.text: It is better to keep the subscription link on its own domain. On the Domains page, open the subscription domain with the pencil and add the relay domain to Show configs of. The relay configs then appear on the user page and in the subscription. See How to create a subscription link.

docs.title: Remove the tunnel from the relay server
docs.text:
sudo systemctl disable --now xray
sudo rm /usr/local/etc/xray/config.json
sudo bash -c "$(curl -L https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-install/raw/main/install-release.sh)" @ remove

docs.title: Tutorial for setting up GOST tunnel as relay server
Tutorial for setting up GOST tunnel as relay server
docs.text:
This page shows how to turn a server into a relay for Hiddify Manager with GOST (GO Simple Tunnel). GOST is a small open-source program that forwards ports from one server to another.

A relay is a second server, usually inside your own country, that users connect to and that passes their traffic to the main Hiddify Manager server abroad. It helps when the main server’s IP is blocked or slow from your country. Read more about relays.

docs.title: Why GOST instead of plain IP-Tables forwarding?
docs.text:
• You can point the tunnel at the main server’s domain instead of its IP; if the main server’s IP changes, you only update the DNS record.
  • It runs as a system service and starts again by itself after a reboot.
  • It works with every Hiddify Manager protocol, because it moves raw TCP and UDP traffic. Your proxy traffic stays encrypted by the proxy protocol itself.

An easier way

The Hiddify Relay Builder can install GOST for you from a menu.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A main server with Hiddify Manager installed. See the installation guide.
  • A relay server with Ubuntu or Debian and SSH access as root. New to SSH? See How to connect to a server with SSH.
  • A domain that points directly at the main server’s IP (proxy off, not through a CDN), or just the main server’s IP.

docs.title: Install GOST on the relay server
docs.text:
This guide installs GOST v3 (the go-gost/gost project), the actively developed version of GOST.

  1. Connect to the relay server with SSH.

  2. Install GOST with the official script. It picks the right build for the server’s processor (amd64 or arm64) and puts it in /usr/local/bin/gost:

    bash <(curl -fsSL https://github.com/go-gost/gost/raw/master/install.sh) --install

  3. Create a service file, so GOST runs in the background and after every reboot:

    sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/gost.service

  4. Paste this into the editor:

    [Unit]
Description=GOST relay to the Hiddify Manager server
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/gost -L tcp://:443/main.example.com:443 -L udp://:443/main.example.com:443 -L tcp://:80/main.example.com:80
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

  5. Replace all three main.example.com with the main server’s direct domain (or its IP). Save with Ctrl+S and exit with Ctrl+X.

  6. Start the service and make it start at every boot:

    sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now gost

docs.title: Check that it works
docs.text:
sudo systemctl status gost

You should see active (running). Press q to leave. If you see failed, read the error with journalctl -u gost -n 30, fix the ExecStart line and run the two commands of step 6 again.

To forward more ports, add another -L tcp://:PORT/main.example.com:PORT to the ExecStart line; for UDP write udp:// instead of tcp://. If a firewall (for example ufw) is on on the relay server, open the same ports in it.

If you installed GOST v2 before

v2 (the ginuerzh/gost project) is only maintained now; v3 replaces it. The -L tcp://... command form is the same in both, so just run the install command above (it replaces /usr/local/bin/gost) and then sudo systemctl restart gost.

docs.title: Add the relay in Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
1. With an A record, point a subdomain (for example relay.example.com) at the relay server’s IP. In Cloudflare keep the proxy off (DNS only).
  2. In the panel, open Domains in the sidebar, click Add Domain, type the subdomain and click Check.

  3. In the Mode step, under How is it set up?, choose Relay. Under Which TLS?, Valid TLS is usually best; since GOST forwards port 80 too, the panel can get a certificate for the relay domain.

  4. If you chose Reality or Fake, enter the relay server’s IP in that domain’s Advanced › Force Configs to Use These IPs / Domains.

  5. Edit your subscription domain, also select the relay domain in Show configs of, and apply the changes (Actions › Apply Now).
The full steps to add a relay to the panelEvery option of the relay domain, with screenshots.

docs.title: Remove GOST from the relay server
docs.text:
Run these commands on the relay server:

sudo systemctl disable --now gost
sudo rm -f /etc/systemd/system/gost.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/gost.service /usr/local/bin/gost
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: Tutorial for setting up an HA-Proxy relay server
docs.text:
About this guide

This guide sets up the relay server by hand with HAProxy, for Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 or Debian 12 / 13 and Hiddify Manager v14.5. For an easier way that builds the relay from a menu, see Hiddify Relay Builder.

A relay server is a second server, usually in Iran, that your users connect to. It passes their traffic on to your main server (Hiddify Manager) abroad. HAProxy is a fast, well-known program that does this for TCP connections.

TCP only

HAProxy passes TCP only. Configs that use UDP, such as Hysteria2 and TUIC, do not work through this relay. If you need UDP, use Dokodemo-Door or GOST.

docs.title: Step 1: install HAProxy on the relay server
docs.text:
Connect to the relay server over SSH and install HAProxy:

sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y haproxy

docs.title: Step 2: write the config
docs.text:
Open the config file:

sudo nano /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg

Go to the end of the file (keep the global and defaults parts that are already there) and add the lines below. Change two things:

  • 10.10.10.10: the IP of your main server.
  • 443 (both): the port. Users connect to the relay on the first one; the second is the main server's port. Hiddify Manager uses 443 by default.
frontend relay_in
    bind *:443
    mode tcp
    default_backend main_server

backend main_server
    mode tcp
    server main 10.10.10.10:443

Save with Ctrl+S and close with Ctrl+X.

docs.title: Step 3: check the config and restart HAProxy
docs.text:
sudo haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg
sudo systemctl restart haproxy

The first command checks the file and must print Configuration file is valid. If it prints an error instead, fix the line it names and run both commands again.

docs.title: Step 4: add the relay to the panel
docs.text:
Register a subdomain with the proxy off (DNS only) that points to the relay server's IP. In the panel, open Domains › Add domain, type the subdomain, choose Relay (1) in How is it set up?, and finish the wizard.

Step by step, with pictures: How to add a relay server (domain) to HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Step 5: add the relay configs to the subscription
docs.text: On the Domains page, open your subscription domain with the pencil and add the relay domain to Show configs of. The relay configs then appear on the user page and in the subscription. See How to create a subscription link.

docs.title: Remove HAProxy from the relay server
docs.text:
sudo systemctl disable --now haproxy
sudo apt-get remove -y haproxy

docs.title: Tutorial for setting up IP-Table tunnel as relay server
docs.text:
This page shows you how to turn a server into a relay for your Hiddify Manager server using IP-Tables, the firewall built into Linux. It is the simplest method: one script, no extra software to keep running.

A relay server is a second server, usually inside your own country, that your users connect to. It forwards their traffic to your main HiddifyManager server abroad. This helps when the main server's IP is blocked or slow from your country. Read more about relay servers.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A main server with Hiddify Manager installed. See the installation guide.
  • A relay server running Ubuntu or Debian, with a clean IP and enough bandwidth and CPU for your users. RAM matters little: a small, cheap server (for example 256 MB of RAM) is enough, and you can run several of them.
  • SSH access to the relay server as root. New to SSH? See how to connect to a server via SSH.
  • The IP address of your main server.

docs.title: Set up the relay server
docs.text:
1. Connect to your relay server over SSH.

  2. Run this command:

    bash <(curl https://gist.githubusercontent.com/hiddify-com/63836c9a158eca29bad6c941610028cf/raw/0e4e2138148ab9d3d678723fd904b1cad461ce62/relay.sh)

  3. When asked Enter your main server IP like(1.1.1.1):, type your main server's IP and press Enter.

  4. The script installs iptables and iptables-persistent. If a blue screen asks whether to save the current IPv4 (and IPv6) rules, choose Yes.

    The script forwards TCP ports 80 and 443, and all UDP traffic, to your main server, and saves the rules so they come back after a reboot.

  5. The script turns on IP forwarding (needed for the tunnel) only until the next reboot. Make it permanent:

    echo "net.ipv4.ip_forward=1" | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-relay.conf
sudo sysctl --system

docs.title: Check that it worked
docs.text:
Run this on the relay server:

sudo iptables -t nat -L -n

You should see DNAT lines that point to your main server's IP. If you do not, run the script again and check the IP you typed.

If ufw is on

If the ufw firewall is on on the relay server, it must allow forwarding: in /etc/default/ufw set DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY to "ACCEPT" and run sudo ufw reload. Your provider’s firewall must also leave ports 80 and 443 open.

docs.title: Add the relay server to Hiddify Manager
docs.text:
1. With an A record, point a subdomain (for example relay.example.com) at the relay server’s IP. In Cloudflare keep the proxy off (DNS only).
  2. In the panel, open Domains in the sidebar, click Add Domain, type the subdomain and click Check.

  3. In the Mode step, under How is it set up?, choose Relay. Under Which TLS?, Valid TLS is usually best; since this script forwards port 80 to the main server too, the panel can get a certificate for the relay domain.

  4. If you chose Reality or Fake, enter the relay server’s IP in that domain’s Advanced › Force Configs to Use These IPs / Domains.

  5. Edit your subscription domain, also select the relay domain in Show configs of, and apply the changes (Actions › Apply Now).
The full steps to add a relay to the panelEvery option of the relay domain, with screenshots.

docs.title: Remove the relay rules
docs.text:
The forwarding rules live in the nat table. To delete them and save the empty rule set, run this on the relay server:

sudo iptables -t nat -F
sudo netfilter-persistent save

Warning

This deletes every rule in the nat table, including any you added yourself.

To also turn IP forwarding off, delete the file you created:

sudo rm /etc/sysctl.d/99-relay.conf

docs.title: Using the servers' IPv6 for a steadier tunnel
docs.text:
Checked for Hiddify Manager v14.5

The relay server is built with Hiddify Relay Builder; the HiddifyManager part is for v14.5.

Running the tunnel between the relay server (usually in Iran) and the main server over IPv6 has become an effective way to get a steadier connection: IPv6 routes are often disrupted less than IPv4 ones.

docs.title: Two ways to use IPv6
docs.text:
1. A local IPv6 on both servers: you create a private IPv6 network between the relay and the main server, and the tunnel uses it. See Tutorial for setting up local IPv6 for the relay server.
  2. The main server's real IPv6: the tunnel connects to the main server's own IPv6 address. Both servers need IPv6 on their network card; check it with ip a on each server (look for an inet6 address that is not fe80::…).

Note: in practice, the GOST and Dokodemo-Door methods work best for both ways.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Hiddify Relay Builder on the relay server, as described in its guide. When the install finishes, its menu opens.

  2. Choose GOST or Dokodemo-Door.

  3. Choose the first option of that method, then add inbounds, and enter the main server's IPv6 (or the local IPv6) in the format the menu asks for.
  4. Enter a port of your choice.

  5. Add the relay to the panel. Register a subdomain with the proxy off (DNS only) that points to the relay server's IPv4. In the panel, open Domains › Add domain, type the subdomain, choose Relay in How is it set up? and finish the wizard. Then add the relay domain to Show configs of of your subscription domain. Step by step: How to add a relay server (domain) to HiddifyManager.

    In Add domain, choose Relay (1):

docs.title: Suggested proxies
docs.text:
For this kind of relay, these proxies work well. They are in Proxy Editor › Proxies:

  • tcp relay vmess
  • httpupgrade relay vmess

They can help keep the connection stable, especially when filtering is heavy.

docs.title: Tutorial for setting up a WST (wstunnel) relay server
docs.text:
About this guide

For wstunnel 11.1 (October 2026) and Hiddify Manager v14.5. wstunnel changed its commands in version 7; if you followed an older version of this page (v5.0), use the new commands below. For an easier way that builds the relay from a menu, see Hiddify Relay Builder.

A relay server is a second server, usually in Iran, that your users connect to. It passes their traffic on to your main server (Hiddify Manager) abroad. wstunnel carries that traffic inside a WebSocket connection, which looks like normal web traffic and can also pass through a CDN such as Cloudflare.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• The main server with Hiddify Manager installed: installation guide.
  • A relay server (Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 or Debian 12 / 13), usually in Iran.
  • A domain or subdomain for the main server, for example tunnel.example.com: direct (DNS only), or behind Cloudflare. Port 8080 works through Cloudflare too.

docs.title: Step 1: install wstunnel on both servers
docs.text:
Connect over SSH to the main server, run these commands, and then do the same on the relay server:

wget https://github.com/erebe/wstunnel/releases/download/v11.1.0/wstunnel_11.1.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz
tar xzf wstunnel_11.1.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz wstunnel
sudo install -m 755 wstunnel /usr/local/bin/wstunnel
wstunnel --version

The last command prints the version, for example wstunnel 11.1.0. On an ARM server, use linux_arm64 instead of linux_amd64.

docs.title: Step 2: run the server side on the main server
docs.text:
Create a service, so the tunnel starts by itself after a reboot:

sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/wstunnel.service

Paste this, save with Ctrl+S and close with Ctrl+X:

[Unit]
Description=wstunnel server
After=network-online.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/wstunnel server ws://[::]:8080 --restrict-to 127.0.0.1:443 --restrict-to 127.0.0.1:80
Restart=always
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

--restrict-to lets the tunnel reach only ports 443 and 80 of this server, so nobody else can use it as an open proxy.

Then start it and check it:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now wstunnel
sudo systemctl status wstunnel --no-pager

The status must say active (running).

docs.title: Step 3: run the client side on the relay server
docs.text:
On the relay server, create the same file with the client command. Replace tunnel.example.com with your main server's domain:

sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/wstunnel.service

[Unit]
Description=wstunnel client (relay)
After=network-online.target
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/wstunnel client -L tcp://0.0.0.0:443:127.0.0.1:443 -L tcp://0.0.0.0:80:127.0.0.1:80 ws://tunnel.example.com:8080
Restart=always
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

-L tcp://0.0.0.0:443:127.0.0.1:443 means: listen on port 443 of the relay server and send everything to port 443 of the main server. Add more -L parts for more ports.

Then start it and check it:

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now wstunnel
sudo systemctl status wstunnel --no-pager

docs.title: Step 4: add the relay to the panel
docs.text:
Register a subdomain with the proxy off (DNS only) that points to the relay server's IP. In the panel, open Domains › Add domain, type the subdomain, choose Relay (1) in How is it set up?, and finish the wizard.

Step by step, with pictures: How to add a relay server (domain) to HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Step 5: add the relay configs to the subscription
docs.text: On the Domains page, open your subscription domain with the pencil and add the relay domain to Show configs of. See How to create a subscription link.

docs.title: Remove the tunnel
docs.text:
On both servers:

sudo systemctl disable --now wstunnel
sudo rm -f /etc/systemd/system/wstunnel.service /usr/local/bin/wstunnel
